Sports.title: Heartbroken Tenerife fans gather at vigil for Jesus de Miguel after tragic death following goalkeeper collision
Sports.content:
Next

DEVASTATED Tenerife fans put together an emotional vigil to pay tribute to Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died after a harrowing clash on the pitch.

De Miguel passed away at the age of 30 after a freak accident with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono on Monday Spanish Segunda Division game at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium.



Owono, 25, was sent off in the closing stages of the second half when his knee collided with the striker’s head and chest as he ran out to clear out a long ball during a dangerous counter-attack with the score at 2-2.

The Spaniard was left motionless after the impact and medics rushed to the scene as players were left in tears before the referee abandoned the game in the seventh minute of stoppage time.





According to Marca, De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest on his way to hospital and was resuscitated by paramedics.

The Madrid native was admitted to intensive care, where his condition was described as “stable but serious” by Tenerife on Monday night.



But tragedy struck as his health deteriorated and he was pronounced dead on Tuesday morning.

Heartbroken Tenerife fans gathered around their home stadium, where the incident took place, to honour their beloved player with flowers, candles and emotional letters.

One message read: “Today the heart of Tenerife is in mourning. It’s hard to find words when someone who has been part of our history leaves too soon.”

Another commented: “Your departure hurts us. It hurts us to think that we will no longer see you defend this shirt, that there will be no more celebrations, more hugs or more shared moments.”

A third issued the following touching tribute: “Keep scoring goals in the sky.”



And another message read: “Your name will be linked to that ascent, to that shared illusion and to a blue and white family that today mourns your loss. Heliodoro and Tenerife will never forget you.”

Fans – many of whom struggled to hold their tears – also kept a minute’s silence for De Miguel.

According to AS, Andorra players showed “great concern” for Owono on their way back from Tenerife.



The Equatorial Guinea international was “visibly shaken” after breaking down in the dressing room.

The same report adds those close to Owono describe him as “caring” and a “very kind” person with “no malice”.

Owono’s social media accounts have been deactivated since the incident and he reportedly intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before the news of his death emerged.

The keeper is expected to avoid criminal sanctions but may still face a sporting punishment.

Sports.title: Carrick seemed intent on becoming first Man Utd boss sacked at half-time – but this could be his Mark Robins moment
Sports.content:
Next

FOR 45 minutes against Roma, Michael Carrick seemed intent on becoming the first Manchester United manager to be sacked at half-time.

He will hope the next 45 minutes are his Mark Robins moment. That is doubtful, but as a United player and coach, he now has moments to cherish against Roma.



A familiar banner was unfurled by a United supporter by the tunnel at the interval that read, “Play like you mean it”.

Carrick played as though he had a career death wish before that bedsheet was brandished.



The game has been up for Carrick for weeks, yet the United decision-makers continue to let him play. They are playing with fire.

At least the players finally came alight. They clocked that bedsheet when it first made an appearance at Craven Cottage almost three years ago to the day and won.



They seemed to get the message again.

The stirring fightback will soften criticism of Carrick but should not spare him beyond this week, given the inevitability that he will stride down the Old Trafford touchline against Aston Villa on Sunday.

That should be his curtain call.

Of all the chastening moments in the past seven weeks for United, nothing came close to the first 20 minutes against Roma.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It was only halted by a half-hearted attempt at a protest when 27 tennis balls were lobbed onto the pitch.

United showed them at 2-0 down. Italian football has been in decline for 20 years yet two of their teams have embarrassed them.

Roma could not keep it up for another 45 minutes.

Diogo Dalot spent a season on loan in Italy with AC Milan and he would not be short of volunteers on the Stretford End to drive him back there for a reunion with Ruben Amorim.

He was booed as he approached the tunnel at the pause.



United supporters sounded as angry with Dalot as they are with the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

With Luke Shaw a resident in the physio’s room again, Dalot is the longest-serving member in the United squad. He often looks the most amateurish.

The right back was listed at left back on the tactical teamsheets, as he was against Bournemouth and Chelsea. Dalot has played at left back dozens of times.



Yet Carrick attempted to reinvent him as a left winger. Dalot’s roguish role there gifted Roma their two goals.

What compounded it was Dalot was playing right in front of Carrick. Worse yet, Carrick evidently okayed Dalot abandoning his station.

Repeatedly picking Leny Yoro at right back and Ayden Heaven at centre back is asking for it.

Those 20-year-olds can be cut some slack on account of their youth. They lack senior teammates to dig them out of a hole.

But Dalot is into his ninth year at United. He is No.1 scapegoat, on account of his longevity and the sheer lack of success during that period.



United supporters were on his back with the game goalless. Dalot kept on finding a charcoal shirt and the murmurs of disapproval grew louder. One irate fan started venting at him. Then Mathias Soule scored.

Dalot was the furthest United player forward when Kobbie Mainoo ceded the ball. The back four was the shape of a banana.

Astonishingly, it appeared to be part of the plan.



Seconds before Heaven conceded a penalty, Carrick was urging United players to move higher up the pitch and seemed fine with Dalot being nearer the Roma area than his own.

He showed why he has survived at United for so long. For all Dalot’s faults, he possesses some resilience and fortuitously assisted Matheus Cunha’s equaliser.

During that fleeting respite when the game was goalless, Carrick implored a United player, or players, to press on two separate instances inside the first nine minutes. The instructions fell on deaf ears both times.

United’s game plan consisted of playing high and going long to a non-existent striker.

Bryan Mbeumo can chip in with a goal but United did not play to his strengths until Fernandes played him through to agonisingly clip both posts with one shot.



Even the worst United sides can stir the soul. After Lyon in 2025, Roma in 2026. Dalot scored in the former.

The death march has slowed down and Carrick has avoided the ignominy of matching the dull Dave Sexton’s 10-match winless run 48 years ago.

Cunha will not be his Robins, though.

EMRE BELOZOGLU has returned to his Fenerbahce after the club was snubbed by Sergio Conceicao.

He left the Magpies for Fenerbahce, where he would have multiple spells as a player.

Sports.title: Champions League clash stopped as fans shoot flares from outside stadium onto pitch and burning on roof
Sports.content:
Next

A CHAMPIONS LEAGUE clash was suspended for two minutes after flares were fired onto the venue’s roof and pitch.

Dutch outfit Feyenoord were hosting Italian giants Inter Milan on Tuesday night.

But home fans outside the ground reportedly did not react well to Inter scoring to go three goals up, as they fired flares in the air above the stadium.



Flaming remnants of the pyrotechnics then floated down on and into the 47,500-seater De Kuip.



Video from the venue shows flaming debris scorching the roof as more floated down towards the ground.

Another piece could be seen smoking on the grass in the middle of the vacant penalty box.

Referee Glenn Nyberg called a stop to the match with barely 20 minutes of the fixture to play.

But it was deemed safe to continue two minutes later, as Inter defended their lead to leave with all three points.

Yann Aurel Bisseck, Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski came up with the goals for the Serie A title chasers.

Ex-Spurs man Djed Spence shone at full-back notching two assists on top of his clean sheet for the visitors.

But while Feyenoord have much to celebrate at the top of the Eredivisie, their European fortunes have not been so kind.

The side, managed by former Arsenal and Rangers star Giovanni van Bronckhorst, have managed just one win in their opening four clashes in the competition.

That win came over Cesc Fabregas‘ Como, while Barcelona and Betis joined Inter in securing wins over the side on their way to 30th-place in the League Phase after four games.

Sports.title: Gabby Logan forced to apologise as Bruno Fernandes swears on live TV after Man Utd’s epic comeback win over Roma
Sports.content:
Next

GABBY LOGAN was forced to apologise after Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes swore live on TV after his side’s 3-2 comeback win over Roma.

The Red Devils produced a miraculous turnaround on Tuesday night after a bleak first half at Old Trafford.



Matias Soule struck in the first ten minutes before ex-Aston Villa star Donyell Malen then made it 2-0 from the spot after Ayden Heaven‘s handball.

United were left reeling at half time but Fernandes pulled one back from the spot – after his first missed effort was retaken – before Mateus Cunha won it with a late brace.



The incredible result could have very well saved Michael Carrick‘s job for now amid rising pressure on his position.

Emotions were high after the final whistle and Fernandes gave an emotionally-charged interview to Amazon Prime – insisting he wanted to win “every f***ing game” for the club.



When asked about Carrick’s future, he replied: “We don’t need to save anyone’s job.

“The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff.

“We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together.

“It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

“A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

“The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn’t performing. And that’s fair.

“Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.



“The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

“And it doesn’t change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.”

Fernandes had previously fallen out with Carrick after hitting out at his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 defeat to Como last month.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Diogo Dalot has another rotten outing but Matheus Cunha puts on attacking masterclass despite red card
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED came from two goals down to beat Roma in a dramatic Champions League comeback to give manager Michael Carrick a vital boost as he fights to save his job.

United fans staged protests against the ownership but the quality of coaching came under the spotlight after yet another defensive collapse in the first half.



United avoided a 10th game without a win despite Roma leading 2-0 at half-time following Matias Soule’s 11th minute strike and Donyell Malen‘s penalty.

But the hosts, battered and bruised by the toxicity from fans, fought back through a Bruno Fernandes spot-kick and two late goals from Matheus Cunha – who was later sent off after two bookings.



Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated the United players from a bouncing Old Trafford.

Senne Lammens – 6

The Belgian was easy prey behind arguably one of the worst defences in the Champions League. A good save to his right stopped 3-0 before the break.

Welcomed a quieter second half after his outfield players finally decided to show up. Was not at fault for the goals but his distribution has been off it.

Leny Yoro – 6

The central defender started at right-back and often found himself sprinting towards his own net with Carrick asking his players to push high.

He naively backed off in the lead up to the penalty being conceded. Made a huge recovery tackle to deny Rodrigo Mora after 2-0.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Looking stronger in forward areas and coping reasonably well with the mayhem, despite his youth.



Harry Maguire – 5

Guilty of dreadful mistakes with poor clearances glued straight into danger zones at every turn, one of which resulted in the penalty.

Another player who improved in the second half, but Roma‘s attacks had stalled by then. Had three chances to score from quick corners in the second half but could not level. Booked.

Ayden Heaven – 5

A 20-year-old defender should be allowed to nourish and develop, but Heaven is always given a baptism of fire.

Roma‘s cross flew over him to a sitting Soule before he conceded a penalty a few minutes later when Soule’s shot hit his low arm.

Looked overwhelmed and you can hardly blame him. Thrown in after Carrick dropped Lisandro Martinez following his needless red card at Chelsea.



Diogo Dalot – 3

No man’s land.

Dalot left the entire left side vacant when Roma had possession to allow Soule the Freedom of Manchester to touch, wait and slot past Lammens inside 11 minutes.

Carrick had Dalot and Yoro as auxiliary wingers, and it was schoolboy defending at times.



Kobbie Mainoo – 6

Back in the line up after a month out, but gave up possession too easily for Marten de Roon intercept a loose pass in the lead up to the opener.

His long range shot just before the break was United’s first on target attempt. The England midfielder improved in the second half when United had possession. Was involved in feeding Lacey for the third goal.

Carlos Baleba – 4

All the excitement about the £70m singing has quickly dried up. The 22-year-old was behind the pace and launched a free pass out of play behind Yoro before the break.

He pulled his right hamstring when he was through on goal with a tap-in available 30 seconds after the restart.

Bruno Fernandes – 7

The skipper found his spark after scoring a retaken penalty, having been let off the hook when encroachment erased an awful first attempt easily saved by Roma’s third-choice keeper.



The strike ended a goal drought that stretched back to the 4-0 win over Sabah on September 10.

He fumbled a first half shot and instantly threw his arms into the air in disgust over Baleba’s scruffy pass.

United are yet to trigger his one-year extension or agree fresh terms with their out-of-form captain. We might have to envisage a world without Fernandes at Old Trafford.



Amad – 5

The 24-year-old was not clinical enough and is guilty of too many touches inside the box.

Gets into good positions but you rarely believe he will score. He is without a United goal since December 14. Replaced by Shea Lacey, who was more threatening.

Matheus Cunha – 8

After a drab first half, the Brazilian soon became United’s best player and saved the day, playing with anger and venom. Stunning touch and finish from a tight angle to secure 3-2.

Scored two, won a soft penalty, launched himself topless into the crowd beneath the away end and was given a standing ovation after his sending off.



He was brilliant in the second half and cleverly rattled by the fan backlash inside Old Trafford, which helped his performance.

Booked for his wild celebrations and picked up a second yellow for a silly foul in stoppage time.



Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Linked up well with Cunha but poor touch let down a decent breakaway. Painfully unluckily when his strike bounced between both posts straight after Fernandes’ penalty.

Had a couple of opportunities to push through on goal but just didn’t have the pace.

Had a positive impact the ball.

The teenager provided more than Amad in his 12 minutes on the pitch. His incredible pass assisted Cunha’s second. Should be gunning for Amad’s spot.

Lisandro Martinez (Heaven, 75) – 6

Dropped to the bench after his reckless red that condemned United to defeat at Chelsea. Was booed by Old Trafford when he came on after a month of antics.

MATHEUS CUNHA went from hero to villain against Roma with a dramatic brace and a red card.

The Brazilian forward netted twice in three minutes to propel Manchester United to a much-needed win in the Champions League.



United looked down and out against Roma at half-time as the players were booed off after falling 2-0 down.

But a second-half resurgence saw them claim a famous win after a penalty from Bruno Fernandes and Cunha’s brace.



The former Wolves star was full of excitement after his second goal as he whipped off his shirt and jumped into the crowd.

This earned Cunha his first yellow card and then a late challenge on Leonardo Balerdi followed moments later.

The referee wasted no time in showing Cunha his second booking and his red card.

Fortunately for United, they were not made to pay for Cunha’s red card and going down to ten men.

Michael Carrick‘s side were able to hold on to the 3-2 scoreline and claim only their third win of the season.

Goals from Matias Soule and Donyell Malen had put Roma in a commanding position before the break.

United defender Diogo Dalot took the brunt of criticism for the first goal as he was far from the correct position.

The players were booed off by the fans at the break and Alan Shearer slammed them as “embarrassing” on Amazon Prime commentary.

United suffered another blow early in the second half as midfielder Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury.

But they were handed a way back into the game after winning a penalty for a foul on Cunha.

Sports.title: Man Utd 3 Roma 2: Matheus Cunha inspires stunning comeback from 2-0 down that might just save Michael Carrick’s job
Sports.content:
Next

YOU had to be here to see it, believe it.

From utter despair, the brink of humiliation, to a comeback win to earn a place in the Manchester United book of legends.



And while this most astonishing of triumphs came from nowhere, it might, just might prove an unlikely turning point.

The night when Michael Carrick went from dead manager walking to getting the chance to prove he deserves the job after all.



As Matheus Cunha scored twice in the space of three second half minutes, transforming another defeat into a glorious triumph, United went from zeroes to heroes.

Battered and broken for 45 minutes, seemingly set to suffer a defeat that would leave scars for ever, only to somehow, against all the odds, end up with a first win in 10 games.

Sir Alex Ferguson will have loved it, seeing one of his old stalwarts throw caution to the wind and be rewarded for his gambles.

A night which seemed to sum up everything that is wrong with United finished with roars of sheer, delirious joy.



Sparked by Bruno Fernandes’ twice-taken penalty, Cunha then had the maddest of final minutes.

First the Brazilian was in the right place when Leonardo Balerdi’s air-shot gave him the chance to sweep home from close range – an absolute gift.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Then, as the roars became deafening, Cunha did it again, waltzing through to smash in off the post from a tight angle, stunning the Roma fans who had previously bellowed their lungs out.

That was followed by a second yellow card and a slow, disbelieving walk to the dressing room.

Yet when the final whistle went, there were no villains in red – an hour after there had been a whole cast of them.



At the interval, the surprise was that United and Carrick were not already dead and buried.

The manager’s decision to ask Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro as auxiliary wingers, totally ignoring their prime roles, seemed utter folly.

If that was the plan, it unravelled inside 17 minutes as United’s chronic inability to do the defensive basics bit them once again.

The opener summed up just how poor United are.

Bad enough was Kobbie Mainoo coughing up the ball just inside the United half yet the lack of reaction was criminal.



Rodrigo Mora, wide on the left, had an age to see the day-dreaming Dalot was out of the picture – 25 yards the wrong side of his man.



And when Heaven – in for the benched Lisandro Martinez – missed the ball completely, Matias Soule had time to pick his spot past the exposed Senne Lammens.

Carrick went back to his bench for a video nasty replay but – after Cunha failed to get on the end of Bruno Fernandes’ cross – the horror show was back.

This time, Dalot was on the edge of the Roma box as the Italians played up the field, before Harry Maguire added his name to the list of villains.

Soule looked to have wasted the chance to feed the lurking Malen only for Maguire to hand the ball back to him and when Heaven’s right arm blocked the Roma man’s shot, Spanish ref Jesus Gil Manzano pointed instantly to the spot.

Malen, a force reborn since he left Aston Villa for the Italian capital in January, sent Lammens the wrong way.



Cue the second stage of protests, a cascade of tennis balls thrown onto the pitch – far more effective at stopping Roma then United’s back line or the green and gold balloons released before the start – as Carrick was left perplexed and mournful.

The last time Gian Piero Gasperini came to Old Trafford, his Atalanta side had squandered a two goal lead.

At that stage, a repeat did not seem at all likely.



Roma were fitter, sharper, simply better, United shambolic.

Old Trafford was the Theatre of Screams, mainly directed at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers but often at the home team too.

Only a desperate foot by Yoro prevented Soule presenting Mora with a sitter as United were opened up like a tin of tomatoes once again, before Lammens denied Malen after he exposed Heaven’s hell and Soule was a fraction wide.

The half-time jeers were brutal. And deserved.

When Carlos Baleba burst through within 45 seconds of the restart only to ping his right hamstring, it felt like a perfect embodiment of United’s misery.



Likewise, as Fernandes was denied by debut-making keeper Devis Vasquez after Cunha’s tumble in the vicinity of Gianluca Mancini was bought by the ref and confirmed by VAR, there was shock.

But the video booth spotted Bryan Cristante had encroached before clearing and the United skipper took his second chance.

Within seconds, United looked to be set to level, as Bryan Mbeumo but saw his shot bounce off BOTH posts before being cleared.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now it was a siege, which looked to have been repelled.

Enter Cunha. Astonishing. Remarkable. Enough to keep Carrick in his job beyond Sunday? Maybe.

Sports.title: Fernandes claims players don't need to save Carrick's job, but did they?
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has come out in support of head coach Michael Carrick, but reiterated that the players didn't need to save his job in their 3-2 comeback win against Roma.

United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges.

It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days.

The spirit shown in the performance suggested at least some on-pitch support for Carrick, whose tenure appeared to have been hanging on by a thread ever since the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes was named on the bench for that game after publicly questioning the tactics in a sobering 4-1 defeat to Como four days prior. His words after Roma, though, were a lot more defiant than accusatory.

"We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes told Amazon Prime post-match.

"We've been working so hard to get out of this situation altogether. It's been tough. There's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had to clear the air. Nothing like that happened.

"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that it was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.

"The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me. It should be [a turning point]."

Image: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick celebrates his first win in ten games

Carrick himself similarly played down suggestions that the turnaround could've helped his cause, saying "it's a win for us as a football club," when asked how the result could change the narrative.

"I think we've shown a lot of character as a group to weather what we've had to. You find out a lot about each other, the players will find out things about me. I certainly do about them and their character and what it means to them and what they're prepared to put in."

The win, and the nature of it, feels very reminiscent of a 2018 3-2 win over Newcastle during Jose Mourinho's time at the club. Two early goals stunned the home side, who were already under immense pressure for their poor start to the season.

In the second half, a response. A player who reportedly had his issues with Mourinho, Anthony Martial, found the net en route to a comeback which was secured by a severely underperforming South American in Alexis Sanchez.

Tonight, the role of Mourinho was played by Carrick. The role of Martial you could argue was played by Fernandes, regardless of how he feels his comments following Como were perceived. And the role of Sanchez was bettered by Cunha's heroics.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson reflects on Manchester United's 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League

Did it save Mourinho his job? Ultimately, it didn't. He was sacked by December that year, but maybe it gave him a bit more time at the helm.

In the ten games prior to the Newcastle win, Mourinho's United had only won three times. In the 13 after, they picked up five, plus draws against Chelsea and Arsenal that weren't to be scoffed at. The issue was, the expectations at United were higher in 2018, and that return wasn't cutting it.

In reality, if Carrick managed a run of five wins, four draws and four defeats over the next 13 games, he probably isn't shown the door and is given more time to build on the project. Especially if there are some disagreements from the higher-ups on who should be the man to replace him if they went down that route.

Manchester United

Aston Villa Sunday 8th November 4:25pm Kick off 4:30pm

There is just one variable that will make or break things for Carrick. Can he go back-to-back? If his United side can beat Aston Villa on Sunday, it could be the statement the former midfielder needs to earn him more time.

Unai Emery is widely regarded as the best boss in the Premier League. If Carrick is sacked, many United fans would be begging to see him take the hot seat. But, with the spirit and belief in the dressing room higher than it has been in two months following Tuesday's spectacular comeback, Carrick has a chance to get one over on Emery and leave a final impression on his bosses before the international break.

It won't be until Sunday evening, when the final whistle is blown at Old Trafford, that we will truly know whether or not Carrick's men saved his job, rather appropriately, in Fergie time.

Watch Manchester United vs Aston Villa on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, kick-off 4.30pm.

Sports.title: Cunha completes wild Man Utd comeback win over Roma from two down
Sports.content:
Manchester United produced an extraordinary comeback from two down to beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win in 10 games.

Michael Carrick looked on the brink when his disjointed team were completely undone for Matias Soule's opener and Donyell Malen soon made it two from the penalty spot. But Matheus Cunha won one of his own, scored two and was sent off in a wild contest.

United had been booed off at the break and when Carlos Baleba had to go off early in the second half with a hamstring injury it all looked dismal for United. But when Cunha won a penalty that Bruno Fernandes scored after a retake it altered the momentum.

Bryan Mbeumo struck both posts with one shot soon after and the noise inside Old Trafford was astonishing thereafter. Roma cleared one off the line and United had two more penalty shouts as the Italian side - unbeaten in Serie A - began to wobble badly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson reflects on Manchester United's 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League

Leonardo Balerdi's error proved it, his woeful clearance allowing Cunha to slot home the leveller. And it was the same player with a stunning near-post finish from Shea Lacey's pass who completed the comeback to the delight of the disbelieving crowd.

Cunha was sent off for a silly foul to ensure a tense finale but United held on for a first win in 54 days. Improbably, Carrick left the pitch not just to applause but having presided over a win in the Champions League. And a spirited one at that.

Analysis: A comeback from nowhere

Where on earth did that come from? Roma were two up and it could have been more against a United side whose spirit appeared as broken as their tactics in a first half that seemed like surrender. But strange things can still happen at the Theatre of Dreams.

It is difficult to overstate the incoherence of those opening minutes. Watching Fernandes throw his arms in the air in disgust at a Baleba pass late in the first half, it looked like a team in disarray and desperate to blame someone else for the situation.

Image: Matheus Cunha smashes in the winner for Manchester United against Roma

United's tactical setup early on against Roma was arguably even worse than against Como when Fernandes criticised his manager. They were continually cut apart in the left-back position with Diogo Dalot up the pitch and Ayden Heaven exposed.

At that stage, thought turned to the balance of the squad and the quality of it, the confidence and the team spirit, the players, the coach and the ownership. None of that completely goes away after a chaotic 45 minutes but this was at least something.

It was a team telling the fans that they can show spirit, that they are not prepared to let it slide further without a fight, that they can still conjure quality from nowhere. The scenes at the end of the game showed that at this great club, sometimes, that can be enough.

Fernandes opens up on Carrick situation

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes speaking to Amazon Prime:

"Fans want to win games, they've been used to seeing this club at the top, winning trophies, winning games every week. For them it's been so frustrating to see the club in this situation.

"I just want to make everyone aware that we're all frustrated with the situation at the moment and we all want to get out of this. Hopefully this win today gives the start of something good for us.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson reacts to Bruno Fernandes's penalty goal for Manchester United in their Champions League clash with Roma

"It has been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had cleared the air, then after, nothing of that happened.

"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench [against Bournemouth] because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.

"The manager is the one that makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club.

"It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me. It should be [a turning point]."

Carrick praises Lacey on 'important night'

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick speaking in the press conference:

"Proud of a lot of people actually, proud of the players, and they deserve a lot of credit for pulling through that in a tough situation.

"And for the supporters, you know, to be there, they were desperate for us to give them something they could get their teeth into.

"I think it is really important for the players to know what this place can do.

"I am not getting too carried away with things, but it is an important night."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United's Michael Carrick hailed the second performance of his team after they came back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League

On the impact of Shea Lacey with his assist for the winning goal:

"Again, not going too over the top, but at the same time, absolutely delighted for Shea. We love him to bits. He is a great young man.

"He is desperate to do well, he has got great ability, so in terms of coming inside and finding a pass, that is not surprising actually, he has got that little glint in his eyes, he plays with a bit of mischief if you like.

"So it is always lovely to have that, but I was just as happy seeing him defending as a right-back when we needed that. I was just as pleased to see him do that on the defensive side.

"I think he gave everybody a bit of a lift coming on the pitch and it was fantastic to see."

Sports.title: Burrage receives death threats and abuse after Chennai Open defeat
Sports.content:
Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing

Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open

Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday.

Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down against India's Vaishnavi Adkar.

She looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes.

The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," Burrage said in the accompanying message.

German player Eva Lys tagged the WTA from her Instagram handle and asked: "When will something be done?"

The 27-year-old appeared to struggle with the humid conditions and called the doctor with her opponent about to serve for the match.

Burrage was visibly shaking and had her blood pressure and oxygen levels checked as well as ice rubbed on her arms and legs. She was able to resume the contest but lost the final game to love.

Last July, Burrage urged gambling companies and social media companies to do more to tackle online trolls.

Speaking after her first-round defeat to American Caty McNally at Wimbledon, Burrage said she has had to stop herself from looking at her phone due to online abuse.

"I think it's very simple to have someone's ID connected to their account and that would, I think, quickly stop what people write and make them more accountable," Burrage said.

"I'm just guessing that they're gamblers; some of them say, 'You've lost me this amount of money' or whatever, so some of them are. I don't know, that's the only explanation I've got otherwise they are just very bad people.

"But yes, it's tough and today I'm trying not to look at my phone. It's not easy to deal with, but I do think there could be more being done."

A report from the Women's Tennis Association and International Tennis Federation revealed that 458 players were direct targets of abuse in 2024. The report, produced using an AI-led detection system developed by the Signify Group, found that 40 per cent of the social media abuse came from frustrated gamblers, a figure that rose to 77 per cent for direct abuse directed towards players' personal accounts.

Image: Katie Boulter blames gamblers who have lost money for the abuse

Katie Boulter also opened up about the level of abuse aimed at some players and said she and her family have received death threats last year.

Boulter believes much of the abuse comes from gamblers who have lost money and while she has learned how to better handle it over the years, incidents can raise genuine concerns for her safety.

"I think it just kind of shows how vulnerable we are. You really don't know if this person is on site. You really don't know if they're nearby or if they know where you live or anything like that," she said.

"At the very start of my career, it's probably something I took very personally [...] getting comments about the way you look."

"It becomes more apparent every single time you go on your phone."

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

Sports.title: Norwich thrash Derby to heap pressure on Eustace
Sports.content:
Norwich piled more pressure on Derby boss John Eustace after thrashing the Championship strugglers 4-0 at Pride Park.

On his 47th birthday, Eustace saw his side ripped apart by the pace and movement of the Canaries, who scored three times before the break.

Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich in complete control before substitute Jovon Makama wrapped up a third straight win for the visitors and condemned Derby to a fourth defeat in five games.

Derby have won only once this season and Friday night's home game with Bolton now looks like a huge one for Eustace.

They went into the game as only one of two teams without a home win in the Championship and they fell behind in the eighth minute. Jack Stacey crossed from the right and although Yongwa's header was saved, Musaba slammed the rebound into the roof of the net.

Musaba had a great chance to score his second in the 15th minute when Andre Brooks played him in but his low shot struck the legs of goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Norwich looked like scoring every time they came forward and after Zetterstrom made a reflex save to deny Mathias Kvistgaarden, Maghoma made it two with a curling effort from the edge of the box in the 27th minute.

Boos rang out from the home fans and only the woodwork denied Norwich a third when Stacey's shot hit the inside of a post and was cleared off the line by Alex Mowatt.

It got even worse for Derby just before half-time when they were torn apart again and after Brooks fired the ball in from the right, Yongwa made no mistake from 12 yards.

The half-time whistle was met with another chorus of disapproval from the home fans and it was no surprise when Derby made three substitutions for the second half.

Derby at least had an effort on target with a Carlton Morris header forcing Daniel Grimshaw into a diving save and there was certainly more urgency about their play but Norwich were not finished.

Makama came to the party in the 66th minute with a rasping drive from the edge of the area which Zetterstrom could not keep out.

That was the signal for Derby fans to head for the exits and some of those who stayed joined in when Norwich fans taunted Eustace with chants of "sacked in the morning".

It was certainly a miserable night for Eustace and Derby, who even at this early stage look like a team fighting relegation.

The managers

Derby's John Eustace:

"To be in the situation we are now is really disappointing.

"There are reasons why, we've got nine defenders out which certainly doesn't help, but collectively we haven't been good enough and I take responsibility for the performances.

"Ultimately you can make as many excuses as you want with injuries and suspensions but I get judged on results and results haven't been good enough.

"The club is much bigger than me and all the great work we've done over the last 16 months has been something I'm very proud of and not to continue that throughout the summer and up to now has been tough.

"Football is about results and to lose 4-0 at home after losing 4-1 at the weekend is not acceptable and it's my head at the table.

"Of course it hurts, I'm a very proud person but the Championship is relentless, it's ruthless and we have a lot of injuries and we have to respect that fact as well.

"It is very frustrating at the moment but I'm not a quitter and I know we can get more out of the group which is something we will keep trying to do."

Norwich's Philippe Clement:

"I'm really pleased with what the team did, we could have scored more than the four goals and keeping a clean sheet after a long time will also help the team with their confidence.

"The structure of the team is good and I've seen a lot of positives with the guys who started and the guys who came on. That's what I want to see, no complacency and a mature game in controlling it in most of the moments.

"The group knows me for a long time and I've said the message a lot of times, I hate it when people become complacent, I want to see a hungry team full of desire for more and not to be happy with where they are."

Sports.title: Stoke battle to victory at Blackburn
Sports.content:
Jack McGlynn scored an audacious free-kick as Stoke held off a late Blackburn comeback to win 2-1 in the Championship.

After weathering early Blackburn pressure, McGlynn caught everyone off guard in the 43rd minute, finding the net with a spectacular set piece from the left instead of the expected cross to notch his fourth of the campaign.

Substitute Moussa Baradji's own goal in the 68th minute gave the Potters a deserved cushion as they seemed set for a comfortable victory.

But Andri Gudjohnsen's tap-in halved the deficit in the 87th minute and the Icelandic forward thought he had equalised three minutes later when skilfully steering a header into the far corner but referee Andrew Kitchen penalised the striker for a push, much to the fury of the Rovers fans and coaching staff.

Despite the late scare, Stoke held on to make it eight wins in 11 and move level on goal difference with second-placed Birmingham.

Stoke's victory here last season owed much to Viktor Johansson's heroics and he was at it again within four minutes when he produced a stunning stop to tip Todd Cantwell's rasping 18-yard drive behind.

Johansson was needed again close to the half hour when Hayden Carter pounced on a loose ball and strode forward into the space to unleash a low drive that the Swede pushed wide for a corner.

Despite their dominance, Rovers fell behind just before the break thanks to an outrageous free-kick from McGlynn. Wide on the left, the American went for goal rather than sending in a cross everyone was expecting and while Balazs Toth got a hand to it, the referee checked his watch to indicate it was over the line.

Dapo Afolayan planted a header wide of the far post after meeting Jayden Fevrier's right-wing cross, as Rovers tried to respond.

Robert Bozenik spurned a glorious chance just after the hour when played through by Million Manhoef, but he could not slot beyond the outstretched Toth.

Stoke recycled possession, the ball fell to Ben Johnson on the edge of the area and his venomous strike deflected wide with Toth well beaten.

The visitors' pressure finally told in the 68th minute when Manhoef was given time and space to race through Blackburn's defence and though Toth pulled off a sharp save down to his left, substitute Yuri Ribeiro's attempted clearance hit fellow replacement Baradji and rebounded into the empty net.

Gudjohnsen handed Rovers a lifeline three minutes from time when Johansson failed to hold Sam Morsy's shot, pouncing for his ninth of the season and he thought he had helped Rovers to a great escape with a towering header three minutes later from Gady Beyuku's cross but it was controversially ruled out and Stoke held on.

The managers

Blackburn's Tony Mowbray:

"Having watched it back, it's embarrassing really. People come to watch football to see entertainment and goals.

"Listen, I can't understand it really. I've watched it back. Does he put his hands up? Yes because the guy is going to back into him, to protect himself and hold him off. Is it a forward motion and a push? No. Does the guy throw his arms up in the air? Yes. I think the referee gets it hugely wrong. Hugely wrong.

"What hurts a little bit more is the inconsistency of the officials, I suppose.

"Thinking back a few weeks to West Brom away when Gudjohnsen gets blatantly pushed with two hands. Play on, they go down the other end, get a penalty, get back to two each and then win the game late on. Just the inconsistency of it.

"I thought ultimately we played pretty well tonight. We've played probably not as well and won football matches. There you go, that's the game."

Stoke's Mark Robins:

"You look for quality in the game and the first goal was that. Honestly, I saw the goalkeeper, where he was stood and I'm thinking 'go on, please see it'.

"He (McGlynn) moved to his right a little bit more to open his stance up and I thought 'go on', and he did it and honestly, he's the only one who could do it out of our team on the pitch. I think (Todd) Cantwell may try that. He's got the audacity to do that, and the ability to do that. I also think there's a couple of others on our team who could do that, who are that good.

"But for Jack, that's incredible. To see it, to spot it, to try it - but to execute it is absolutely fantastic.

"We manage to hold on after the goal was disallowed but rightly so, picked the three points up. Support was absolutely brilliant."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick enjoyed one of his finest nights as a Manchester United player in the Champions League against Roma, scoring twice in a 7-1 win in the quarter-final, second leg in 2007. The re-run here was all about his managerial survival at the club.

The situation looked impossibly grim for him at half-time. Amid an atmosphere of continued fan anger towards the United ownership, Carrick’s team had been implausibly bad. Roma took a 2-0 lead into the break and the truth was that the scoreline greatly flattered United.

What happened next was a fightback for the ages. For Carrick, it might even have topped 2007. United’s defending had been so loose, so generous. But they finally showed the other side to their game – the one about attacking punch; derring-do. They found a solution to their woes at the back. Keep the ball in the other half.

Matheus Cunha was the hero and it said plenty about the chaos of this tie, the wildness of the emotions, that he ended up being sent off for a second yellow card in the 90th minute. His lunge at Leonardo Balerdi was the definition of a rush of blood.

Before that, Cunha had supplemented a Bruno Fernandes penalty – which the captain converted after a retake – with a touch and finish in the 83rd minute following an error from Balerdi. Then came the coup de grace.

It was a burst from Kobbie Mainoo, who was positive on his return to the starting XI after injury, and a fizzed pass from the substitute, Shea Lacey. Cunha took the ball with a lovely first touch before flashing a shot in off the inside of the near post. Cunha likes to celebrate his goals with a surfing move. This time, having torn off his shirt, it was a surf in the crowd, which led to his first booking.

The United support sing about having seen it all. This was just extraordinary. Can it save Carrick? It was the team’s first win in 10 matches in all competitions so it was only a small step forward, even if it put United in a good position to qualify for the knockout rounds of the Champions League. In the heat of the moment, it felt like a giant one.

Carrick will go into Sunday’s Premier League game at home against Aston Villa – another must-win – with renewed belief. It was easy to say that his players had fought for him. As much as that, after all of the criticism of them, they fought for themselves.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes hits his retaken penalty high into the net to start the United comeback. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

Carrick had cut a relaxed figure at the pre-match press conference on Monday. He had seen some good signs, he insisted. There had been bursts. A win was coming. Nobody saw it at half-time, only yet more evidence of the defensive disasters that have blighted the season.

With Luke Shaw still injured, Carrick was forced to persist with Diogo Dalot out of position at left-back. Dalot pushed high at the outset, which felt bold. His positioning was pure folly on the opening Roma goal.

The visitors transitioned quickly and when Rodrigo Mora looked up from the inside left, all he could see was Matías Soulé in acres of space on the opposite channel. Where was Dalot? Mora played the pass. Soulé took a touch and swept past the exposed Senne Lammens.

Quick Guide Champions League roundup: PSG hit Villarreal for six Show Paris Saint-Germain set a record as the quickest team to score four goals in the Champions League by powering into a 4-0 lead after 17 minutes against Villarreal on their way to a 6-0 win. João Neves started the goal-blitz before Desiré Doué, Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz quickly put the tie to bed. Ruiz struck his second to make it 5-0 soon after the interval and substitute David Boly completed the scoring as PSG extended their 100% Champions League start and moved three points clear at the top of the table. Since taking just two points from their first three Ligue 1 games this season, which included a 2-1 home defeat to Monaco, PSG have now won 10 successive games in all competitions. Inter were equally convincing, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip. Yann Bisseck curled in the opener from long range, Pio Esposito headed the second before ⁠half-time and Piotr Zielinski completed the scoring from ​distance after ​the restart. Sporting Lisbon beat Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, a day after parting ways with their head coach, Rui Borges. Under the reserve coach, Tiago Fernandes, the Portuguese giants picked up their third win in the Champions League this season, with Issa Doumbia scoring the decisive goal in the game at Stamford Bridge. Aleksey Batrakov scored two goals in quick succession to seal a 2-0 win for Galatasaray against Stuttgart. Batrakov opened the scoring in the 12th minute at Rams Park and struck again three minutes later. Austria's Lask won 4-0 against Slovan Bratislava and Bodø/Glimt drew 0-0 with Lille Stadiums across Europe fell silent before kick-off in memory of the Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel, who died earlier on Tuesday after a collision on the pitch in the Spanish second division match against Andorra on Monday. Agencies Photograph: Andreu Esteban/EFE Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

United’s defending for the second goal was even worse. Leny Yoro turned and ran back towards his own goal as Roma advanced up the left and when the move appeared to have broken down for them around the United box, there was Harry Maguire to gift it back to Soulé with a dreadful miskick. He dropped his shoulder and shot; the ball hit Ayden Heaven’s hand and Donyell Malen converted from the penalty spot. Again, Dalot had been high up the pitch.

The mutiny could be felt before kick-off. The green and gold balloons of protest against the Glazers blew around the stadium. The sounds of it were everywhere; the chants against the club’s ownership a constant. When the clock showed 20 minutes and five seconds – or 2005; the year of the Glazer takeover – the Stretford End erupted in a planned move; hurling tennis balls down on to the pitch.

Moments earlier, a grisly Dalot error on the ball had almost led to Malen getting in for a third Roma goal and the first half was just an ordeal for United. Roma were well organised in their 3-4-2-1 shape and they got in up the right time and time again.

View image in fullscreen Matias Soulé celebrates scoring Roma’s first goal to stun Old Trafford. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

They might have had many more before the interval; Mora, Malen and Soulé all went close. United were so easy to play through. They were nervous on the ball. The lack of cohesion was glaring.

Carrick was in the last chance saloon during half-time. Maybe United had nowhere further to fall. They rebelled. Carrick lost Carlos Baleba in the 46th minute after the midfielder pulled his hamstring as he shaped to shoot in a promising position. Then United caught a break – two, actually – and the mood shifted sharply.

It was a soft penalty award for a push by Gianluca Mancini on Cunha after he played a give-and-go with Fernandes. But when United had that sinking feeling after Fernandes saw his kick saved by Devis Vásquez, they were reprieved when the referee, Jesús Gil Manzano, ordered a retake for encroachment. Fernandes lashed home.

Bryan Mbeumo, played through by Cunha for a one-on-one with Vásquez, saw his shot hit one post and then the other one before refusing to cross the line.

United threatened from corners. Maguire went close. Dalot had a header cleared off the line. It was Dalot’s cross for Cunha’s equaliser – a reward for the full-back’s perseverance. Cunha’s winner was the prompt for bedlam.

Sports.title: Raphinha underlines Barcelona’s class to give Aston Villa a reality check
Sports.content:
This was a chastening night for Aston Villa, and a familiar one for Unai Emery in this corner of town. On a processional night at the Camp Nou Barcelona produced a performance of unhurried, high-grade incision, easing to a 3-0 Champions League victory that never really seemed to tip into an actual close-quarter contest before it was already gone.

“There are a lot of things to learn today,” Emery said afterwards. “Overall we are competing fantastically in the Champions League; we have nine points. Today, we saw there is still more to do to get to this level. Even sometimes in this match we were close to achieving it. We had chances, but we must be ruthless in the final third. Three-nil maybe was more than we deserved.”

This Barcelona team will always give you a chance, a thrilling mix of high-spec possession football and large open spaces behind their own teasingly high line. But Villa never looked like getting their teeth into those tender spots, always held at arm’s length, fists whirling in the space between.

Two goals here for Raphinha maintained his numerically superlative start to the season. But Pedri was the real star, producing 69 minutes of elite midfield guile, a footballer who at times like these seems to be tickling you very gently to sleep while someone else sticks the dagger in.

This was a significant game for its emotional weight, rather than any real sporting jeopardy at this early meandering stage in the Champions League’s expanded format. For the Villa fans crammed into their pen at the top of the stand it was a chance to register a note of progress for this high-wire, ever-evolving team just by taking part.

Currently the Camp Nou is in a state of mid-renovation chaos, packed with debris and random clutter, and with vast gushing holes in the raggedy corrugated roof. Think: Old Trafford, but deliberately like that. The new tiers at the top of the stands are already in place. The internal fixtures are being laid between hoardings and fences. Even on a drab and chilly November night you could already feel the outline of the coming mega-stadium.

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal curls Barcelona into an early lead. Photograph: Pedro Salado/Getty Images

But the atmosphere here was still a little thin at the start, the cagoule-clad home sections heavily speckled with empty seats. Hansi Flick put out a strong team here, with Lamine Yamal on the right and his hard-running straight-man Anthony Gordon on the opposite flank. Rodri and Pedri were the midfield pivot, a delicious-looking thing in outline, two physical extremes, the familiar wardrobe-like unit of high-spec midfield generalship, and next to him a more classically twirling, ball-funnelling Barça-issue sprite. Pedri is fun to watch even away from the ball, with that easy, fluid way of moving, just rolling along, never really seeming to stop or switch directions, like a paper bag being blown across the turf.

João Neves started the goal-blitz before Desiré Doué, Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz quickly put the tie to bed. Ruiz struck his second to make it 5-0 soon after the interval and substitute David Boly completed the scoring as PSG extended their 100% Champions League start and moved three points clear at the top of the table. Since taking just two points from their first three Ligue 1 games this season, which included a 2-1 home defeat to Monaco, PSG have now won 10 successive games in all competitions. Inter were equally convincing, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip. Yann Bisseck curled in the opener from long range, Pio Esposito headed the second before ⁠half-time and Piotr Zielinski completed the scoring from ​distance after ​the restart. Under the reserve coach, Tiago Fernandes, the Portuguese giants picked up their third win in the Champions League this season, with Issa Doumbia scoring the decisive goal in the game at Stamford Bridge. Aleksey Batrakov scored two goals in quick succession to seal a 2-0 win for Galatasaray against Stuttgart. Batrakov opened the scoring in the 12th minute at Rams Park and struck again three minutes later. Agencies Photograph: Andreu Esteban/EFE Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Emery picked a team to press and stifle the space. It was always likely to be the plan against these opponents, ideologically wed to their own version of the Cruyffian omni-ball possession game. But then, everyone has a plan until they get lulled into a state of early-onset mental fatigue chasing shirt numbers and empty spaces.

Villa sat deep and snapped into their challenges. There were a couple of long passes from John McGinn on the right to set Nicolas Jackson in beyond the Barcelona line. On the other side Lamine Yamal looked, as ever, like a different species of human every time he took the ball, just in the way he snaps and grooves inside, a player who walks on to every pitch carrying his own portable yard of space.

With seven minutes gone it was Lamine Yamal who opened the scoring, in a way that felt almost too easy and too natural, cutting in from the left, too quick in his movements, all alone in front of goal suddenly even in that crowded space, with time to clip a simple left-footed shot into the far corner.

The Camp Nou let out a devotional roar. Lamine Yamal ran through his brand-friendly celebration routine in front of the ultras behind the goal. And at that point you feared for Emery’s team on that open right side.

Villa did come surging back straight away, winning a succession of corners. Johan Manzambi shot wide after good work from Jackson. But with 12 minutes gone Ian Maatsen was booked for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he eased away by the touchline, a Chekhov’s shotgun-style scenario for any full-back given the nightmarish job of marking this miracle of feints and snaps and pond-skater glides.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Gordon had a shot well saved by Zion Suzuki after a disastrous attempt to play out from the back had been strangled by the Barcelona press. But the game wasn’t really changed by Barcelona going 1-0 up. When they play like this the test is as much patience, concentration and retaining the energy to break when chance arrives. It did finally on 33 minutes, Manzambi driving down the left before shooting too close to Joan García.

But half-time arrived with Barcelona looking a little too easy and unbloodied for their lead.

Rodri was withdrawn and replaced by 19-year-old Marc Bernal, another high-grade home-farmed Catalan central midfield product. Nothing much changed. Villa continued to chase shadows, and also press, mark and nibble at the ankles of shadows whenever they got the chance.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha slots a first time finish past Aston Villa’s goalkeeper Zion Suzuki for his second, and Barcelona’s third. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP

And with 52 minutes gone it was 2-0, the goal scored by Raphinha via a deflected shot, Villa seeming a little hypnotised by a sustained spell of possession and pressure. Pedri made the moment happen with a driving run through the centre followed by a nudged forward pass. It was a fascinating piece of midfield play. Pedri had spent the previous 90 seconds lurking behind João Cancelo, sitting in that space and watching the play, then accelerating on to the ball like a rugby union full-back waiting for the moment to enter the line.

Emery made a triple substitution on the hour mark but before long it was 3-0. This time it was Cancelo’s turn to produce a moment of sublime skill. First he skipped away form McGinn like a man teasing the family labrador. Then he produced an outrageously cinematic low cross with the outside of his right foot for Raphinha to twinkle in and finish neatly again. The goal was his 19th in 13 appearances this season for Barcelona.

Villa came close, clipping the post from a Barcelona head in the crush at a corner. Pedri came off to an adoring ovation: he is just a delight to watch when he has space to direct the flow and tempo of the game. Villa barely got close enough to shake his hand before he was gone.

The final minutes ticked down in front of a steadily emptying stadium. Villa are still well-placed in the first phase mega-table. Emery will crave another chance to get closer to this calibre of opponent before the campaign is out. But this was a demonstration of the gap, still, at the very top.

Sports.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
Sports.content:
“This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final. On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or, the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious.

It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good.

Although it began with Julián Alvarez bending a shot just wide after 115 seconds, the best picture of the first half was probably the Argentinian’s second shot nineteen minutes later. If that first effort had come from the edge of the area, the chance presenting itself, the second came from the edge of the centre circle, deep inside Atlético’s half and was not so much about opportunity as the lack of them. True, Manuel Neuer was a long way off his line but Alvarez was seventy yards away and his shot never really took flight and was never likely too either, drifting wide.

It was hard to avoid the conclusion that he had gone for it out of a kind of impotence, a desire to do something, anything. Atlético were given so few chances to get near to Neuer’s goal and not very many to get near the ball. There was one moment when a Marc Pubill cross almost reached Alexander Sørloth who couldn’t duck low enough to reach it at the far post, and another when the Norwegian momentarily seemed to have escaped Dayot Upamecano. That, though, was about it. He cut a large and pretty lonely figure.
