Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Could Land Vergil Ortiz With Lara Win
Sports.content:
The winner of the Tim Tszyu vs. Erislandy Lara fight could face the winner of Vergil Ortiz Jr. vs. Keith Thurman in the first quarter of 2027, according to Chris Mannix. Tszyu will challenge Lara for the WBA middleweight title on December 12 in Australia.

The target is the first quarter of 2027. Both December fights have to play out, and the winners would still have to make a deal.

Boxing executives love mapping out tournament brackets on paper, but they constantly ignore whether the American public actually cares enough to buy the final product.

Neither Ortiz Jr. nor Tszyu has established real pay-per-view drawing power in the United States. Tszyu sells tickets in Australia, but putting him behind a stateside paywall has always yielded modest numbers. Ortiz produces exciting scraps, yet his profile remains largely confined to hardcore followers rather than mainstream sports fans. Expecting casual buyers to drop $60 to $80 on DAZN PPV for Ortiz against Tszyu was already a massive stretch.

If the upsets hit, the whole concept falls off a cliff.

Keith Thurman has fought only once in nearly five years, and Erislandy Lara turns 44 next spring. A Lara-Thurman clash in 2027 belongs in a time capsule from 2017, not on a premium pay-per-view platform. Lara’s safety-first, counter-punching style has always been poison for commercial metrics, while Thurman’s long stretches of inactivity killed off whatever casual fanbase he once commanded.

Building an expensive pay-per-view model around two fights that could easily produce Lara vs. Thurman is promotional Russian roulette. If the favorites slip, the networks are left holding the bag on an unsellable relic.

Lara can make Tszyu look bad by taking half a step back and catching him with the straight left when he reaches. Tszyu will have to cut off the ring and make Lara work after he lands, because following him around gives the champion time to pick his shots and get out. At 43, how often can Lara do that if Tszyu keeps making him move? That’s the part of this fight Tszyu can exploit.

Against Ortiz, Tszyu could find himself doing the moving. Ortiz can get close behind his jab and go to the body when an opponent covers up. Tszyu likes to plant his feet to get power on his right hand, and Ortiz would give him chances to throw it. The cost is what comes back if Tszyu stays in front of him after he lets it go. He could land the cleaner shot and still spend the rest of the round trying to get off the ropes.

Thurman can spoil that pairing, and Lara can make the whole discussion academic for Tszyu. But if Tszyu wins in December and Ortiz is next, he could have only a few months to prepare for a man who will make him fight for the same ground Lara is willing to give up.

Sports.title: Jermell Charlo Takes the Safe Route With Brock Jarvis
Sports.content:
Jermell Charlo’s choice of Brock Jarvis reveals the modest ambitions of his ring return. After more than three years away, the former undisputed 154-pound champion booked a matchup designed for him to win. Jarvis brings genuine power, yet the two premier opponents on his resume stopped him inside four combined rounds. Keith Thurman did it at age 36 while shaking off a three-year hiatus himself.

Charlo (35-2-1, 19 KOs) meets Jarvis (23-2, 21 KOs) across ten rounds at middleweight. The bout serves as the co-feature to Tim Tszyu’s clash with Erislandy Lara at Cbus Super Stadium on Australia’s Gold Coast, streaming on DAZN on December 12. For Charlo, it marks his first live action since dropping a lopsided decision to Canelo Alvarez up at super middleweight in September 2023.

Thurman had sat out since 2022 prior to taking on Jarvis in March 2025. Even as an older veteran operating well past his peak, Thurman needed just three rounds to dismantle the Australian. Any thought that ring rust might leave Thurman vulnerable vanished instantly.

Before that, Liam Paro served as the only world-level name on Jarvis’s ledger, wiping him out inside a single round back in October 2022. While Jarvis rebounded from the Thurman defeat by halting the undefeated Sam Beck in four rounds last August, his record against elite opposition remains telling. His 21 knockouts look great on paper, but that power evaporates against seasoned champions.

“I’m willing to fight on a co-main event all the way in Australia because that’s how hungry I am,” Charlo said.

Charlo publicly aims for a belt in a second division, yet this booking proves he wants an easy touch before testing ranked 160-pound contenders. During his peak run, Charlo broke down Tony Harrison in the 11th round to reclaim his WBC strap, then stopped Brian Castaño in the 10th round of their rematch to unify all four belts. He excelled at solving dangerous, technical operators who gave him early fits. Jarvis has never proven he can force an elite boxer into those kinds of adaptations.

The card placement carries plenty of irony. Charlo sits beneath Tszyu, who was originally scheduled to challenge him for the undisputed crown before a hand injury forced Charlo out in early 2023. Tszyu now gets to headline for a middleweight belt against Lara, leaving Charlo to rebuild on the undercard.

An early night would deliver Charlo the tune-up he wants while setting him up for serious contenders. However, if Jarvis manages to hang around or steal rounds late, everyone will see that Charlo has lost a step. Thurman barely needed to dip into his old toolbox to erase Jarvis, setting a clear bar for what Charlo must do.

Jarvis is custom-made for the showcase. He is an aggressive puncher with zero defense against elite competition, which makes him the perfect target to get starched inside three or four rounds. Once Jermell produces a highlight-reel knockout, his team can blast the clip across social media, erase the memory of the toothless Canelo performance, and sell the illusion that the old, ferocious Charlo is fully back.

From there, the real target board is tiny. If Tszyu beats Lara, an Australia stadium showdown between Tszyu and Charlo carries built-in promotional heat from their canceled 2023 meeting, and Main Event/No Limit Boxing will back up an armored truck full of cash to stage it.

If Tszyu falls through, Ennis is the next logical target. Boots has been hunting for an established, marquee American name to build a pay-per-view around, and Charlo offers name value without the lethal threat of an active prime champion. Beyond those two, nobody in or around 154 to 160 moves the needle financially to justify the risk.

Jermell wants the reward without running the gauntlet against young, hungry killers. Knocking out Jarvis is simply the paid audition to secure the bag.

Sports.title: IBF Reorders Lindolfo Delgado vs. Arthur Biyarslanov Talks
Sports.content:
The IBF made the correct call by keeping Lindolfo Delgado in contention for its vacant 140-pound championship after his withdrawal from the Riyadh event. Following a report from Darshan Desai, the sanctioning body ordered Delgado and Arthur Biyarslanov to reopen negotiations. While Biyarslanov certainly earned quicker clarity on the status of his bout, stripping Delgado of his title shot would have been an excessive penalty for prioritizing safety and preparation.

Delgado (24-0, 16 KOs) and Biyarslanov (21-0, 17 KOs) had been scheduled to meet on the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli undercard. Biyarslanov traveled to Saudi Arabia as planned. Delgado remained behind after his trainer, Robert Garcia, cited regional missile threats alongside a grueling travel schedule. Under that proposed itinerary, Delgado would have had barely two days on the ground to overcome jet lag and shed final pounds.

Biyarslanov voiced valid frustration after enduring twelve weeks of camp away from home, followed by seven days of silence in Riyadh. He put in the work, made the flight, and reasonably expected direct word on whether the contest remained intact. Delgado’s camp owed him that basic communication while sorting out logistical hurdles.

Still, traveling to Riyadh is not the same as arriving with proper runway to contest a world championship. Biyarslanov got into town early and settled into fight week. Garcia faced a delayed flight plan, extended ground travel, and a dangerously compressed weight cut. Just because one camp navigated the journey without incident does not invalidate the other side’s athletic and safety concerns.

Now, the ruling brings the two undefeated contenders back to the negotiating table for the title Richardson Hitchins vacated upon moving to 147 pounds. What remains is securing a firm location and date. Biyarslanov has already invested a full training camp and traveled across the globe. Before he launches another grueling camp, he deserves concrete details on where and when this matchup will actually happen.

Sports.title: Matchroom Is Wasting Teremoana Teremoana’s Prime
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana is nearly seven years older than Moses Itauma, but Matchroom is still handling him like a fragile prospect who just took up the sport. The Australian turns 29 in February, sits on 12 knockouts in 12 fights, and is doing nothing more than treading water.

Marching him out against Hemi Ahio on November 18 in Melbourne is pure filler, a safe exercise that teaches nobody anything.

Ahio has a right hand, sure, but he is a regional gatekeeper meant to be blown away. When Teremoana flattens him inside two rounds, Eddie Hearn will celebrate like something meaningful happened. It will not be.

Teremoana blew out Curtis Harper, Bowie Tupou, and DeAndre Savage in four rounds total. Stacking up quick knockouts against guys brought in to fall over proves nothing. Teremoana is running out of track to waste rounds on heavyweights who cannot throw back.

Matchroom should be throwing him in with fighters like Filip Hrgovic, Fabio Wardley, Joseph Parker, Frank Sanchez, or Bakhodir Jalolov. Parker has the ring knowledge to expose any flaw in Teremoana’s game. Sanchez would make him miss wildly, forcing him to adapt. Wardley would make him pay for every careless swing. Those bouts carry real risk, which is precisely what Teremoana needs if he expects to be taken seriously.

Jalolov is the real grudge match. The giant southpaw outpointed Teremoana at the Paris Olympics, and Teremoana has done little since then besides crush lower-tier opponents before breaking a sweat. A pro bout with Jalolov would settle whether Teremoana has actually grown into a genuine threat, or if he is simply a big puncher dominating weak competition.

Itauma is 21 and can afford easy nights while he matures. Teremoana has been a pro since 2020, turns 29 in months, and is burning up his peak years on glorified sparring sessions. Knocking out Ahio gets him to 13-0, but it does not tell the public whether he belongs with the elite. If Matchroom keeps feeding him soft touches for number 14, everyone will realize the promotional machine is just hiding him from real danger.

That Olympic background makes this entire situation impossible to defend. When an amateur competes on the world stage against elite international talent, he already knows how to box. He knows how to deal with different styles under immense pressure. Fighters with that kind of foundation are supposed to move quickly through the professional ranks. Instead, Teremoana is nearly twenty-nine years old, six years into his paid career, beating up club fighters who have zero business sharing a ring with him.

Eddie Hearn loves treating every signing like an unpolished project requiring years of gentle matchmaking. Matchroom protects records to manufacture shiny undefeated records, but that approach does Teremoana no favors. Heavyweights his size do not possess an infinite clock. Burning his athletic prime on showcase bouts against regional gatekeepers accomplishes nothing. Hearn gets cheap main events for overseas broadcasts while protecting his investment from suffering a loss.

The bigger issue rests directly on Teremoana. A heavyweight with genuine ambition never sits back quietly while his promoter dishes out safe opponents. He should be banging on Hearn’s door every week, demanding top fifteen names, forcing Matchroom to take the training wheels off completely. Elite punchers do not accept soft paydays. They push their handlers to secure bouts against legitimate contenders who possess the tools to punch back.

Settling for second-tier opposition reveals either a total lack of self-belief or satisfaction with being a protected house fighter. If he truly believed he belonged among the division elite, he would demand dangerous fights right now without hesitation.

Every time he signs to blast out an overmatched opponent in two rounds, he throws away months of his prime that he will never recover. If he refuses to force Matchroom into testing him against real competition, his career will end before anyone discovers how good he actually was.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Uses Online Backlash To Fuel Shane Mosley Jr. Clash
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley figures getting rinsed across social media might actually work in his favor. Losing his WBO middleweight strap threw his name directly into feeds belonging to fans who had never watched him box. Now, he plans on using Shane Mosley Jr. to make an impression that actually sticks.

“Winning caps it all off, 100 percent,” Bentley said during their Zuffa Boxing 12 faceoff on Sky Sports. “I mean, everyone’s saying my name. I wouldn’t know about flowers yet, ’cause right now I’m getting rinsed online, but that’s all cool.” Bentley pointed out that casual fans tuning in because of the drama finally get to watch him perform. He fully expects to stop Mosley inside the distance.

Bentley clashes with Mosley this Saturday at Copper Box Arena in London. It was the exact matchup Bentley pushed for before taking on mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández. The WBO shut down his appeal, stripping his belt on the spot. While Bentley kept his spot on the card, the sanctioning drama created an instant buzz. The real casualty was the world title he could have carried into a massive unification clash.

That loss stings because Bentley still craves marquee matchups. He insists he technically remains the champion, keeping his sights locked on the middleweights signed to Zuffa. Carlos Adames got mentioned during the press festivities. Bentley made it clear he intends to hunt division leaders as a challenger, targeting the exact names he wanted during his title reign. Zuffa offers the platform, yet Saturday comes without any guarantees.

Mosley acknowledged Bentley lost his strap through boardroom politics rather than ring action, though he still expects to cruise to a points victory. Coming off a signature win against Serhii Bohachuk, Mosley wants the spotlight Bentley created. Invading London to steal a victory puts Mosley first in line for major fights under the promotional banner. Forcing Bentley into a messy boxing match could also ruin the knockout statement Bentley promised.

Bentley walked himself into a trap. Flattening an opponent who just upset Bohachuk forces the critics to shut their mouths after the WBO embarrassment. An emphatic stoppage forces Zuffa to open the checkbook for Adames. Scraping past Mosley on a dull decision does nothing for him, leaving him on the outside looking in with zero leverage. Internet trolls jumped on his neck the second the belt vanished. Saturday determines if Bentley backs up his mouth or becomes a punchline in his own backyard.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Walks Into Clarke Ambush At Copper Box
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith gets back in the ring against Cheavon Clarke on Saturday, November 7, at Copper Box Arena in London. The bout headlines Zuffa Boxing 12, putting the former WBO cruiserweight champion in front of a man holding an amateur victory over him from 2016.

Billam-Smith enters at 22-2 with 14 knockouts, aiming to hold his place near the front of the division. Clarke comes in at 12-2 with 9 knockouts, looking to make his previous success count on a major professional stage.

The preliminary bouts begin at 12 p.m. Eastern Time, which is 5 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time. The main card takes over at 2 p.m. Eastern, or 7 p.m. locally in the UK. The headline ring walks are expected around 5 p.m. Eastern and 10 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time, though that timing will shift depending on how quickly the supporting fights wrap up. Viewers in the United States and Canada can watch the card through Paramount Plus. Fans in the UK and Ireland can watch the main card on Sky Sports, with online streaming through NOW and the preliminary matches carried on Sky digital platforms.

The supporting lineup features Denzel Bentley taking on Shane Mosley Jr. in a ten round middleweight co-feature. Heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter meets Ivan Balaz on the main portion of the show, followed by a cruiserweight match between Lucas Roehrig and Connal McDonald, a middleweight bout featuring Sam Hickey against Amaury Massenaux, and Kayla Allen versus Julia Igel. The preliminary portion includes Zach Parker against Umar Dzambekov at light heavyweight, Masood Abdulah taking on Adan Palma, and the debut appearance of Vinnie Kemp.

Both main event fighters fought grueling bouts in June. Billam-Smith wore down Ryan Rozicki until Rozicki stayed on his stool after the seventh round. Clarke hit the canvas twice in the fourth round against Jack Massey, yet recovered to stop Massey three rounds later. Clarke owns the quicker hands over ten rounds, which means Billam-Smith cannot afford to spend long stretches following his opponent around the perimeter.

Billam-Smith must use his jab to establish distance, force Clarke toward the ropes, and work on the inside to sap Clarke of his bounce. Even if Billam-Smith lands clean early, Clarke has already shown he carries fight-ending power when wounded, meaning the former champion needs sharp discipline to avoid getting caught on the way in.

For Billam-Smith, he is entering that dangerous zone where a fighter’s style catches up with their shelf life, making this matchup against Clarke a massive upset potential.

Look at his recent stretch. Billam-Smith does not have easy nights. He does not box on the outside and slip shots; he relies on imposing physical will, eating three clean punches to land four of his own. By the final bell against Gilberto Ramirez, Brandon Glanton, and Ryan Rozicki, his face looked like ground beef. His skin splits if someone looks at him wrong, and the scar tissue around his eyes has become an open invitation for referees and ringside doctors to intervene.

When a pressure fighter like Billam-Smith, who absorbs heavy punishment, starts racking up rounds at 35 or 36, the decline rarely happens gradually. It happens off a cliff. The punch resistance cracks, the reflexes slow by half a second, and suddenly shots that used to get brushed off start rattling the frame.

Clarke is precisely the wrong stylistic matchup for an aging, battle-worn brawler to face in a ten-round fight. He has the amateur pedigree and hand speed to exploit Billam-Smith’s porous defense. Billam-Smith comes forward in straight lines with his chin up. Clarke has already proven in the amateurs that his hand speed gives Billam-Smith fits, and fast combinations against an opponent with compromised scar tissue is a recipe for severe cuts early.

Despite his advanced age, Clarke still possesses real power and resilience. Jack Massey dropped Clarke twice in the fourth round, and Clarke still showed the composure and engine to recover and stop Massey three rounds later. If Billam-Smith hurts Clarke, he cannot just swarm carelessly, because Clarke throws violent counters when trapped.

At this point, the schedule works entirely against Billam-Smith. At ten rounds instead of twelve, the distance favors the explosive, faster starter. Billam-Smith typically needs eight or nine rounds of grinding pressure to break a man down. In a ten-rounder, if Clarke banks four of the first six rounds behind speed and angles, Billam-Smith runs out of road and has to chase recklessly.

If Billam-Smith gets dragged into another trench war where he has to swallow flush shots to make Clarke work, this has all the ingredients of an ambush. Clarke has the speed, the confidence from their amateur history, and the firepower to hand the former champion a costly defeat.

Sports.title: Mannix Says Munguía and Melikuziev Have Reached Terms
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev have reportedly come to terms for a WBA super middleweight title fight. Munguía named his mandatory challenger after beating Nikita Zon by unanimous decision Saturday in Riyadh, but Sergio Mora still doubts he’ll take the fight.

“I think Munguía is going to stay away from him,” Mora said during his discussion with Chris Mannix. “Well, I think he’s going to fight him. I don’t think he’s going to give up his belt, and everything I’ve been told [is] that they’ve come to terms on the fight,” Mannix said on his channel. He gave no date for the defense.

Mora had already picked Melikuziev before the Zon fight. He sees a natural 168-pounder who uses his southpaw angles better than Zon and hits harder. Mannix brought up Melikuziev’s close fight with Darius Fulghum, when he needed a knockdown in the 12th. That’s a fair reason to hesitate over picking Bektemir, but Munguía gave him something specific to work on in Riyadh.

When Zon hurt Munguía in the sixth, the champion bent forward and pulled his gloves up around his ears. Zon kept hooking at the sides of the guard. Mora thought a straight punch or an uppercut could have brought Munguía’s head up and given referee Tony Weeks a reason to stop it. Both men backed Weeks for letting it continue. Munguía came back to hurt Zon in the same round.

What would worry me about Bektemir is what happens before Munguía gets to the ropes. Munguía likes to walk a man down and get close enough to work with both hands.

Every step in gives a southpaw with good feet a chance to move outside his lead foot and send a left hand through the middle. Munguía can come back from one bad minute, as he showed against Zon. Against Melikuziev, he may have to solve that left hand every time he tries to get his own offense going.

Sports.title: Could Rocky Marciano Take Away Larry Holmes’s Jab?
Sports.content:
Larry Holmes was one win away from matching Rocky Marciano’s 49–0 record when Michael Spinks took his heavyweight title in September 1985. After losing a close unanimous decision, Holmes had something to say about the champion whose record he’d come up short of tying. “Marciano couldn’t wear my jockstrap,” he said.

I thought Spinks earned that decision by taking the final round, and I gave Holmes the rematch, which Spinks won by split decision. But the crack about Marciano got me thinking about something Holmes did in the ring. He sometimes left his left arm extended between jabs to keep a shorter man at a distance. Most fighters would try to get around it. I think Marciano would have started punching it.

Rocky could come up from his crouch with a short uppercut into the elbow or dig a hook into the upper arm when Holmes covered up. He’d take some clean jabs getting close enough to do it. But if those punches made Holmes think twice about leaving the arm out, Marciano would have more room to step in. A punch that looked wasted in the fourth could buy him a shot at the ribs in the tenth.

Holmes could make that a slow and painful trade for Marciano. A quick jab and half a step back would leave Rocky reaching for an arm that was already gone. If Marciano tried to cover the extra ground by ducking in from too far away, Holmes could catch him with the right uppercut. Rocky might do good work once he got his head against Holmes’s chest and still spend most of the round trying to get there.

The danger for Holmes would come when he started pulling straight back with his hands down. Marciano was behind against Jersey Joe Walcott before knocking him out in the 13th to win the title. In the Ezzard Charles rematch, he scored an eighth-round stoppage with his nose badly split. Holmes could be well ahead after ten rounds and still have to watch where his left hand came back after every jab. If it dropped to his waist, Marciano could throw his right over it without having to get all the way inside.

I’d take Holmes by decision over 15 rounds. I can see Marciano hurting him late, especially if the work on the arm took some snap off the jab. But Holmes could win the first two minutes of a round from a distance and make Rocky spend most of the last minute closing it. I’d give Holmes more of those rounds than I’d give Marciano the kind where he got close early and kept him there.

Ghana News.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
Ghana News.content:
South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's former ruling party, the African National Congress (ANC).

This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes.

Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection.

For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended.

Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime.

At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%.

Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral.

"What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday.

In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support.

The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard.

Sanele Ntombela (left), seen here with his friends Tshiamo Mbange (centre) and Lwandle Dladla, is excited to cast his vote

We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.

They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services.

But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change.

"We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said.

Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties.

On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road.

The ANC faces immense pressure to reverse years of decline

The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so.

The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision.

"It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said.

Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker.

Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it.

The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships.

South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery.

Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life and he told the BBC of the community's daily struggles with accessing water and electricity.

"Every Monday we know we won't have water after 2pm," he said.

Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the "arrogance" he says local leaders have towards residents and "change the status quo".

These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa's local governance.

Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa's 257 municipalities.

A recent report only gave 39 clean audits - the highest ranking a public entity can achieve - between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng's three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list.

Earlier this year auditor-general Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg "needs ongoing attention".

"If we don't that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living," she told lawmakers.

The city has been labelled "effectively bankrupt" due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years.

Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa's wealthiest city as well as the country's seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in.Of South Africa's eight metros, only three are governed by a single party. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party.

But that might change.

Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a "verdict ... and judgment" on the ANC.

"And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done," she said.

Several polls point to a continued decline in support for the party in Wednesday's election, contested by over 500 political parties.

One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC's support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021.

The same poll, along with others, points to a slight increase in electoral support for the Democratic Alliance (DA), especially in Johannesburg. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time.

DA leader Helen Zille has been vying for the mayoral chain in the city and her unusual campaign has attracted a lot of attention.

The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a "Gusheshe".

She believes the DA is the country's best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that "towns and cities that work best are under DA governance".

Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa's ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue being the order of the day across Gauteng.

These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities.

Zandile Mncube says things have got worse in her township over the years

Verwoerd said in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power.

Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country's best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC.

Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a "different story", Verwoerd said.

The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government.

The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election.

Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA.

A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections.

Another political analyst Dr Levy Ndou echoed Verwoerd's assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros.

"We're not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run," he said.

Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline.

Ndou attributed this to the "calibre" of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns.

South Africa's electoral commission has seven days to announce the results, but parties have 14 days to form a governing structure.

Ghana News.title: GIS trains 146 officers to strengthen firearms accountability
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) has trained 146 officers in weapon safety and armoury management in a move to strengthen accountability in the handling, storage and tracking of firearms and ammunition.

The two-day seminar, held at the Ghana Immigration Centre of Excellence in Accra on 28th and 30th October 2026, brought together regional and selected sector commanders for practical training in the safe handling, storage, issuance and tracking of weapons.

The programme was organised in collaboration with armoury management experts from the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), the Ghana Police Service (GPS) and the Small Arms Commission of Ghana.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Comptroller-General of Immigration, Mr Samuel Basintale Amadu, described the training as a timely intervention to protect officers, safeguard state-owned weapons, prevent the loss of firearms and ammunition, and sustain public confidence in the Service.

He urged participants to apply the knowledge and skills acquired to improve practices within their respective commands, stressing that proper weapon management was fundamental to professionalism, discipline and operational readiness.

The Armourer General of the Ghana Police Service, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Isaac K. Asante, highlighted the risks associated with weak inventory controls, poor record-keeping and inadequate supervision of weapons.

He urged Regional and Sector Commanders to maintain accurate registers, conduct regular inspections and enforce strict procedures for the issuance and return of firearms and ammunition.

DCOP Asante emphasised that every weapon and round of ammunition must be accounted for and traceable to a responsible officer at all times.

Lieutenant Colonel Frank Tetteh-Kumah, Commander of the 851 Ammunition and Explosives Ordnance Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces, also took participants through standard operating procedures governing military armoury management.

He encouraged the Immigration Service to adopt relevant aspects of the military’s systems, particularly in physical security, access control, documentation, routine audits and command-level accountability.

A delegation from the Small Arms Commission, led by its Director of Operations, Emmanuel Felix Mantey, facilitated sessions on stockpile management and firearm safekeeping.

The sessions addressed measures to prevent weapon diversion, restrict unauthorised access, improve storage conditions and ensure proper tracking of firearms throughout their lifecycle.

The Head of Intelligence of the Ghana Immigration Service, Deputy Commissioner of Immigration (DCOI) Kwasi Opoku Apau, described the seminar as timely, particularly in view of the Service’s expanding responsibilities in border and national security.

He said building officers’ capacity in weapon safety and armoury management was essential to the Service’s ambition to become a model institution in migration and border management.

The Ghana Immigration Service says the seminar is expected to improve compliance with weapon-safety procedures, strengthen supervision across Regional and Sector Commands and foster a stronger institutional culture of accountability in the management of firearms and ammunition.

Ghana News.title: Samuel Abu Jinapor writes on Tuesday’s incident in Parliament
Ghana News.content:
Samuel Abu Jinapor, MP for Damongo and Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee

At Tuesday’s sitting of Parliament, I raised serious and disturbing allegations concerning the alleged sale of Ghanaian diplomatic passports for amounts ranging from US$10,000 to US$50,000.

In my capacity as Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee, I called for the Minister for Foreign Affairs to appear before Parliament and account for these allegations.

The Majority Leader objected to my intervention. However, I maintained that allegations of such gravity, already circulating in the public domain, cannot simply be ignored. They have serious implications for Ghana’s international reputation, the integrity of our diplomatic passports and the credibility of our institutions.

As Ranking Member, I consider it my solemn duty to bring such consequential matters before Parliament, without fear or favour. I owe this duty to Ghana, my constituents and the New Patriotic Party.

The Rt. Hon. Speaker, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, subsequently directed me to withdraw the said statement.

I have enormous respect for the Office of the Speaker and for Rt. Hon. Alban Bagbin personally. That respect, however, does not diminish my constitutional and parliamentary responsibility to raise matters of grave national concern and demand accountability.

I am deeply grateful to my colleagues on the Minority side who stood firmly with me and walked out in solidarity when the Speaker directed that I be escorted out of the Chamber.

Let me be clear: Respect for parliamentary authority and the pursuit of accountability are not mutually exclusive.

I remain a disciplined, patriotic and respectful Member of Parliament, but equally a proud and committed member of the Mighty Minority, determined to hold the Government accountable, particularly in matters concerning our foreign affairs.

Accountability is non-negotiable!

God bless our homeland Ghana.

Ghana News.title: SDA Church steps in to rescue overstretched Wa Municipal Hospital from environmental crisis
Ghana News.content:
The Wa Municipal Hospital has received a critical environmental intervention from the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church to combat health risks amid severe labour shortages at the facility.

Members of the Wa Central and Peggrie Estate SDA churches dedicated their Sunday to an extensive weeding and sweeping operation across the hospital’s overgrown grounds.

The Wa Central District Head Pastor, Pastor Whaley Asonre Aboungo, explained that the facility was specifically chosen because strict environmental hygiene is essential to protect vulnerable patients from preventable conditions like cholera.

Citing biblical principles from Deuteronomy, Pastor Aboungo emphasised that cleanliness is a daily duty to God and humanity, noting that ignoring this civic responsibility is considered a sin.

The church's intervention highlighted the dire operational constraints facing the healthcare facility. Joseph Adongo, the Wa Municipal Hospital Administrator, revealed that the hospital currently has no dedicated outdoor labourers.

Although the facility already carries over 100 casual workers on its payroll, management faces immense difficulty hiring additional grounds staff. Adongo explained that whenever interior cleaning or cooking staff resign, the hospital is forced to pull its outdoor contract laborers inside, leaving the exterior environment neglected.

Expressing profound gratitude for the intervention, he appealed to other corporate bodies and religious organisations to emulate the SDA Church’s initiative to support their overstretched workforce.

Local leaders are leveraging this event to advocate for broader, systemic changes to waste management across the municipality.

Pastor Aboungo appealed directly to the President, regional ministers, and municipal chief executives to deploy public dustbins at strategic corners to actively discourage littering.

Addressing the structural issues, Municipal Environmental Health Officer Kanyiti Razak urged a shift from a linear waste disposal system to a circular economy that treats waste as a resource. Mr Razak recommended that citizens practice strict waste segregation at the source to reduce the volume of refuse transported to final disposal sites, and he challenged local religious leaders to dedicate at least five minutes of their regular services to sanitation education.

Moving forward, the SDA leadership plans to evaluate the uncompleted portions of the hospital grounds before deciding whether to return next month or redirect their ongoing community cleanup efforts to other public spaces, such as local markets.

Ghana News.title: NDC admits error in clearing Obuasi SHTS headmaster amid abuse allegations
Ghana News.content:
The General Secretary of the NDC, Fifi Kwetey, has acknowledged that the party mishandled its initial response to sexual abuse allegations against the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), saying it should have waited for further evidence before taking a position.

Zakaria Abdulai, the headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, was the NDC Juaben Constituency Secretary who had plans to contest in the NDC Juaben constituency chairmanship race.

He said the party’s decision to initially support the headmaster followed a meeting at which he strongly denied the allegations and presented them as a politically motivated attempt to destroy his reputation.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, November 3, Mr Kwetey said the party had originally intended to ask the headmaster to step aside or withdraw, given the seriousness of the reports emerging about him.

However, at a meeting on Monday, October 19, the party decided to hear his account before taking action, in keeping with what Mr Kwetey described as the need to give him a fair hearing.

He said the headmaster’s emphatic denial, coupled with a report by the Ghana Education Service (GES) which had cleared him, influenced the party’s decision at the time.

He said Mr Abdulai spoke with such conviction that party officials were persuaded that the allegations could have been part of a political plot against him.

Documentary changed the party’s position.

Mr Kwetey said, in hindsight, the party should have delayed its decision until it had watched the investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, which was broadcast later that evening.

He explained that the party was unaware that the documentary would be aired on the same day it met the headmaster and reached its initial position.

“If we had heard about it, we would have said we pause that decision, watch that evidence properly,” he said.

According to him, the documentary fundamentally altered the party’s understanding of the allegations and prompted a reassessment of the headmaster’s account.

Mr Kwetey said he watched the documentary and subsequently spoke directly with Mr Awuni the following morning, after which the party concluded that the matter was far more serious than had been presented during its earlier engagement with the headmaster.

He said the NDC consequently changed its position and directed Mr Abdulai to withdraw.

“It appeared like a flip-flop only because we had not had full access to that documentary,” he explained.

The General Secretary insisted that had the party seen the documentary before its October 19 meeting, it would have maintained its original position that the headmaster should step aside.

‘A lesson learned’

Mr Kwetey conceded that the party’s handling of the matter offered an important lesson about how it should respond to serious allegations, particularly where further evidence is expected to emerge.

He said the party’s failure to consider the documentary before making its initial decision had affected its assessment of the case.

The controversy centres on allegations of sexual abuse involving female students of Obuasi SHTS and the school's headmaster. The allegations were brought into the public domain through an investigation by Mr Awuni, triggering public concern and calls for accountability.

The headmaster was subsequently interdicted by the GES, while the police began investigating the allegations.

Mr Kwetey’s comments represent an acknowledgement by the NDC that its initial assessment was made without access to evidence that later proved decisive in changing the party’s position.

Ghana News.title: Cybersecurity gaps could expose Traffitech users to fraud — Technology Consultant
Ghana News.content:
Technology consultant Maximus Amertogoh has called on the Ghana Police Service to strengthen cybersecurity safeguards around its newly introduced Traffitech-GH system, warning that uncertainty over official notification channels could expose motorists to fraud.

He says the authorities must clearly identify the telephone numbers, sender IDs and websites authorised to communicate traffic violations and receive payments under the automated enforcement programme.

In a Facebook post, Mr Amertogoh asked how motorists could distinguish genuine notices from messages sent by fraudsters, especially when they weren't sure which number or website the police would use.

“We don’t know which number or website must send us the alerts. Got an alert from a number,” he wrote, urging the authorities to introduce additional security measures to protect users.

His concerns come as the Ghana Police Service begins nationwide enforcement under Traffitech-GH, a technology-driven system designed to detect traffic offences and improve compliance with road regulations.

The system's introduction has therefore brought into focus the need for sustained public education, not only on traffic offences and penalties but also on how to verify notices and protect personal and financial information.

How the system works

The programme, which became operational on November 1, uses cameras and sensors to capture vehicles committing traffic offences, initially focusing on speeding.

The evidence is reviewed by authorised personnel before an Electronic Notice of Violation (ENV) is issued to the registered vehicle owner through SMS.

The notice is expected to contain details of the offence, including the vehicle registration number, location, date and time of the violation, the applicable fine and the deadline for payment.

The police have indicated that the system is intended to reduce reliance on manual enforcement and confront motorists with evidence of their driving behaviour.

Police guidance on scam messages

The Ghana Police Service has published guidance to help motorists identify genuine Traffitech notifications and avoid fraudulent payment demands.

According to its official frequently asked questions, authentic electronic violation notices should carry the sender identification GPS-MTTD.

The police also caution motorists against making payments through unofficial links, private telephone numbers or individuals. Payments for Traffitech fines are to be made through the designated government payment portal.

Motorists who receive suspicious messages or calls are advised to report them to the police on 191 or 18555.

Ghana News.title: Diplomatic passport row rocks Parliament as Minority stages walkout
Ghana News.content:
Parliament was thrown into a tense confrontation on Tuesday, November 3, after Speaker Alban Bagbin ordered the Member of Parliament for Damongo, Samuel Abu Jinapor, out of the chamber following a heated disagreement over allegations that diplomatic passports were being sold for as much as $50,000.

The dispute, which ended with the Minority caucus abandoning proceedings in protest, erupted during a parliamentary discussion on the issuance of diplomatic passports, a process undertaken on the authority of the Minister for Foreign Affairs.

Contributing to the debate, Mr Jinapor alleged that he had evidence that diplomatic passports were being sold for between $10,000 and $50,000.

He called for an investigation into the alleged transactions, raising concerns about the integrity of the process through which the travel documents were issued.

His remarks drew an immediate challenge from the Majority Leader, James Agalga, who demanded that the Damongo MP produce evidence to support the claim or withdraw it.

Speaker Bagbin also intervened, directing Mr Jinapor to substantiate the allegation or retract it.

However, the exchange between the Speaker and the MP became increasingly heated as Mr Jinapor maintained his position before eventually withdrawing the allegation.

Despite the withdrawal, Mr Bagbin directed the Marshal of Parliament to escort the MP out of the chamber, citing his failure to comply promptly with the earlier directive.

The order provoked a protest from the Minority caucus, whose members subsequently walked out of the chamber in solidarity with their colleague.

The incident brought proceedings to a halt and exposed tensions between the two sides of the House over the handling of allegations made during parliamentary debate.

Ghana News.title: Bayern stay unbeaten in Europe with Atletico win
Ghana News.content:
Karl, 18, scored his first Champions League goal of the season

Bayern Munich continued their unbeaten Champions League start with a comfortable 2-0 win over Atletico Madrid.

Teenage star Lennart Karl had a first half to forget, but he redeemed himself by breaking the deadlock with a sneaky finish nine minutes after the restart.

The 18-year-old nipped in behind Robin le Normand, snatched the ball from the Atletico defender and chipped it effortlessly over Jan Oblak.

Konrad Laimer doubled the visitors' lead, blasting a ferocious strike over Oblak and into the roof of the net after Harry Kane picked him out in space.

Kane, in his first European match since winning the Ballon d'Or, had less luck in front of goal and missed a chance to equal Cristiano Ronaldo's record for the longest Champions League scoring streak.

The England captain had scored in his previous 10 appearances, but he failed to trouble the Atletico goalkeeper - shanking an acrobatic attempt wide before drilling a low strike off target.

Oblak made a fine save to tip a deflected strike from Dayot Upamecano on to the crossbar, while Manuel Neuer had a quiet evening at the other end - facing just one shot on target from the hosts.

Bayern remain unbeaten in the Champions League this season and they continue their campaign against Lille on Wednesday 25 November, while Atletico face Norwegian champions Viking on the same evening.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats

Seven flights across Europe were targeted by suspected bomb threats. While no official link has been established, several countries are investigating if the incidents were a coordinated attempt to disrupt airspaces.

World.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms makes US history as first Black woman elected governor
World.content:
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has made history as the first Black woman elected governor in the United States.

The former Atlanta mayor emerged victorious over her billionaire opponent, Republican Rick Jackson, who spent more than $200m of his personal fortune in an attempt to succeed popular outgoing Republican Governor Brian Kemp.

Bottoms, an adviser to former US President Joe Biden, was propelled to victory in part by the state’s significant Black voting bloc, which turned out in large numbers during early voting.

During the campaign, she faced Republican attempts to characterise her time as mayor as a crime-ridden decline for the state’s largest city.

“It’s a longstanding playbook to paint Atlanta as this big bad place,” Bottoms told the Associated Press news agency.

Bottoms’s win marks the third consecutive time that Georgia Democrats have nominated a Black woman for governor. Stacey Abrams lost in 2018 and 2022 to Kemp, who is leaving office in January after eight years due to term limits.

World.title: Ballot shortages reported in Dearborn, Michigan
World.content:
NewsFeed Ballot shortages reported in Dearborn, Michigan

Reports of ballot shortages at several Dearborn polling stations have raised concerns over voter access as Michigan residents cast their ballots in a crucial Senate race. The mayor has urged voters not to leave polling lines. Al Jazeera’s Mikail Malik reports.

World.title: Kazakhstan releases second tiger into the wild
World.content:
NewsFeed Kazakhstan releases second tiger into the wild

Kazakhstan has released a second Siberian tiger, this time a male named Amur, into a nature reserve as part of an ambitious programme to restore wild tigers to the country. Tigers have been extinct in Kazakhstan for more than 70 years.

World.title: Democrat Roy Cooper flips North Carolina US Senate seat
World.content:
Democrat Roy Cooper has won North Carolina’s United States Senate race, marking a significant pickup for the party as it looks to take back control of the chamber.

Cooper, a moderate former two-term governor, is the first Democrat to be elected to one of the state’s two US Senate seats since 2008, when former President Barack Obama carried it in his first White House bid.

He replaces outgoing Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who opted not to seek a third term in office after becoming a frequent critic of US President Donald Trump.

Since becoming the Democrats’ Senate nominee, Cooper consistently led his Republican opponent, former Republican National Committee chairman Michael Whatley, forcing Republicans to pull funding for Whatley’s campaign.

Cooper’s win is significant in a state that has narrowly voted for Trump three times since 2016.

World.content:

US President Donald Trump says he plans to stop the annual $3.8bn military aid package to Israel by the end of the year. US funding to Israel has become a contentious topic. What else do we know?

World.title: UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice amid record cases
World.content:
The election, held at UN headquarters, required several rounds of voting to fill the fifth and final seat.

Share UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice amid record cases on social media

The United Nations has elected five judges to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) for nine-year terms, as the court faces a record caseload, including South Africa’s genocide case against Israel over its war on Gaza.

The vote was held on Tuesday at UN headquarters, with candidates requiring an absolute majority in both the General Assembly and the Security Council to win.

Dapo Akande of the United Kingdom, Francois Alabrune of France, Mahmoud Daifallah Hmoud of Jordan, Rena Lee of Singapore and Phoebe Okowa of Kenya were elected to the 15-member panel.

Their terms are set to begin on February 6, 2027.

The two UN bodies initially agreed on four candidates but failed to select a fifth. The Security Council supported Ecuador’s Marcelo Vazquez-Bermudez, while the General Assembly backed Okowa, prompting further rounds of voting.

Vazquez-Bermudez later withdrew from the race, and Okowa subsequently won the backing of the General Assembly and the Security Council.

The votes were held by secret ballot concurrently, but separately.

The ICJ is based in The Hague and has 15 judges, each from a different country. They serve nine-year terms and may be re-elected. To ensure a degree of continuity, a third of the bench is elected every three years.

The election comes as the World Court faces a record workload.

ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa told the General Assembly on October 29 that 24 contentious cases are pending, covering disputes over territory, human rights and the interpretation of international treaties.



Among them is South Africa’s case accusing Israel of violating the Genocide Convention in its war on Gaza. The court has previously ordered provisional measures but has not issued a final ruling on whether genocide occurred.

In October 2025, the court issued an advisory opinion outlining Israel’s obligations towards the UN and humanitarian organisations operating in the occupied Palestinian territory.

Separately, the court announced on Tuesday that it would deliver a judgment on November 19 in The Gambia’s case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya minority.

Established in 1945, the ICJ is the UN’s principal judicial organ, responsible for settling disputes between states and providing advisory opinions on questions of international law.

World.title: Jon Ossoff wins Georgia Senate race, defeating Republican Mike Collins
World.content:
Ossoff is re-elected for a second term, winning a key seat for Democrats as the party tries to retake the Senate.

Incumbent Democratic US Senator Jon Ossoff has won re-election in the state of Georgia, one of the midterm cycle’s marquee contests.

He has defeated Republican Congressman Mike Collins, a staunch ally of President Donald Trump who faced intense scrutiny during the campaign regarding alleged ties to people espousing white supremacist ideology.

Ossoff, who has served as a US senator since 2021, campaigned on affordability, healthcare, and government accountability.

Collins, meanwhile, focused on the president’s agenda, immigration enforcement and reducing the size of the government.

Republicans had hoped to defeat Ossoff, the first Jewish senator in a state that backed former President Joe Biden in 2020 before reversing course and narrowly supporting Trump four years later.

Ossoff, seen by some as a possible contender for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, will rejoin his fellow Democrat in the Senate, Raphael Warnock, Georgia’s first Black senator, who is also rumoured to be considering a run for the presidency.

Georgia’s US Senate seats were critical for building the Democratic Party’s power in Congress and in the South, a largely Republican stronghold.

Ossoff was leading Collins 63 percent to 29 percent with 56 percent of votes counted, according to the Associated Press news agency.

Trump won Georgia narrowly in 2024 after losing the state to Biden in the 2020 presidential election.

In 2023, Trump and others were charged in Georgia with attempting to overturn the 2020 election loss by pressuring a senior state official to recalculate the results in his favour. The case was dismissed after Trump returned to office in 2025.

World.title: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
World.content:
Puente announced his decision at the end of a lengthy congressional session on Tuesday evening in which he had outlined new rail safety measures and had been grilled by the opposition.

He also said: "I am not only stepping down from my position as minister of transport, but... I am also withdrawing my name from the lists for the early legislative elections."

Puente's position immediately came under scrutiny after the 28 October crash.

The main opposition, the conservative People's Party (PP) and the far-right Vox, were both calling for his resignation - as were some of the government's allies.

They argued that the minister should take responsibility for a high-speed rail system that many Spaniards now regard as unsafe and whose credibility even Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez admitted was "broken".

The opposition also criticised Puente for appearing to blame human error for the crash, claiming the minister was trying to deflect the blame from his own failings.

But, having said he was going to remain in his post just a few days ago, his resignation appears to have taken many by surprise.

The rail accident and Puente's decision have come at a crucial moment in the Spanish political calendar, with early general elections on 29 November.

Many observers see the accident as a massive electoral setback to the Socialist-led government that will make it impossible for SÃ¡nchez to defy the polls and win the election.
