World.title: Nigeria: The Assassination of a Peacemaker
World.content:
blog

An Islamic preacher's brutal after-dark execution is a tragic reminder of what is at stake in the struggle to vanquish jihadism in northern Nigeria.

It tells you everything you need to know about the moral confusion surrounding the jihadist insurgency that has throttled vast swaths of northern Nigeria that Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka, the respected Islamic cleric who was gunned down outside his Dutsin-Ma, Katsina state residence last week by two armed men on a motorcycle, is being described by sections of the media as "controversial." For, if Malam Masussuka was "controversial," it raises the legitimate question of what to call his assassins.

Prior to his assassination (a friend of the cleric, one Adamu Abubakar, also lost his life), Mr. Masussuka had received numerous death threats, including on social media, from those who wanted him to stop doing what he was doing: preaching against extremism, contesting conservative interpretations of sections of the Quran and Hadith, and generally being a voice for theological moderation and peaceful coexistence between Muslims and Christians in the northern region of the country. In June 2025, Mr. Masussuka was honored for his efforts with a Peace Ambassador award by the Abuja-based Network for Good Governance and Transparency. Receiving the award, Mr. Masussuka reiterated the keynote of his advocacy as reorienting Nigerians "to embrace peace and unity" and challenging "hate speech and extremist ideologies."



If Mr. Masussuka's message of peace and tolerance was music to some ears, there were others who bitterly resented what he stood for and were desperate to have him removed from the scene. For example, in November 2025, just five months after he was honored for his peacemaking interventions, Mr. Masussuka received an official summons from the Katsina state government "for questioning over allegations that his sermons contravene established principles of Islamic law." At the time, Mr. Masussuka had also complained to the government that he was being insulted by members of Jama'atu Izalatil Bid'ah wa Ikamatis Sunnah--commonly known as Izala or 'Yan Izala.

Last week, though, it wasn't an Izala member who finished off Mr. Masussuka and his friend. Rather, it was gunmen deputized by a different extremist group, Jama'atu Ansarul Muslimina Fi Biladis-Sudan (meaning "Vanguard for the Aid of Muslims in Black Africa"), popularly known as Ansaru, who did. We know this because the group has claimed responsibility through a four-minute video obtained by Premium Times, a leading Nigerian newspaper. In the video, the terror group did not mince words about why they decided to eliminate Mr. Masussuka: because he was "an (arnai) infidel, not a Muslim. He was contracted to disrupt Islam and confuse Muslims." While it is not clear from Ansaru's video who or what entity they believed had "contracted" Mr. Masussuka, what is beyond dispute is the group's bloodcurdling warning to "other infidels" who "belittle the Hadiths of the Prophet": "You should repent. You should stop, or else we are coming for you." Translation: Ansaru is coming for you if you dare insist that (Nigerian) Muslims and Christians should peacefully coexist.

For some time now, the origins of the decadeslong jihadist violence in northern Nigeria and much of the Sahel have been a subject of intense litigation. While some scholars and analysts have insisted that the violence has nothing to do with religion and that it is best seen as an expression of legitimate grievance against failing states, others (I belong to this group) have argued that not only is the violence mobilized by various terror groups ultimately religious in essence, neither the violence nor the totality of their praxes can be understood without recourse to this basic and inextricable religious factor. The latter position does not dispute the need for investment in good governance, or that such will not work to vitiate the appeal of terror groups to disaffected young men; the argument has always been that after all is said and done, we need to face the reality that there are those who engage in violence because they see it as a religious obligation. For such people, no amount of investment in good governance or infrastructure will do. If that were so, there would be zero extremism in societies where social opportunities are abundant, relatively speaking. As a matter of fact, part of what Islamist groups take exception to (and they could not be more transparent about this) is the very apparatus of the modern state that seeks to pacify and draw them into its fold. Their grouse, not to put too fine a point on it, is unbelief, not the poverty of good governance.

This is where the late Malam Masussuka comes in. The reader will notice that he was abused, threatened, and ultimately assassinated, not for his extremism, but because he disavowed extremism. In other words, Mr. Masussuka lost his life because he preached moderation and peaceful coexistence, and we need no further confirmation than the video message from Ansaru. How in the world this makes someone "controversial" (looking at you, BBC) is beyond me.

For context, Mr. Masussuka is not the first Islamic cleric in northern Nigeria to be silenced for good by armed gunmen. In May 2025, Islamic scholar Sheikh Mustapha Aliyu was brutally murdered by armed bandits who had earlier abducted him. Around the same time, Chief Imam Alkali Salihu Suleiman was killed by his abductors in the northwestern state of Zamfara. Sheikhs Jaafar Mahmud Adam and Auwal Albani Zaria, both respected Salafi scholars, lost their lives in similar circumstances in 2007 and 2014, respectively.

Nor, crucially, is this Ansaru's first rodeo as far as eliminating its ideological adversaries is concerned. Since its emergence as a splinter faction of Boko Haram in 2012, the group has been linked to several high-profile attacks and kidnappings across the country. These include the 2012 prison break in Abuja, the ambush of a Nigerian military convoy in 2013, the kidnapping and subsequent execution of seven foreign construction workers during the same year, and assaults on military bases leading to the execution of dozens of Nigerian army personnel in August 2020 and April 2022.

Ansaru is officially proscribed and designated as a terrorist organization by Nigeria, the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union.

All of which raises an interesting question: If Ansaru and the many cognate terror groups currently active in Nigeria and across the Sahel have not been shy about their aims, why is it that many commentators continue to play the ostrich, attributing to terror groups moral and political objectives that they unambiguously deny? One reason is that many are wary of antagonizing Muslims--especially Muslim minorities in Western countries. Such people wrongly equate condemning the rampages of Islamists with taking sides with alleged Islamophobes. Nothing could be further from the truth. Indeed, refusing to back moderates like Malam Masussuka only allows religious bigots in northern Nigeria--and elsewhere--to avoid confrontation with their own demons.

Close 

Failure to decisively champion the Masussukas of this world has another regrettable consequence. It lets bigots get away with not just bad but objectively regressive arguments. Those of us who care about modernity and its amenities can ill afford not to speak up against the plague that is Islamist terror, which, drilled down to its essence, is a rejection of life, value pluralism, and the right of the individual to choose what is best for him (and vitally, change his mind) in matters of faith. What this means is that, from the standpoint of the Islamist terrorist, we should all be "infidels." This particular point bears emphasizing because, if past experience is anything to go by, it really does not matter whether or not we are interested in Islamism. Islamists are interested in us, and there is no better antidote to their poisonous ideology than standing our argumentative ground and taking sides with and empowering moderates and peacemaking agents like the late Mr. Masussuka.

In the meantime, one would hope that this tragedy is the final nail in the coffin of the risible argument that violence in northern Nigeria has nothing to do with religion. As should be obvious by now, no amount of wishing Islamism away would make it disappear.

World.title: Africa: Women Still Shut Out of Power As Gender Bias Undermines Africa's Democracy
World.content:
Discriminatory social norms, unequal power relations and growing gender-based violence continue to undermine women's participation in political leadership across Africa, despite progress in representation and the adoption of laws promoting gender equality, United Nations and European Union officials have warned.

Speaking at the opening of a two-day Inter-Regional Dialogue on Advancing the Transformation of Gender Social Norms to Enhance Women and Youth Participation and Representation in Leadership and Decision-Making in Zanzibar, UN Women Representative in Tanzania, Julia Broussard, said women's political representation remained disproportionately low, with entrenched attitudes continuing to influence who gets opportunities to lead.

Broussard said women occupy just over a quarter of parliamentary seats across sub-Saharan Africa, while in Tanzania they account for approximately 38 per cent of Members of Parliament.

However, she warned that progress in representation had not necessarily translated into equal influence in decision-making spaces.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Beyond the numbers, discriminatory social norms and unequal power relations continue to shape who is seen as a legitimate leader, whose voice is heard and whose contributions are valued," she said.

Citing the OECD's 2023 Social Institutions and Gender Index, Broussard said 43.9 per cent of Tanzanians believed men made better political leaders than women, highlighting the attitudes that continue to reinforce gender inequality in public life.

She said such perceptions had practical consequences, affecting the opportunities women receive, the support they can mobilise and their ability to influence decisions.

Women who venture into politics also face violence and intimidation, including technology-facilitated gender-based violence, which further discourages their participation.

Tanzania's Minister for Community Development, Gender, Elders and Children, Saada Mkuya Salum said women aspiring to political leadership continued to face social scrutiny and criticism that often left them with little opportunity to defend themselves.

"It's not easy at all. They will write. They will comment. They will do everything. And you don't have a chance actually to explain," she said.

She added that although progress had been made in empowering women, the systems and attitudes that historically excluded them remained firmly entrenched.

"So even the journey, women journey much as enhanced, are empowered somehow, but the journey has never and I believe it's not going to be that easy because of these systems that have been rooted," Mkuya said.

The Minister said Tanzania was proud of the progress made but warned that discriminatory social norms, weak institutional support and inadequate assistance for female candidates continued to undermine meaningful participation.

"We're proud of progress but they also tell us that when we are heading into the right direction we are not there yet and we will not get there as long as deep-rooted discriminatory social norms, institutions that support women's advancement and inadequate support for women candidates continue to restrict their participation," she said.

Mkuya also highlighted the additional burden placed on women by traditional household and caregiving responsibilities, which often leave them with less time and resources to build political networks, mobilise support and pursue leadership positions

European Union Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community, Jean-Marc Pisani, echoed the concerns, arguing that women's underrepresentation was not primarily a question of legal frameworks or leadership capabilities, but of deeply rooted social attitudes and the failure to translate commitments into practice.

Pisani said women held an average of 27 percent of parliamentary seats and 26 percent of local government positions across sub-Saharan Africa.

Regional disparities remain significant, with women accounting for approximately 31 percent of parliamentary representation in East and Southern Africa, 20 percent in Central Africa and 16 percent in West Africa.

Rwanda, where women hold 64 percent of parliamentary seats, demonstrates what can be achieved through political will and strong institutions, he said.

"Norms are not a cultural footnote to democracy. They determine who can take part in it," Pisani said, pointing to research showing that about half of the world's population still believes men make better political leaders than women.

He warned that violence against women in politics was increasingly moving into digital spaces, where abuse, threats and disinformation targeting female candidates and leaders were becoming additional obstacles to their participation.

"These are not private harms. They are attacks on democracy itself," he said.

Both officials called for a broader approach to gender equality, arguing that increasing the number of women in political institutions would not be enough without addressing the social and institutional barriers that limit their influence.

Broussard called for more inclusive political institutions, gender-responsive media coverage and the active involvement of men and boys in challenging discriminatory attitudes.

She also highlighted the importance of recognising young people, particularly young women, as agents of change rather than merely future leaders.

Pisani similarly urged men to take an active role in dismantling barriers by supporting women's political ambitions, speaking out against harassment and sharing decision-making power.

He also challenged journalists to examine how media narratives shape public perceptions of leadership and influence what girls believe they can achieve.

Close 

"The stories a society tells about leadership shape what its girls believe they can become," he said.

The two officials also pointed to ongoing interventions aimed at translating gender equality commitments into tangible improvements.

Broussard highlighted Tanzania's legislative reforms, including the recognition of violence against women in politics as an electoral offence under the Presidential, Parliamentary and Councillors Election Act.

She also cited initiatives supporting women parliamentarians through partnerships involving the Uwongozi Institute and the European Union, as well as community engagement programmes with the Tanzania Media Women's Association (TAMWA).

Pisani said the European Union had committed €90 million to its Gender Transformative Action programme, Breaking the Glass Ceiling, which supports gender-responsive policies, legal empowerment and community-level efforts to challenge discriminatory social norms.

The dialogue, bringing together participants from 23 countries, including journalists, women in politics and community leaders, is being convened by the International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA), with support from the European Union and UN Women.

The meeting seeks to facilitate exchanges on practical strategies for transforming gender norms and strengthening women's and young people's participation in leadership and decision-making.

World.title: Kenya: IG Kanja Denies Police Custody of Missing Tanzanian Activist Twaha Mwaipaya
World.content:
Nairobi — Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has denied that security officers arrested or detained missing Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya, even as he faced questions in the High Court over investigations into a wave of abductions.

Appearing before the Milimani High Court on Tuesday, Kanja told Justice Alexander Muteti that Mwaipaya had never been in police custody anywhere in the country, distancing the National Police Service from his disappearance.

"My Lord, I'd wish to inform this court we don't have the subject in our custody throughout the Republic of Kenya," Kanja said.

He also denied knowledge of any arrest involving the activist by officers from the National Police Service, insisting that police could not have removed someone they had never detained.



However, Kanja confirmed that a report on Mwaipaya's disappearance had been lodged at Ruai Police Station and that investigations were ongoing.

The Inspector General's appearance came amid mounting pressure on security agencies to account for the activist, who was reportedly abducted on October 25 in Kamulu, Machakos County.

The court had directed police to produce Mwaipaya, dead or alive, following an application by human rights organisations led by Vocal Africa.

Kanja maintained that police treat reported abductions as criminal offences and initiate investigations whenever such incidents are reported.

"Not at all, we don't abduct and make people disappear," he told the court when questioned about allegations of police involvement in enforced disappearances.

"Any abduction is to be treated as an act of criminality," he added.

However, his assurance that investigations were underway faced questions over whether authorities had made progress in identifying and prosecuting those responsible for abductions.

During cross-examination, lawyers challenged Kanja to name individuals who had been arrested and brought to justice over abductions reported in the country.

Asked whether he could identify any perpetrators who had been held accountable, the police chief said several investigations were still ongoing.

"We have got many cases that are running even now. Investigations are still ongoing," he said.

Pressed further on whether any suspects had been brought to book, Kanja described the investigations as tedious, saying they involved extensive work.

He acknowledged that some cases could have been concluded but said he would need more time to provide details.

Close 

The police chief nevertheless maintained that Kenyans had confidence in his leadership, arguing that the country remained safe and secure.

"From north to south, from east to west, this country of ours is safe and secure. The properties of people are safe and secure. That is why Kenyan people are confident in the Inspector General," he said.

The activist was reportedly seized at around 2pm on October 25 while travelling in a taxi to visit friends in Kamulu.

Amnesty International Kenya and the Defenders Coalition said the individuals involved were travelling in three vehicles, including a Toyota Land Cruiser hardtop, and called on authorities to urgently establish his whereabouts and guarantee his safety.

The High Court is expected to give further directions on the petitioners' application as the search for Mwaipaya continues.

In a post shared via X, Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF)'s acting spokesperson Chris Magezi said Elwelu had been arrested on Monday, November 2, describing him as a "renegade" officer who was involved in subversive activities.

World.title: Paul Pelosi hit with 6-month driving ban after pleading no contest to misdemeanor hit-and-run
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Paul Pelosi is banned from getting behind the wheel for six months after crashing into a parked car and fleeing in California wine country, landing the former House speaker’s husband back in court four years after his DUI conviction.

Pelosi, 86, struck an unoccupied parked vehicle in Yountville July 3 and fled, Napa County District Attorney Allison Haley said Tuesday.

The husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., pleaded no contest to misdemeanor hit-and-run and a traffic infraction for making an unlawful turn.

PAUL PELOSI ABSENT FROM FIRST COURT APPEARANCE ON HIT-AND-RUN CHARGE IN NAPA COUNTY CRASH CASE

Napa County Superior Court Judge Scott R.L. Young placed Pelosi on probation for one year and prohibited him from driving for six months, the maximum period allowed under the California Vehicle Code provisions cited by prosecutors.

Young also ordered Pelosi to complete a 10-day work program and report to the Napa County Department of Corrections for booking only by Nov. 20.

WATCH: PELOSI DODGES QUESTIONS ON HUSBAND'S NEW HIT-AND-RUN CHARGE

Pelosi paid $11,191.14 in restitution to the vehicle’s owner as part of the plea agreement, according to the district attorney’s office. He was also ordered to pay court fines and fees.

The July collision involved a parked Tesla, according to the criminal complaint previously reported by Fox News Digital. Pelosi was allegedly driving a burgundy Maserati convertible and left without attempting to identify the owner or leaving the information required under California law.

PELOSI STAFFER PUMPS THE BRAKES WHEN PRESSED ON HUSBAND'S HIT-AND-RUN: 'THAT'S ENOUGH'

Deputies later located Pelosi about a half-mile away. He allegedly told officers he had intended to return to the crash site.

Pelosi previously faced criminal charges over a different Napa County crash in 2022, when he pleaded guilty to misdemeanor DUI.

TIGER WOODS SET FOR PLEA CHANGE HEARING AFTER DUI ARREST FOLLOWING FLORIDA ROLLOVER CRASH

That conviction required him to attend a DUI education program and use an ignition interlock device. He was also sentenced to and ordered to pay restitution and fines.

His driving history also includes a 1957 crash in San Mateo County that killed his 19-year-old brother, The New York Times reported. Pelosi was behind the wheel, but a jury cleared him of wrongdoing.

More recently, Pelosi accumulated traffic infractions across four Bay Area counties, according to the Times. The outlet reported violations in Napa, San Mateo, Marin and San Francisco involving speeding, running a red light, driving against traffic on a one-way street and cellphone use without a hands-free device.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Prosecutors said the public attention surrounding Pelosi’s case prompted the announcement, noting that misdemeanor hit-and-run cases involving only property damage generally do not receive a news release.

Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

World.title: Teen previously convicted in shooting accused of killing pregnant mom of 4 inside Spirit Halloween
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A California teen released after a prior shooting arrest is now accused of gunning down a pregnant mother of four at a Spirit Halloween store, prompting prosecutors to push to try the 17-year-old as an adult.

Monte Smith was arrested Nov. 2 after the attack at Fairfield’s Solano Town Center left Constance Hages, 31, dead and six others wounded, according to Fairfield police.

The Solano County District Attorney’s Office has also charged him with two counts of murder and asked a judge to move his case to adult court.

CALIFORNIA GUNMAN REPEATEDLY RELEASED BEFORE DEADLY RAMPAGE, FIERY SHOOTOUT WITH DEPUTIES

Smith had already been arrested in another shooting before the deadly attack at Spirit Halloween, according to Fairfield police. That case involved gunfire in a local high school parking lot after school hours in 2025. He received a sentence and was later released, the department said.

"It’s time for change in California," Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall said, according to KTVU. "I don’t know how many more people have to die at the hands of youth. Hopefully we’ve had plenty enough."

MARYLAND MAN ACCUSED OF GIRL'S FATAL SHOOTING RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE

Prosecutors also pointed to Smith’s record in explaining why they want him kept in custody.

"Due to the seriousness of these crimes, the minor’s criminal record, and the threat to public safety, the people will argue that Smith remain detained," the DA’s office said.

TWO TEEN SUSPECTS HELD AFTER 5 FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN 'TARGETED MASS SHOOTING'

The filing also alleges a prior violent offense conviction, described as a strike, though the DA’s announcement did not specify the underlying offense.

Hages’ death has left four children without their mother, according to a GoFundMe organized by her aunt, Clanisha Morton. Police confirmed Hages was pregnant when she was killed.

"Constance was deeply loved, and her absence has created an overwhelming void in the lives of everyone who knew and cherished her," Morton wrote.

The family is raising money for funeral expenses and care for her children.

15-YEAR-OLD ACCUSED OF FIRING INTO CROWD DURING DEADLY SEATTLE MASS SHOOTING CLAIMS SELF-DEFENSE

The gunfire erupted around 8:30 p.m. Oct. 30, after Smith allegedly walked into the store and spotted another customer whom investigators believe he intended to target, police said.

He pulled out a gun and fired multiple rounds, striking that person and six others, according to police. Hages died at the scene.

Investigators have not identified the intended target or said what led to the shooting.

Smith fled within minutes, just as officers arrived, police said. As first responders treated the wounded, a school resource officer helped investigators identify the suspect.

The officer recognized Smith as a former student while reviewing surveillance video from the store and immediately alerted detectives, according to police. That recognition helped identify him within hours of the initial 911 call, and detectives ultimately located him at a residence in neighboring Suisun City.

Police initially withheld Smith’s name because of his age. The DA’s office later publicly identified him in its charging announcement.

CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATION SHOOTING KILLS TEEN, INJURES CHILD AND TWO OTHERS

The FBI also assisted with the investigation, confirming to Fox News Digital that its Evidence Response Team helped Fairfield police process a portion of the crime scene.

In addition to the two murder counts, Smith faces three counts of attempted murder, three counts of assault with a semiautomatic weapon and multiple gun enhancements, according to the DA’s office. Prosecutors also filed a multiple-murder special circumstance allegation.

The office announced that Smith’s arraignment and detention hearing was scheduled for Nov. 4 at 9 a.m. Its request to prosecute him as an adult requires a judge’s approval.

Police have not identified the school involved in the earlier shooting or said when Smith was released in that case.

In an update Saturday about the surviving victims, police said a 16-year-old boy, a 19-year-old man and a 32-year-old man were in critical condition, while a 23-year-old man was in critical but stable condition. Two other men, ages 19 and 43, had been treated for gunshot wounds and released.

The department’s arrest announcement did not provide updated conditions.

"Although an arrest has been made, our work is not over," Fairfield police said. "The criminal justice process will now move forward, and we remain committed to ensuring accountability for the lives impacted by this senseless act of violence."

Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact Fairfield police at 707-428-7600 or email 1030mall@fairfield.ca.gov.

World.title: Trump-backed Byron Donalds to make history as Florida’s first Black governor
World.content:

Rep. Byron Donalds just made history as the first Black politician to win a gubernatorial election in Florida as Fox News Decision Desk projected the congressman winning Tuesday's election.

He is also the first Black Republican in the nation's history elected governor.

Donalds, a three-term congressman from southwest Florida, defeated Democratic rival former Rep. David Jolly in a close race to win the Sunshine State's gubernatorial election, the Fox News Decision Desk projects.

With his victory, the top House ally of President Donald Trump and MAGA champion with a growing national profile will succeed term-limited GOP Gov. Ron DeSantis in steering the nation's third most populous state.

"I am humbled and grateful beyond measure," Donalds said in a victory statement posted to X. "As your Governor, I will give you everything I have. We are going to make life in Florida more affordable. We are going to keep our streets safe. We are going to invest in our young people so that they can attain the Florida Dream that all of us love so dearly. Florida is the envy of the nation. I will fight day and night to keep it that way and to lift our state to even greater heights."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Continuing and building upon DeSantis' conservative agenda was a key part of Donalds' campaign for governor.

Donalds was endorsed by Trump in February of last year, before he even formally launched his campaign for governor. Donalds declared his candidacy for governor during an appearance on Fox News' "Hannity."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Backed by Trump, Donalds won nearly half the vote in Florida's August GOP gubernatorial primary. He topped a crowded field of rivals that included Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner, and business executive James Fishback.

Donalds made headlines in late September when some references to Trump, whose approval ratings have continued to decline, were scrubbed from his campaign website.

A New York City native, Donalds moved to Florida to attend college. He worked in the finance, insurance, and banking fields before entering politics. A one-time Democrat, he became a Republican in 2010 amid the Tea Party movement. Donalds was elected to the Florida House in 2016, serving two terms before winning a seat in Congress.

Jolly, a Florida native who served as a top advisor to then-Rep. Bill Young, also worked as a lawyer and a lobbyist before winning a special congressional election in March of 2014. He won a full two-year term to the House later that year before losing re-election in 2016.

After leaving office he became a vocal Trump critic and a cable news political commentator. Jolly left the GOP in 2018 and became a Democrat last year before launching his gubernatorial campaign.

During their showdown for governor, Donalds showcased anti-socialism messaging, repeatedly claiming that Jolly embraced "radical socialism."

Firing back, Jolly told Fox News two weeks ago, "Byron Donalds is a liar. I've condemned socialism in the DSA [Democratic Socialists of America] hundreds of times, and he knows that."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Florida was once the largest of the general election battlegrounds, but the state has shifted to the right over the past decade. DeSantis won his 2022 re-election by nearly 20 points and Trump carried the state by 13 points in his 2024 White House re-election victory.

But despite Republicans enjoying a roughly 1.5 million registered voter advantage over the Democrats in the Sunshine State, Democrats are competitive again in Florida thanks to a rough political climate facing the GOP.

World.title: Ravens turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano after Lamar Jackson lands on IR, coach Jessie Minter says
World.content:
It’s time for rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano to take center stage. On Thursday night, the undrafted UConn product will go from simulating plays in his living room with his wife to making his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

First-year Baltimore Ravens coach Jessie Minter confirmed that Fagnano, who has spent most of the season as the team’s No. 3 quarterback, will start Thursday night. It is unclear whether Tyler Huntley will serve as his backup after the veteran quarterback sustained an injury in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

With his start in Week 9, Fagnano will become only the second undrafted rookie to start a regular-season game for the Ravens. "It's special," Fagnano said. "It's really the only way I can think about it."

Fagnano is moving to the top of Baltimore’s depth chart after Lamar Jackson’s return from a three-game absence was cut short by a thumb injury early in Sunday’s 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Jackson had missed those games because of a high left ankle sprain.

Fagnano has also dealt with injury concerns after stepping in for the injured Jackson and Huntley. He practiced with a brace on his right ankle on Tuesday. "Every game you got bumps and bruises," Fagnano said. "It's just football, a physical game we play. It feels good, though."

Fagnano earned one of the Ravens roster spots after he put together what was widely considered a strong preseason. The 25-year-old threw for 91 yards in his NFL debut.

Baltimore has dropped three consecutive games and enters Week 9 in the cellar of the AFC North.

World.title: Illinois teachers union boss Stacy Davis Gates gets major pay bump as state reading scores lag
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The president of the Illinois Federation of Teachers (IFT) received a reported $70,000 annual pay raise while many Illinois students continue to struggle with reading proficiency.

The IFT Executive Board approved a pay increase for IFT President Stacy Davis Gates, raising her compensation for that role from $180,000 to $250,000 annually, according to an Oct. 29 report from NBC Chicago.

The state-level raise comes on top of her existing salary as president of the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU), where public records show she earned just under $195,000, based on that figure and her newly reported IFT salary, her combined annual pay would total approximately $445,000.

HOUSE GOP LAUNCHES PROBE INTO 5 MAJOR LABOR UNIONS OVER DEM SPENDING DESPITE MAGA MEMBERSHIP BASE

The nearly 39% pay increase drew criticism from the Illinois Policy Institute, a free-market think tank.

"The Chicago Teachers Union spends more money running itself than it does representing teachers. According to its own reporting, less than 19% of CTU’s spending went toward representation," Mailee Smith, vice president of policy and litigation at the Illinois Policy Institute, told Fox News Digital.

"Davis Gates’ raise reflects the same misplaced priorities seeping into the Illinois Federation of Teachers: more dues money going toward leadership compensation instead of serving members," she continued.

Smith also criticized the disparity between Davis Gates' reported compensation and the salaries of classroom teachers.

"Teachers look for support in their classrooms and representation at the bargaining table," Smith added. "A nearly 39% raise for a leader does not help with either of those, especially when the average Illinois teacher only makes a fraction of Davis Gates’ total combined annual salary of $445,000."

Neither Davis Gates, the CTU nor the IFT responded to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

The compensation boost comes as Illinois schools face questions about student reading and math proficiency.

According to 2024 results from the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) — often referred to as the Nation's Report Card — only 30% of Illinois fourth graders scored at or above the proficient level in reading. Among eighth graders, 33% scored at or above that benchmark.

Chicago Public Schools' results also show significant proficiency gaps.

In Chicago, 23% of fourth graders performed at or above the NAEP Proficient level in reading in 2024. Meanwhile, 60% of fourth graders scored at or above the NAEP Basic level in math, a slight increase from 59% in 2022 and up from 50% in 2003.

The Illinois Policy Institute reported that 46% of Chicago Public Schools (CPS) students in grades three through eight met reading proficiency standards during the 2025-26 school year, according to data from the 2026 Illinois Report Card. Among CPS 11th graders taking the ACT, 44% scored proficient in reading and 28% in math, the institute reported.

COREY BROOKS: CHICAGO SCHOOLS ARE FAILING KIDS AT THE ONE SKILL THAT CAN CHANGE THEIR LIVES

The CTU has also drawn criticism over its political and social activism. The Washington Post editorial board previously criticized the union's emphasis on progressive social justice initiatives as Chicago students struggled with reading and math proficiency. Internal union documents previously reported by Fox News Digital also showed spending on progressive political causes.

Smith said Illinois state and local leaders should prioritize classroom needs.

"Illinois needs to put students and teachers first, while current leadership seems more focused on radical agendas and elevating their leaders," Smith told Fox News Digital.

"It also follows a record of double standards: Davis Gates has demanded others pay their ‘fair share,’ but let her own utility bills pile up," Smith continued. "She chose private school for her own child while opposing scholarships for low-income families. Now she’s receiving a large raise right after local teachers rejected a dues hike to protect their paychecks."

World.title: Spencer Pratt says $1,200 hotel 'fortress' was cheaper than security as death threats mounted
World.content:

Spencer Pratt explained why his controversial stay at the Hotel Bel-Air was actually the cheaper option as he faced death threats while running for mayor of Los Angeles.

The 43-year-old reality star faced scrutiny in May after TMZ reported he had been staying at the luxury hotel despite appearing to suggest in a campaign ad that he was living in an Airstream trailer on the site of his California home, which was destroyed in the devastating Pacific Palisades fire.

At the time, the outlet reported that Pratt had been staying at the Hotel Bel-Air for more than a month, though "The Hills" alum disputed that characterization, saying he had spent no more than six days there during the previous month.

SPENCER PRATT’S MAYORAL RUN BACKED BY PARIS HILTON, KRISTIN CAVALLARI AS CELEBRITY DIVIDE DEEPENS

In a lengthy X post he shared Tuesday, Pratt, who lost in the June primary election, defended his choice to stay at the pricey hotel during the race.

"Why is he spending $1,200 a night? Why couldn’t he stay somewhere for $300 a night? Well, the answer to that question is not as pretty as any of us may like to hear," Pratt wrote.

REALITY TV STAR SPENCER PRATT GAINS TRACTION IN LOS ANGELES MAYORAL RACE AFTER FIERY DEBATE

"Most people simply presumed that I was being a bougie spoiled brat, and that I was abusing campaign funds," he continued. "They expected me to stay at a cheaper hotel, but what they don’t realize is … the Hotel Bel Air was the cheapest hotel in all of LA.

"At the time, I couldn’t explain the math to people, and my campaign staff told me I wasn’t allowed to divulge the real reason I had to stay there, but now that the election is coming to a close, I don’t need to listen to anyone anymore."

'ENTOURAGE' CREATOR BACKS SPENCER PRATT FOR LA MAYOR, SAYS CITY 'HAS COLLAPSED' UNDER CURRENT LEADERSHIP

Pratt had previously told TMZ in May that the Airstream had become unsafe, saying that the Bel Air Hotel's "armed security" made it "the only option." He claimed that supporters of his opponents, Mayor Karen Bass and City Councilmember Nithya Raman were "getting increasingly desperate and hostile" due to his performance at the May debate and strong polling numbers.

"I can't talk about specific threats, but that lot is ... unsafe now," he said at the time.

JIMMY KIMMEL ATTACKS FIRE VICTIM SPENCER PRATT AS 'SCREAMING JERK,' LECTURES LA VOTERS ABOUT MAYORAL ELECTION

In his X post, Pratt, who ran as a Republican, elaborated on the threats that he received, which he attributed to political violence.

"Throughout the campaign, I endured numerous death threats, to the point where I had to hire full-time security," he wrote. "Anyone who’s had to hire security knows that they will always tell you to not discuss your death threats; they find that it often has the opposite effect you would expect; normal people should hear it and think ‘whoa, we need to dial back the temperature, this isn’t acceptable’, but the reality is that commie street animals get inspired, and you will end up getting copycats if you advertise your threats."

SPENCER PRATT VOWS TO LEAVE LA AND FIND 'LAST AMERICAN DREAM' IN ANOTHER CITY IF MAYORAL BID FAILS

Pratt went on to detail specific incidents he said led him to fear for his safety and that of his family.

"People were breaking into my lot in the Palisades and leaving notes on the airstream with white powder in them," he wrote.

DEM MAYOR FACES REALITY CHECK AFTER ACCUSING RIVAL OF 'EXPLOITING' PALISADES FIRE: 'ABSOLUTE TONE DEAFNESS'

The TV personality also claimed that a "lunatic" who was "hellbent on tracking me down" charged at his young son while he was boogie-boarding in the ocean. Pratt shares sons Gunner, 8, and Ryker, 3, with his wife and former "The Hills" co-star Heidi Montag, 40.

"So, I had to hire a second security detail for my family while I was away campaigning," he wrote. "I don’t know if you’ve ever had to hire 4-5 armed security professionals with blacked out SUVs, but…it’s not cheap. One of the first things they told me was that my lot in the Palisades was a security nightmare; perched mid-slope on a hill, totally exposed in a bowl, surrounded by elevated positions where a shooter could easily traipse through the wilderness of the State Park, and have a clear line of sight to every inch of my property.

SPENCER PRATT: LOS ANGELES ANGRY WITH KAREN BASS’ MISMANAGEMENT

"I wasn’t allowed to stay on that property, even if I wanted to," he added. "Enter the Hotel Bel Air."

Pratt explained that the famed LA hotel, which has hosted celebrities, presidents and royalty, is an unusually secure property due to its design.

PRATT CONCEDES LA MAYOR RACE WITH SCATHING VIDEO TEASING NEXT MOVE, BOMBSHELL INFO HE HOLDS: 'COMMIE ANIMALS'

"While $1,200 a night isn’t very unique for a decent hotel in a major city, there’s something else about the hotel that is unique," Pratt wrote.

"Unlike my turkey shoot of a lot in the Palisades, the Hotel Bel Air is surrounded with a fortress wall, with a single point of ingress, a fatal funnel that takes you over a moat, just to enter the property. You then must navigate a labyrinth of walled off bungalows, and it is very easy to get lost. Unlike normal hotels, it is a very secure facility.

"When my security team dropped me off behind the walls of the Bel Air, they felt good about leaving me alone in the secure facility," he continued.

"Had I stayed anywhere else, I would have needed to book out 3 rooms for my team to maintain overnight security, which would’ve cost an additional $3,000 per night. Paradoxically, by this calculation, I was actually saving a ton of money by staying at the secure Bel Air; even staying at a Motel 6 would’ve cost me more money, and in a campaign…money is everything."

Pratt claimed that threats of political violence disproportionately affect Republican candidates, arguing that the cost of protecting himself forced his campaign to spend money on security that his Democratic rivals could devote elsewhere. The reality star recalled that Raman appeared at a debate preparation event without visible security while he was accompanied by several armed officers.

"We have an epidemic of left wing violence that puts republicans at a permanent fundraising disadvantage," he wrote. "I knew that I needed armed security, and even though it severely crippled our campaign by siphoning off an insane amount of our fundraising dollars, we had to do it, because we knew that nobody else was going to protect us."

Pratt said that while his campaign has ended, the security concerns that prompted him to hire armed protection have continued.
