Part of the Florida Panhandle — more than 3,200 kilometres away — observes central standard time during the winter, which is also UTC-6.

A map of the current time zones across Canada and the U.S. during the winter months. Most of Western Canada did not roll back its clocks on Nov. 1, resulting in many time quirks. (Darius Mahdavi/CBC)

British Columbians woke up on Sunday having not changed their clocks for the first time in decades, and most of B.C. will have to get used to being one hour ahead of Washington state to the south and two hours behind Ontario and much of Quebec this winter.

"All of Eastern Canada, for the most part, besides a small portion of Ontario, did turn back their clocks," said Darius Mahdavi, CBC's science and climate specialist.

"So maybe you woke up and your phone had the wrong time on it because it did fall back when it shouldn't have, maybe your phone and your computer disagreed about what time it was."

Those aren't the only quirks that will result from B.C.'s decision not to roll back its clocks last weekend.

Alaska communities will have to adjust to being two hours behind B.C., observing a UTC-9 standard during the winter, despite sharing a large land border.

Meanwhile, residents of Point Roberts, Wash. — a U.S. pene-exclave of Washington state at the southern tip of the Tsawwassen Peninsula, completely cut off by land from the rest of the country — will see their time zones shift by an hour when they cross the border to attend school or access services in Blaine, Wash.

Most of B.C. has now moved to daylight time year-round, a permanent UTC-7 time standard called Pacific time (PT).

The decision to stick with daylight time year-round has prompted criticism from scientists, who said sticking with standard time would have been better for population health overall.

World.title: P.E.I. Premier Rob Lantz facing pressure to step down
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

On the opening day of the P.E.I. legislative session, Lantz faced criticism over the state of the province under his leadership, while some in his own party revealed their petition for a review of his leadership. CBC reporters Steve Bruce and Wayne Thibodeau with that story.

A formal petition signed by some members of the P.E.I. Progressive Conservative Party is calling for a vote on Premier Rob Lantz's leadership.

Lantz secured his position as party leader and premier following a leadership contest win in February over Mark Ledwell with 53.1 per cent of the vote.

Martie Murphy, a longtime member of the party, said the petition is currently signed by more than 120 members. She said some in the party have become discouraged.

"We feel like doing nothing is political demise because we're not going to climb up in the polls with the leadership the way that it is," she said.

"It's really everybody. It's a combination of rural, city. So it's everybody that has a concern where the Island sits right now. The leadership is in question. They have lost the confidence from Islanders and party members."

PC Party member Martie Murphy says the petition is currently signed by more than 120 party members. She says some in the party have become discouraged. (Steve Bruce/CBC)

The petition and resolution, sent to the party association, is asking for a special general meeting for voting on the issue to be held within the next 15 days.

Lantz would have an opportunity to speak at the meeting, and members would vote by secret ballot on whether they want him to step down. Then, it would be up to Lantz to decide next steps.

'Weak public support'

The resolution notes concerns regarding financial responsibility as well as transparency and accountability, pointing to the province's "rapidly escalating and unsustainable deficit," and says there are "significant questions about the current leadership and its ability to responsibly manage the Province's financial affairs."

It goes on to state that the PC Party "continues to experience historically weak public support, with no meaningful improvement reflected in consecutive polls, demonstrating a growing loss of confidence not only among party members but across the electorate, placing the party's future electoral viability and its ability to form government at serious risk."

Lantz said he is aware the party has received the petition and he will "let the party work through that."

He added the party has more than 7,200 members and that, under its constitution, it takes 75 signatures to compel a leadership vote.

"That's a pretty low bar. But in the meantime, I'm just focused on the work of government and the priorities of Islanders," he said.

"Yes, this is a distraction, but I'm focused on the work that I was elected to do."

P.E.I. Premier Rob Lantz says he feels there is 'a small number of people' who never accepted the results of the leadership convention earlier this year. (Rick Gibbs/CBC)

Lantz said he feels there is "a small number of people" who never accepted the results of the leadership convention and they are "trying to compel a discussion."

"It appears to me they just want to roll back the clock to reverse a democratic decision that was made by this party, but it is what it is," he said.

"We'll go through this process, but then people are going to have to move on and focus on working for Islanders."

PC Party president Robert Larsen confirmed via email the party received a petition requesting a special general meeting but did not say when such a meeting may happen or if a vote on Lantz's leadership would occur.

He said the party is consulting legal counsel on what is now required under the party constitution.

Questions regarding Lantz's leadership were brought up in the legislature during question period Tuesday, with Liberal Opposition Leader Hal Perry stating the province is facing "many serious challenges," adding "it is so sad that the source of many of these difficulties is the provincial government."

Liberal Opposition Leader Hal Perry said during question period that the province is facing 'many serious challenges' and pointed to the government as the source. (P.E.I. Legislative Assembly)

"Rather than leading with a clear vision and plan, this government stumbles from one mistake to another. Instead of substance, it's photo-ops and Facebook rather than policy and pocketbooks," Perry said.

"This province has not had the opportunity to endorse this premier or his plans and yet this premier is making incredibly long-term and potentially damaging decisions."

Lantz responded to Perry that Islanders elected the Progressive Conservative government "with a strong majority" and that it is "delivering on that mandate every day."

"Islanders want us focused on access to care, on the price at the pump, protecting jobs from tariffs, and that's what we're doing," Lantz said.

"They don't want us focused on an election right now. We're delivering on a mandate that we were given and that's what we'll continue to do."

World.title: Prime Minister says Russia will not be allowed to compete at 2026 world juniors in Alberta
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Prime Minister Mark Carney says Russia will not be allowed to compete at next month's world junior hockey championship in Alberta.

Carney, speaking in Antigua at the Commonwealth Summit, said Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be permitted to represent their countries in Canada as long as the war in Ukraine continues.

"While Russia and Belorussia [sic] are supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Carney said when asked if Russian players would be denied visas.

"So if you're asking specifically about the world juniors, the Russians will not be there."

His comments come after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled Friday that Russia must be reinstated to international hockey competition, starting with the world junior tournament.

WATCH | Prime Minister shuts down Russian involvement in 2026 world juniors: Carney says Russia won't be allowed to play in upcoming world juniors | Duration closed caption 0:55 Prime Minister Mark Carney said while Russia and Belarus are supporting 'this illegal and unjustified war in Ukraine,' no athlete representing either country will be allowed to compete in Canada, including at this winter's World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta.

Later, a joint statement was released by ministers Anita Anand (Foreign Affairs), Lena Diab (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship) and Adam van Koeverden (Secretary of State for Sport) saying Canada's position has not changed because Russia's actions haven't.

“As a leading host of international sporting events, Canada remains committed to ensuring that sport is not used to confer legitimacy, prestige or international standing on such states, particularly against the risk that Russian and Belarusian participation in international sporting events becomes more normalised," a portion of the statement read.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith previously said the province would comply with the CAS ruling, but following the Prime Minister's announcement she spoke in favour of the federal government's stance in a post on X.

"I agree with this decision completely. The people of Ukraine have suffered immeasurably from Vladimir Putin’s illegal war. Alberta is now home to 70k Ukrainian evacuees who remain unable to return home because of Russia’s invasion of their country. We in Alberta stand with them," Smith wrote.

Several European hockey federations, including Sweden, Finland, Czech Republic and Latvia, have said their teams will refuse to face Russia.

"We respect the decisions of the Finns, the Czechs, the Swedes, other nations, but this is a decision we take on our own," Carney said.

Hockey Canada says it has been consulting with the International Ice Hockey Federation and other stakeholders about the potential impact on the tournament.

The world juniors begin Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer.

European federations add weight to boycott

The Swedish hockey federation said its board decided Tuesday that it would not play against Russia but would still play other games. That was a turnaround from last week, after Sweden initially indicated a boycott was off the table following the CAS ruling.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," federation head Anders Larsson said in a statement, using the team's nickname.

Germany is scheduled to host next year's men's world championship in May, but the chief executive of the country's hockey federation previously said it could pull out over concerns about costs and security.

WATCH | Russia's international hockey ban lifted by Court of Arbitration for Sport: Russia is back in the hockey world champions | Hanomansing Live | Duration closed caption 6:59 Russia had been banned from international ice hockey competitions since 2022 following the invasion of Ukraine. The Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned International Ice Hockey Federation decisions, which excluded Russia from events in the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships. It is unclear how Russia will be included since adding another team will make for uneven groups and longer tournaments.

The Swedish statement came shortly after Norway announced its boycott.

"Our position is that Russia should be excluded from all international championships as long as the war in Ukraine continues and remains unchanged," the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said in a statement. "At the same time, this decision is based on our responsibility to protect the safety and wellbeing of our players, team staff and their families. We believe that playing Russia under the current circumstances could expose our players and team staff to significant security risks. Our priority is therefore their mental health, wellbeing and personal safety."

Norway referred only to the men's world championship in its statement. General secretary Petter Salsten told the AP that, in the case of the world juniors, Norway would potentially be removed from the tournament by the IIHF to make way for Russia. In that case, "if RUS is added, it is a huge possibility that NOR is out," he wrote via email, because Norway was the last team to qualify.

The chairman of Denmark's hockey federation told the Ritzau news agency its teams would not play against Russia. Latvia's federation said it "reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

The Austrian federation told the AP in an emailed statement: "We stand behind the decision of Finland and Norway and are currently looking into whether the European nations will join a boycott together. We are therefore not ruling out a boycott and are still coordinating with the authorities on this."

Finland is the defending men's world champion and Norway was the bronze-medal winner this year.

The growing boycott is similar to the situation in soccer in 2022, shortly after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. On that occasion, all of Russia's potential World Cup qualifying opponents threatened to boycott. FIFA successfully argued at CAS for excluding Russia on the grounds that not doing so risked "irreparable and chaotic" harm to the competition.

Second major sponsor pressures IIHF

Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian Tyres said it will no longer sponsor the world championship if Russia takes part.

Tiina Frazer, senior vice-president for brand, marketing and communications, said that "under the current circumstances, continuing the sponsorship if Russia participates would not be aligned with our values."

Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, a tournament sponsor since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown if Russia plays.

Junior tournaments are affected too, with the Finnish city of Turku saying it will not co-host next year's world juniors if Russia participates.

The Czech federation is hosting the women's under-18 world championship in January and said Tuesday it would speak with the government about whether Russian players would be denied entry to the country.

One political figure in support of Russia's return is Slovakia's pro-Russian Prime Minister Robert Fico.

"I've also always wondered what the value of a gold medal is, if on the way to it you don't have to beat the Russian hockey players, who are undoubtedly among the best in the world," he posted on social media Saturday.

The women's world championship starting in Denmark this week is not affected by the CAS ruling and is going ahead without Russia.

World.title: Colombia’s government presents “Economic Rescue Bill”
World.content:
Colombia’s Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo on Thursday presented an Economic Rescue Bill that seeks to reduce government spending and increase its revenue.

The bill grants extraordinary powers to President Abelardo de la Espriella to slash government spending by decree and includes a tax reform that includes higher sales tax rates on gasoline, coffee, cigarettes and vegetables.

The bill also includes tax breaks for corporations in an attempt to increase investment.

Abelardo’s extraordinary powers

While on campaign, De la Espriella powers vowed a 40% reduction of the State, which the bill falls short of doing.

Article 7 of the bill does grant the president extraordinary powers to “abolish, merge, and split ministries and administrative departments, as well as to determine or modify their names, objectives, and organizational structure,” and allows De la Espriella to “abolish, merge, split, and change the legal status” of other State bodies like the superintendencies, agencies, special administrative units, and public institutions.

Article 96 allows the government to change the personnel hiring of tax agency DIAN, which “would allow for the elimination of annual competitive exams for entry into the DIAN and a return to the practice of appointing thousands of officials,” according to former DIAN director Luis Carlos Reyes.

Last but not least, the bill mandates a 20% reduction in salaries of State employees, excluding the security forces, and cut half of the costs in temporary contracts.

VAT reforms and squeezing the middle class

The bill seeks to remove popular products like cocoa, coffee, sugar and fruits from a VAT exemption list and introduce a 19% sales tac on them.

An increase in taxes on gasoline will inflate its price.

The bill additionally seeks to charge VAT on vice products like liquor and cigarettes, which would make them up to 53% more expensive.

The bulk of these tax increases wouldn’t take fore until after the November 2027 local and regional elections in an apparent compromise to Congress and Colombia’s political forces.

In an attempt to not impoverish the poor, the bill seeks a mechanism that would refund up to 100% of IVA payments to some 19 million of the country’s poorest citizens.

The increased pressure on the middle class has already resulted in opposition from within De la Espriella’s congressional coalition.

Tax benefits for the capitalists

The government seeks to gradually lower the corporate income tax from 35% to 31% and offer a reduced tax rate for large companies that decide to invest in new enterprises.

According to the Inter-American Development Bank, a similar scheme introduced by former President Alvaro Uribe “was ineffective in promoting investment.”

World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: De la Espriella sacks interior minister after Congress bungles Colombia’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara hours after Congress found a procedural flaw in the passed 2027 budget, which makes the law invalid.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella briefly thanked Lara and announced he would be replaced by the ambassador to the Organization of American States, Alejandro Ordoñez.

The news surprised the interior minister, who suddenly left a congressional debate on a law to facilitate the demobilization of illegal armed groups after receiving a message on his phone.

Lara was apparently held responsible for the blunder of Congress, whose two houses approved the 2027 budget but with conflicting versions of an article on financial risk-coverage mechanisms for the Ministry of Finance.

By the time the error was detected, the budget debate had passed its October 20 deadline, forcing De la Espriella to issue a decree that would convert an older version of the budget bill into law.

The interior minister was the administration’s primary political liaison responsible for managing legislative procedure and whip operations in Congress.

Lara’s job was already under pressure after he failed to convince Congress to cede its presidency to the president’s candidate.

While Ordoñez returns from Washington, Justice Minister Ivan Cancino will assume the role of interior minister.

The incoming interior minister is an ultra conservative Catholic with ties to the Society of St. Pius X, which considers the modernizing reforms of the Catholic Church heresies and errors, and was declared in a schism with the church in June.

In Colombian politics and particularly among the opposition, Ordoñez is mainly remembered as the inspector general who illegally removed former President Gustavo Petro from his post as mayor of Bogota in 2013.

Petro was ultimately reinstated and would become president of the country in 2022.

World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Cristina Kirchner meets Lula’s digital strategist in a bid to replicate his comeback in Argentina
World.content:
Cristina Kirchner meets Lula’s digital strategist in a bid to replicate his comeback in Argentina

3rd Tuesday, November 2026 - 20:16 UTC Full article

Kirchner, who is serving a final six-year sentence for corruption under house arrest and is barred for life from public office

Former Argentine president Cristina Kirchner on Monday received Brazilian lawmaker André Janones, creator of the WhatsApp channel that helped Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win re-election, in Buenos Aires, as the Peronist opposition looks to Brazil for keys to defeating Javier Milei in the 2027 presidential election.

Janones, a federal deputy for the state of Minas Gerais, runs “Lula’s Army”, a WhatsApp channel with more than 10.4 million followers to whom he sends daily instructions to share and amplify content on social media, a strategy credited with part of Lula’s comeback against Flávio Bolsonaro on October 25. On the day of the Brazilian election, the Peronists launched their own “Peronism’s Army”, which had passed 80,000 followers after Janones’ visit.

Kirchner, who is serving a final six-year sentence for corruption under house arrest and is barred for life from public office, posed with Janones in a photo he shared on social media with the message: “Beside Cristina Kirchner to tell the world that yes, we can defeat the far right.” Lula’s channel was told to share the post, which drew more than 60,000 interactions within an hour. Janones also met Sergio Massa, the Peronists’ last presidential candidate, but not Buenos Aires province governor Axel Kicillof.

The visit came amid an internal Peronist struggle over the 2027 presidential candidacy, in which Kicillof, backed by several governors and mayors, faces the Kirchner and Massa camp. The former president, who hopes to overturn her conviction before international courts, said in an interview with The Washington Post published on Monday that she could run again: “When I recover my political rights, why not?”

Janones, re-elected as a deputy in October, has ruled out a ministerial post in Lula’s new government and returns to Brazil on Tuesday. His team denied he plans to work on the campaign of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez ahead of the November 29 general election.

World.title: The Pope arrives in an Argentina where bishops are among Milei’s firmest critics
World.content:
The Pope arrives in an Argentina where bishops are among Milei’s firmest critics

3rd Tuesday, November 2026 - 09:29 UTC Full article

Leo XIV has placed social justice at the heart of his pontificate, while Milei has called it “an aberration”

Pope Leo XIV will arrive in Buenos Aires on Sunday on a visit that Javier Milei’s government presents as strictly pastoral, but which takes place amid tension with Argentina’s Catholic hierarchy, one of the most critical voices against the president’s austerity policies. The pontiff will begin a tour in Uruguay on Friday that will continue in Argentina from November 8 to 11 and end in Peru.

“The Pope belongs to all Argentines, not to a political party or a political colour,” presidential chief of staff Karina Milei, who led negotiations with the Church and the Vatican, has repeatedly said. The secretary of worship, Agustín Caulo, insisted it is “an apostolic tour” and that “this should not be politicised”. Authorities expect some 7 million people to follow the Pope in Buenos Aires, Claypole, Luján and Córdoba, in what Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva described as “the largest operation in our history”.

The underlying differences are well known. Leo XIV has placed social justice at the heart of his pontificate, while Milei has called it “an aberration”. A study by sociologist Sol Prieto of the National Scientific and Technical Research Council (Conicet) of documents published by the Argentine Bishops’ Conference between January 2024 and September 2026 found that 42 of the 44 referring to public policy, or 95%, take “a critical position”, on issues such as the social situation, the environment, institutional quality, the lowering of the age of criminal responsibility and a decree curbing migrants’ rights.

Ten days ago, when Milei questioned the idea that many people cannot make ends meet, the president of the Bishops’ Conference, Marcelo Colombo, replied: “That people cannot make ends meet is a fact of reality, not something that needs to be proven.” The Archbishop of Buenos Aires, Jorge García Cuerva, said the Pope “will find a wounded Argentina”. “There is no affinity, but a very strong aversion between most Argentine bishops and Milei’s government,” said researcher Fortunato Mallimaci, who identifies opposition to abortion as one of the few points of agreement.

According to El País, the government sought to limit mass gatherings but the Vatican’s position prevailed, and the Pope will celebrate open-air Masses. Two events are particularly uncomfortable for the government, according to the newspaper: the meeting with trade unionists, business leaders and social movements at the Catholic University of Argentina and the visit to the Pequeño Cottolengo Don Orione, a home for people with disabilities, one of the sectors hardest hit by spending cuts. The place of Vice President Victoria Villarruel, estranged from Milei, at official events also remains undecided.

World.title: Ayuso honours Kast in Madrid on the eve of the Ibero-American Summit: “We defend the same things”
World.content:
Ayuso honours Kast in Madrid on the eve of the Ibero-American Summit: “We defend the same things”

3rd Tuesday, November 2026 - 09:18 UTC Full article

Kast, on his first European tour since taking office in March, replied that Madrid “is one of the most open, free and prosperous regions in Europe” and stressed security, the focus of his government

The president of the Madrid regional government, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, on Monday awarded the region’s International Medal to Chilean President José Antonio Kast, who is in the Spanish capital for the 30th Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government. “On both sides of the Atlantic we defend the same things,” Ayuso said at the ceremony.

“We are free nations and we defend our governments and liberal democracies and the rule of law, which will not yield to authoritarianism,” said the People’s Party leader, who contrasted Chile with Cuba, Nicaragua and Venezuela. Ayuso praised Chile as “an example of what a nation can achieve when it trusts its citizens” and highlighted Kast’s “commitment to freedom, security, prosperity and the defence of institutions”. “We do not want citizens dependent on power; we want them to be masters of their own lives,” she added.

Kast, on his first European tour since taking office in March, replied that Madrid “is one of the most open, free and prosperous regions in Europe” and stressed security, the focus of his government. “It is the first duty of the state. And when the state fails in that duty, the most vulnerable pay. Without security there is no order, without order there is no peace and without peace there is no freedom.”

The Community of Madrid’s International Medal, created in 2017 and purely honorary, is awarded on the regional president’s personal initiative. Previous recipients include Argentine President Javier Milei and Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa; Venezuelan opposition leaders Juan Guaidó and Edmundo González; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky; Pope Leo XIV; and the United States, for the 250th anniversary of its independence. Manuela Bergerot, spokeswoman for Más Madrid in the regional assembly, accused Ayuso of turning the award into “the membership card of her far-right international”. A group of demonstrators protested outside the regional government headquarters.

Kast began the day with a private meeting with Vox leader Santiago Abascal, with whom he has close ties, and plans to meet Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez during the summit, which brings together the countries of Latin America with Spain, Portugal and Andorra.

World.title: Corruption joins the cost of living as a top concern for US voters
World.content:
Corruption joins the cost of living as a top concern for US voters

3rd Tuesday, November 2026 - 00:31 UTC Full article

A Fox News poll published in October found that 88% of voters say they are “extremely” or “very” concerned about corruption in government

The United States votes on Tuesday in midterm elections in which corruption has emerged in the final stretch as one of voters’ main concerns, second only to the cost of living, according to several polls. At stake are all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats and numerous governorships and state legislatures.

A Fox News poll published in October found that 88% of voters say they are “extremely” or “very” concerned about corruption in government. Another survey, by Harris for Britain’s The Guardian, found that nine in ten Americans consider it a problem and that 76% believe public officials care more about enriching themselves than improving people’s lives. According to that study, only the cost of living weighs more heavily than corruption in voting decisions, ahead of immigration and healthcare.

“Just six months ago, corruption was not a top issue for voters. A few days out from the midterms, it has absolutely become one of the issues,” pollster Frank Luntz said. The Brennan Center for Justice estimates that references to government ethics in campaign ads have reached their highest level in 14 years: about 24% in House races and 16% in Senate races.

Democratic candidates have focused their criticism on the business dealings of President Donald Trump and his family, particularly in cryptocurrencies, and on private donations of more than US$300 million for the ballroom being built at the White House, including US$25 million each from Apple and Nvidia. Ethics allegations also extend to candidates from both parties: Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, the Democratic Senate candidate in Minnesota over alleged welfare fraud, and the campaign of Democrat Mary Peltola in Alaska, under investigation for allegedly promoting a candidate with the same surname as her rival.

More than 51 million people have already voted early, 25% more than in the 2022 midterms. Polls favour the Democrats, who need four more seats to control the House and at least four more to take the Senate, with close races in Michigan, Alaska, Maine, Iowa, Ohio, Kansas and Texas. Trump closed his campaign on Sunday with rallies in Iowa and Kansas.

World.title: Falklands representative in London honours the Islands’ fallen at Westminster
World.content:
Falklands representative in London honours the Islands’ fallen at Westminster

3rd Tuesday, November 2026 - 00:08 UTC Full article

Falkland Islands Government Representative, Richard Hyslop, placing a commemorative cross at the House of Commons Garden of Remembrance

The Falkland Islands Government Representative to the UK and Europe, Richard Hyslop, has placed a commemorative cross at the House of Commons Garden of Remembrance in London in memory of Falkland Islanders killed in both world wars and those who lost their lives in 1982.

The cross commemorates the 22 Islanders killed in the First World War, the 25 killed in the Second World War, and the 255 British Armed Forces personnel and three Islanders killed in the Falklands War, according to a statement from the Falkland Islands Government Office in London.

The Garden of Remembrance, installed each year in New Palace Yard outside the Palace of Westminster, was started in November 2021 by the Speaker of the House of Commons, Sir Lindsay Hoyle, in partnership with the Royal British Legion. It allows parliamentarians and representatives of Commonwealth countries and UK Overseas Territories to plant memorial crosses honouring Armed Forces personnel.

“I was honoured to place a commemorative cross in the House of Commons Gardens of Remembrance in memory of those Islanders killed in both World Wars and those killed in the liberation of the Islands in 1982,” Hyslop said. “We must remember the service and sacrifice of those individuals who gave so much to protect the freedoms we enjoy today, we will remember them.”

World.title: An Oxford professor to sit as the UK's chosen judge in the Falklands dispute in Hamburg
World.content:
An Oxford professor to sit as the UK's chosen judge in the Falklands dispute in Hamburg

2nd Monday, November 2026 - 15:23 UTC Full article

British jurist Vaughan Lowe, emeritus professor of public international law at the University of Oxford, will be the judge ad hoc chosen by the United Kingdom in the case between Argentina and London before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea over hydrocarbon exploitation north of the Falklands. Lowe will make his solemn declaration on Monday, November 9, the day before the hearing.

According to a statement from the Hamburg-based tribunal, the public sitting will be held at 10 a.m. in the main courtroom, where Lowe will make the declaration required under article 9 of its Rules. The tribunal's Statute allows a party that has no judge of its nationality among its members to choose one for a specific case. Lowe, who held the Chichele Professorship of Public International Law at Oxford, is one of Britain's most prominent experts on the law of the sea.

The hearing on provisional measures in the case officially named the Case concerning hydrocarbon exploitation in the South-West Atlantic Ocean (Argentina v. United Kingdom) will take place on November 10 and 11. Argentina requested four measures on October 13, including that the United Kingdom prevent exploitation of the Sea Lion field and refrain from granting new permits. London has said it will take part and challenge any attempt to use the proceedings to settle sovereignty. The sittings will be public and broadcast live on the tribunal's website.

World.title: Argentina’s Sea Lion case could founder on Falklands sovereignty, a legal expert warns
World.content:
Argentina’s Sea Lion case could founder on Falklands sovereignty, a legal expert warns

2nd Monday, November 2026 - 00:57 UTC Full article

The expert believes Argentina will pursue every legal, diplomatic and political avenue to block the project, and suggests that Milei may also be seeking to stir national pride ahead of the elections

Argentina’s case against the United Kingdom over the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands “could fall at the first hurdle”: the jurisdiction of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, which cannot settle territorial sovereignty disputes, according to Australian law of the sea expert Donald R. Rothwell. The tribunal will hold hearings on Argentina’s request on November 10 and 11 in Hamburg.

In an analysis published by The Interpreter, the Lowy Institute’s publication, Rothwell, professor of international law at the Australian National University, notes that under Article 286 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea the tribunal is only competent to settle disputes “concerning the interpretation or application” of the treaty. Territorial disputes have traditionally fallen to the International Court of Justice.

The problem, he argues, is that Argentina’s case cannot be separated from the underlying question. “If the UK has sovereignty over the islands, then Sea Lion is a legitimate act of exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf. If the Argentine claim over the islands is valid, then the UK’s conduct is in breach of UNCLOS,” he writes. Argentina alleges that the UK is illegally exploiting the continental shelf, that the project will cause environmental damage and that issuing licences aggravates the dispute over the maritime areas. “Absent the underlying territorial dispute, these would all be legitimate issues for ITLOS determination,” the expert says.

Rothwell compares the case with the 2016 South China Sea arbitration, in which the Philippines “neatly sidestepped” the question of sovereignty over disputed features and focused on China’s maritime claims, so there was never a need to determine who owned what. That, he warns, will not be possible in the case of the South Atlantic islands. Even so, he acknowledges that the tribunal “has generally been reluctant to take a narrow view of its jurisdiction” and recalls that, in the maritime boundary dispute between Mauritius and the Maldives around the Chagos Archipelago, it reached a full determination even though sovereignty between Mauritius and the UK was not fully resolved at the time.

The legal expert believes Argentina will pursue every legal, diplomatic and political avenue to block the project, and suggests that President Javier Milei may also be seeking to stir national pride ahead of the 2027 elections. He adds that US President Donald Trump could intervene, unhappy at the limited British support over Iran; Washington officially remains neutral in the dispute, although Trump has said that position is “under review”. “London will inevitably robustly defend its position on all fronts,” Rothwell predicts, adding that if the case proceeds it will be historic: the first time any aspect of the dispute has gone before an international court.

Sea Lion, operated by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration, lies about 200 kilometres north of the archipelago. Argentina bases its claim on succession to Spanish rights and on its occupation of the islands between 1820 and 1833, when they were taken by the United Kingdom; London cites its continuous presence since then and the islanders’ right to self-determination, confirmed in the 2013 referendum by 99.8% of voters.

World.title: Cost-of-living protests spread across Europe with unrest in France and Germany
World.content:
Cost-of-living protests spread across Europe with unrest in France and Germany

1st Sunday, November 2026 - 15:52 UTC Full article

The protests began a month ago at a high school on the outskirts of Paris over the state of schools and widened to the cost of living

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets of France and Germany on Saturday to protest against the cost of living and deteriorating public services, in mostly peaceful demonstrations that ended in clashes between police and masked groups in several cities. In France, where the third day of protests in a month took place, 565 people were arrested.

According to France’s interior ministry, some 320,000 people took part in about 150 demonstrations across the country, down from an estimated 410,000 the previous weekend. In Paris, 70,000 marched along boulevards on the outskirts to avoid the city centre, some in Halloween costumes. The protests, called by students, trade unions and former members of the “yellow vest” movement, passed off calmly until the end, when masked groups hurled paving stones at police in Paris, who responded with teargas and baton charges. There were also incidents in Marseille, Lyon and Toulouse, where water cannon were used. Four police officers and a gendarme were injured in the capital. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who had deployed 70,000 officers, denounced an “extraordinary” level of violence and described a petrol bomb attack on a riot officer as “attempted murder”.

The protests began a month ago at a high school on the outskirts of Paris over the state of schools and widened to the cost of living. The first major day, on October 17, ended with the looting of hundreds of shops in several cities. Students announced new blockades of high schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday, ahead of a trade union demonstration called for November 5.

In Germany, thousands of young people demonstrated in dozens of cities at the call of the group “Gen Z regelt!” (“Gen Z has got this”) “for education, health, the climate and an affordable life”. After largely peaceful marches, police used water cannon in Cologne against protesters throwing fireworks; in Frankfurt at least two shops were looted, according to a Reuters witness, and in Hamburg burning barricades were set up, according to the newspaper Bild.

There were also clashes in Tirana, the capital of Albania, at a new protest demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Police were on alert in Barcelona, over calls from an anonymous TikTok network, and in Italy, after recent clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna.

World.title: Querétaro-Irapuato train line now 25% complete
World.content:
The 102-kilometer Querétaro-Irapuato train line is 25% complete one year into its construction, according to the Agency for Trains and Integrated Public Transportation (ATTRAPI).

The US $5.3 billion project, which broke ground in September 2025, is being developed in Mexico’s Bajío region, which hosts global manufacturing, agribusiness and technology companies. Once complete, the route is expected to benefit up to 2 million people.

On Saturday, President Claudia Sheinbaum inspected construction of the new train line, which is part of a federal plan to lay 2,500 km (reduced from 3,000) of tracks for passenger and freight services by 2030, at an estimated cost of 700 billion pesos (almost US $37.2 billion).

“The construction of trains is driving employment and economic development in the country,” Sheinbaum said on Saturday. “So, congratulations to those who are with us today, to the companies that are building, to the workers, to the governor of Querétaro, who has been a great help and to the governor of Guanajuato,” she added.

“We belong to different political parties, but that has nothing to do with it when we work together for the good of Mexico.”

The train line will have five stations once complete: Apaseo el Grande, Celaya, Cortazar/Villagrán, Salamanca and Irapuato. As part of the project, 10 viaducts, a box tunnel and 13 roads are being built, creating an expected 3,365 direct and 5,700 indirect jobs throughout construction.

The multinational transportation company Alstom is manufacturing the trains in Hidalgo, each one measuring 100 meters long and capable of being coupled together if required, according to the head of ATTRAPI’s construction unit, Efraín Deschamps Gutiérrez de Velasco.

Querétaro Governor Mauricio Kuri González and Guanajuato Governor Libia Dennise García Muñoz Ledo, both of the opposition National Action Party (PAN), thanked the president for spearheading the railroad, which is expected to enhance connectivity between Mexico City and the Bajío region, generate employment opportunities and spur economic development.

The Querétaro-Irapuato train line will eventually connect with the Mexico City-Querétaro train line, which is currently between 32% and 35% complete, Sheinbaum said during an official tour of the work site on Monday.

With reports from El Universal and Debate

World.title: How might the results of today’s midterm elections in the United States impact Mexico?
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump could make greater security-related demands on Mexico after the U.S. midterm elections, according to a Mexico City-based public affairs and political risk consultancy.

All 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and 35 of 100 seats in the U.S. Senate are on the line in today’s midterms. The Republican Party currently holds majorities in both the House and the Senate, but control of one or both chambers could change in early 2027 when newly elected lawmakers take office.

In a report titled “México y Estados Unidos. Entre la revisión del T-MEC y el impacto de las elecciones intermedias” (Mexico and the United States: Between the USMCA Review and the Impact of the Midterm Elections), Integralia Consultores says that the U.S. midterms “will modify counterweights on Trump, but won’t necessarily reduce pressure on Mexico.”

“A Democratic majority in one or both chambers would lead to increased investigations and oversight of the executive branch, intensifying internal political confrontation. Faced with greater domestic constraints, Trump might focus more attention on foreign policy to build his legacy,” the consultancy writes in the executive summary of its report.

“The fight against drug trafficking and organized crime — which enjoys greater bipartisan consensus than other international issues — could take on greater prominence and lead to new demands on Mexico,” Integralia says.

To date, President Claudia Sheinbaum has maintained a respectful relationship with Trump, even as the U.S. government pressures Mexico on a range of issues, including trade, security and immigration. Her administration has taken some steps that have been interpreted as attempts to appease the Trump administration — such as increasing tariffs on imports from China and sending scores of organized crime figures to the U.S. — but Sheinbaum has remained a steadfast defender of Mexican sovereignty and hasn’t shied away from denouncing what she sees as U.S. meddling in Mexican affairs.

What demands could Trump make on Mexico?

According to Integralia, “[a] Trump with more internal constraints due to a Democratic majority [in Congress] could dedicate more attention” to the international fight against drug trafficking, stepping up demands on Mexico for “cooperation, extraditions and actions against criminal organizations.”

“New threats of unilateral [U.S.] actions [in Mexico] can’t be ruled out,” adds the consultancy.

The Mexican government already cooperates closely with the Trump administration on security issues, but is steadfastly opposed to U.S. action on Mexican soil. Sheinbaum has denounced the Central Intelligence Agency’s alleged participation in a drug lab raid in Chihuahua in April without the authorization or knowledge of her administration.

Her government has sent more than 90 organized crime figures to the United States to face justice, while security authorities have arrested more than 70,000 people for allegedly committing high-impact crimes since she took office in October 2024. In the same period, authorities have seized over 36,000 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of narcotics, and dismantled close to 2,800 clandestine drug laboratories.

Despite the progress in combating crime and violence — homicides declined in every state in the first nine months of 2026 — the Trump administration has continued to pressure Mexico to do more to combat drug trafficking, and the U.S. president himself has periodically threatened unilateral military action against cartels in Mexico.

A continuation of such threats, as Integralia says is possible, would certainly not be a surprise.

Will the midterm results affect USMCA negotiations?

According to Integralia, the United States trade negotiations with Mexico “will move forward regardless of the electoral result.”

“Trump will retain broad authority to maintain or modify tariffs and push for stricter regional content requirements,” the consultancy says.

“However,” Integralia adds, “Republican defeats in states affected by the tariffs could increase pressure within the party to moderate some trade measures and avoid further political costs leading up to 2028,” when the next U.S. presidential election will be held.

In ongoing trade talks with the United States, Mexico is aiming to negotiate a reduction — if not the total elimination — of U.S. tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles. The dialogue is taking place after the Trump administration announced in July that it had decided against renewing the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years to 2042. The three-way agreement remains in effect, but is currently subject to annual reviews.

Both Sheinbaum and Trump said last month that Mexico and the U.S. were “very close” to reaching a trade deal. Such an agreement could improve the prospects of the Trump administration agreeing to a 16-year renewal of the USMCA, although Washington and Ottawa would also need to resolve their trade differences.

The U.S. government has many concerns about the USMCA and its trade relationships with its neighbors, including ones related to trade deficits, energy policy and China.

How could the US midterm results affect Trump’s deportation agenda?

According to Integralia, immigration policy will remain a priority for Trump, “regardless of the makeup of the [U.S.] Congress.”

However, Democratic Party control of Congress “could increase oversight of deportations, ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] operations and the treatment of migrants” by the Trump administration, the consultancy says.

“… Mexico will continue facing pressure to contain migration flows and receive deportees,” Integralia says.

During the second Trump administration, Mexico has received Mexican deportees as well as nationals of other countries. Meanwhile, data indicates that illegal crossings into the United States from Mexico have fallen sharply during Trump’s second term.

A Democratic Party-controlled Congress that increases oversight of ICE and the treatment of immigrants in the U.S. would be a welcome development for the Mexican government, which has filed complaints with prosecutor’s offices in the U.S. regarding the deaths of Mexican citizens in the custody of ICE or during ICE operations.

Eighteen Mexicans have died in ICE custody or ICE operations during Trump’s second term, including Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias, who passed away in the Rio Grande Processing Center in Laredo, Texas, last month after he was allegedly denied medication he needed to control his health problems, including diabetes.

On numerous occasions, Sheinbaum has expressed her opposition to Trump’s aggressive deportation agenda, and said in July she disagreed with his call for continued immigration traffic stops.

“If there is a person who committed a crime, he or she must be pursued. But migration in itself shouldn’t be criminalized,” she said on July 16.

World.title: China-based CATL, global leader in energy storage, signs on for a major Mexican solar project
World.content:
CATL, the world’s largest manufacturer of battery energy storage units, is seeking to become a player in Mexico’s energy-storage business.

Headquartered in China, CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited) has signed an agreement to supply a 313 megawatt (MW)/1,639.45 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system (BESS) to the La Alegría Solar project in the state of Campeche. The project is being developed by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, a Danish global fund manager and investment firm.

At the 2026 World Laureates Forum, Dr. Robin Zeng, CATL Chairman & CEO, shares how CATL uses AI to advance research. CATL has over 600 TB of fundamental research data and more than one trillion test records. Its AI-native platform connects computational research with lab experiments. Watch how AI, scientific data and experimental validation come together to accelerate research. #CATL #AIforScience #ScientificDiscovery #WorldLaureatesForum — CATL (@catl_official) November 1, 2026

According to CATL, La Alegría will incorporate Mexico’s first BESS with an energy capacity exceeding 1 gigawatt-hour and will be the largest battery storage system in the country.

BESS units do not produce electricity themselves. Their function is to store energy generated by other sources and release it when needed, allowing for better use of renewable energy production and responsiveness to supply fluctuations, while providing ancillary services to maintain the stability of the electrical system.

CATL’s plans for La Alegría include more than 1.1 million photovoltaic modules of 685 Watt peak (Wp) each, 101 transformer substations and 202 inverters. Wp is the unit that measures the maximum theoretical power output of a photovoltaic (PV) solar panel.

The evacuation infrastructure includes a 34.5/400-kilovolt step-up substation and a 2.85 km, 400-kilovolt transmission line, occupying a total area of ​​1,206.97 hectares.

The design represents a substantial change from the original configuration as the proposed battery energy storage capacity (1,639.45 MWh) is approximately 5.2 times the 314.98 MWh appearing in the approved environmental documentation.

From auxiliary service to business opportunity

CATL’s desire to expand its presence in Mexico coincides with plans by the Energy Ministry (Sener) to incorporate 935 megawatts of electrical storage capacity — with systems capable of injecting energy into the grid for at least three continuous hours — to support greater energy generation through renewable sources.

Expansión magazine reported that Sener is preparing a call for proposals to develop power generation and storage plants, promising to expedite permits and interconnection studies.

Sener is looking to the BESS market, which would help integrate more solar and wind power plants while helping to maintain the stability of the electrical grid.

These new market conditions open the possibility for CATL to supply equipment and solutions to new projects and move toward long-term operation and maintenance in Mexico’s power system.

Still, CATL’s chief technology officer Amanda Xu told Expansión that market development depends on investors finding conditions that justify allocating capital to storage systems.

With reports from Expansión, PV Magazine and MexCham

World.title: Mexico-Canada trade was up more than 18% through August
World.content:
Two-way merchandise trade between Mexico and Canada increased by more than 18% between January and August compared to the same period of last year, according to data published by Statistics Canada.

Trade in goods between the two North American countries was worth 34.42 billion Canadian dollars (CAD) (US $24.6B) in the first eight months of 2026, a year-over-year increase of 18.3%.

Mexico exported goods worth 26.91 billion CAD to Canada between January and August, a year-over-year increase of 17.4%.

In the same period, Canada’s exports to Mexico were worth 7.51 billion CAD, a year-over-year increase of 21.4%.

Mexico recorded a trade surplus of 19.41 billion CAD in the first eight months of 2026.

Among the goods traded between Mexico and Canada are vehicles and auto parts, electrical and electronic equipment, industrial machinery, agricultural products and metal.

The increase in Mexico-Canada trade this year comes at a time when both countries are navigating trade tensions with the United States, their largest trading partner. The Trump administration, which has imposed tariffs on various Mexican and Canadian goods, announced in July that it had decided not to renew the USMCA for an additional 16 years, although the three-way free trade pact remains in effect.

Despite the imposition of tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles, the value of Mexico’s exports to the United States increased 18.3% in the first eight months of 2026 compared to the same period of last year, according to the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

The total value of Mexico’s exports to the U.S. in the period was US $419.34 billion, a record high.

For every US $1 worth of goods Mexico exported to Canada in the first eight months of 2026, it exported about US $22 worth of goods to the United States.

Mexico-Canada trade grows as the two countries cultivate closer ties

Trade between Mexico and Canada has increased as President Claudia Sheinbaum and Prime Minister Mark Carney have sought to strengthen cooperation between the two countries at a time when the U.S. government is pursuing protectionist trade policies under President Donald Trump.

A key example of their efforts to strengthen cooperation is the Mexico-Canada Action Plan 2025-28, which the two leaders launched in Mexico City in September 2025. The plan covers areas such as trade facilitation and commercial cooperation, investment promotion, trade policy cooperation, innovation and joint action in sustainable mining.

Sheinbaum and Carney have met in person on at least three occasions and have also spoken by telephone several times.

In January, Sheinbaum praised Carney for his speech at the World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, Switzerland, during which the Canadian prime minister asserted that the rules-based international order was undergoing a “rupture, not a transition.”

During a call in August around seven weeks after the Trump administration announced its decision to not renew the USMCA until 2042, the Mexican and Canadian leaders “underscored the importance of renewing … [the trade agreement] as soon as possible to provide greater certainty for North American businesses and workers,” according to a statement released by Carney’s office.

Sheinbaum has stressed that Mexico, the United States and Canada could reach a deal to extend the USMCA for an additional 16 years “at any time,” although the Trump administration has various concerns about the pact and its trade relationships with its neighbors, including ones related to trade deficits, energy policy and China.

The statement released by Carney’s office on Aug. 20 also said that the Canadian prime minister and Mexican president discussed “the progress between Canada and Mexico on cross-border trade.” That progress is reflected in Statistics Canada’s trade data for the first eight months of 2026.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Daniel Saborío, Monterrey’s teenage swimming phenom, takes a bronze at the Youth Olympic Games in Senegal
World.content:
With his sights on qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, 17-year-old Mexican swimmer Daniel Saborío Grillo took another step forward Tuesday, capturing a bronze medal in the 400-meter freestyle at the Youth Olympic Games in Senegal.

The native of Monterrey, Nuevo León, finished in a personal-best 3 minutes, 52.72 seconds, earning Mexico’s first medal in Dakar, Senegal’s capital, and its first swimming medal in the Summer Youth Olympics, now in their fourth edition.

The previous three were held in Singapore in 2010, Nanjing, China, in 2014, and Buenos Aires in 2018.

The Youth Olympics are a smaller, age-restricted counterpart to the Olympics. The current 14-day competition opened Saturday and continues through Nov. 13 in Dakar, nearby Diamniadio and the coastal resort of Saly.

Saborío was one of Mexico’s two flag bearers at the opening ceremony at the Diamniadio Olympic Stadium, which drew tens of thousands of spectators, according to reports.

The other was Ariadna Yarey Chávez Medina, a 17-year-old judo competitor from Tulum, Quintana Roo. Chávez lost her opening bout, a quarterfinal, to Russia’s Anastasiia Dobrovolskaia on Tuesday.

The competition has brought together about 2,700 athletes ages 14 to 17, with 153 medal events across 25 sports.

Mexico — which has sent 62 athletes to compete in 19 sports — captured a second bronze Tuesday when its mixed-gender Baseball5 team defeated Kenya two games to one in the third-place series. Making its Youth Olympic debut, Baseball5 is a 5-on-5 game played without bats or gloves; batters hit a rubber ball with their bare hands.

Saborío arrived in Senegal three months after winning two gold and two silver medals at the Central American and Caribbean Games in Santo Domingo.

In his first event in Dakar, he finished fifth in the 100-meter freestyle. He also is scheduled to swim the 200 freestyle Friday.

Saborío trains while attending high school at Monterrey’s Tecnológico de Monterrey. His longer-term plans include the 2027 Pan American Games in Lima, Peru, and a bid to qualify for the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, Diario de México reported.

However, in last year’s junior world championships in Romania, Saborío did not finish among the top 20 in his individual events.

These Games in Dakar were originally scheduled for 2022, but were postponed four years because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

They are the first Olympic Games held in Africa.

Beyond competition, athletes must complete an education program covering anti-doping, mental health, injury prevention and preparation for life after sports.

With reports from Diario de México, El Universal, Associated Press, UDG TV and Claro Sports

World.title: MND Local BCS: PGA golf and Day of the Dead celebrations in Los Cabos
World.content:
This year, for the first time, the PGA Tour scheduled its two golf tournaments in Mexico in consecutive weeks, putting them back-to-back on its FedExCup Fall Schedule.

Last week, the 2026 VidantaWorld Mexico Open was played in Nuevo Nayarit on the Greg Norman-designed Vidanta Vallarta Course, with three hours of daily coverage televised on Golf Channel — including the somewhat anticlimactic final round, in which Andrew Novak cruised comfortably to a five-shot margin of victory.

The PGA Tour returns to Cabo San Lucas

20 years of PGA TOUR golf in Mexico—and the history continues.

Watch this video on YouTube

From Thursday through Sunday, the action shifts to Los Cabos for the World Wide Technology Championship (WWTC), held at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal course at Diamante in Cabo San Lucas. Yes, Golf Channel will feature plenty of WWTC coverage, too, but for Cabeños (Los Cabos residents) and visiting tourists, the experience promises more fun and local flavor live.

The tournament field was confirmed last Friday, and as expected, many of the best players in the world will be teeing it up in Los Cabos for the WWTC, including returning champion Ben Griffin (coming off a tied-for-fourth-place finish in Nuevo Nayarit), former U.S. Open champion Lucas Glover, and electrifying newcomer Jackson Koivun, who won in just his third start after turning pro this summer and was recently a member of the victorious U.S. President’s Cup team.

Dates: Nov. 5-8

Location: Diamante, Cabo San Lucas

Cost: General admission entry starts at US $35 per ticket, with abundant VIP upgrades available.

Día de Muertos on the water in Los Cabos

The sixth edition of “Altars at Sea” returns to Cabo San Lucas, where celebrations of all sorts — including for Mexico’s iconic Day of the Dead — are judged to be better when they take place on boats.

About 20 ofrenda-laden vessels participated during Monday’s parade in Cabo San Lucas Bay. However, the four-day festival also features art, music and maritime culture, including Sunday’s “mermaids” panel discussion featuring well-known female athletes such as Olympic artistic swimmer Pamela Toscano Millán, open-water swimmer Stephanie Montero and rower Aylin Ibarra Madueña.

Toscano also directed an aquatic performance entitled “The Return of the Chalchiuhcuitle and the Guardians of the Blue Offering” on Monday.

Dates: Nov. 1-4

Location: Cabo San Lucas Bay, Playa El Médano

Cost: Free

Inclement weather postpones women’s-only breast cancer charity fishing tournament

Fishing season in Baja California Sur always has an element of potential profit involved, but charitable causes are usually front-and-center, too. For instance, although Bisbee’s trio of fishing tournaments in Los Cabos — The East Cape Offshore (US $1.6 million), Los Cabos Offshore (US $2.39 million), and Black and Blue (US $7.46 million) — exceeded US $10 million in prize pools this year, Bisbee’s also has a long and storied history of supporting the local community, from Casa Hogar to the innumerable free meals donated through Hope for Los Cabos and the launching of a Los Cabos fireboat.

The prize pool is a bit smaller for the first-ever women’s-only Onco Reto Ferre-Mar (“Women Conquering the Sea”) fishing tournament in the state capital, La Paz, whose name references a local nonprofit — Grupo Onco Reto, which supports women diagnosed with breast cancer — and the tournament sponsor: Ferre-Mar, a marine hardware and outdoor adventure store in BCS. Still, a guaranteed 300,000 pesos is on the line for teams targeting dorado (mahi-mahi), as well as jackpot-eligible species like marlin, tuna and wahoo … with all entry fees going towards the worthy cause.

“All the funds raised in this tournament go directly to (the non-profit), which consists of breast cancer survivors,” Cristina Higuera Murillo, president of Grupo Onco Reto, told Tribuna de Mexico. “We are very excited because we have the support of socially responsible companies.”

Ladies fishing events on the rise in BCS

No, this is not the only ladies-only fishing tournament on the peninsula. The Ladies Shoot Out has been drawing distaff anglers to Los Barriles on Los Cabos’ East Cape since 2025, and the previous version (the Ladies Only Fishing Tournament) for a half-dozen years before that.

This year, La Paz hosted its inaugural women’s shore fishing tournament. Meanwhile, the neighboring state of Baja California also has its own fishing competition for women: Reinas del Mar, or “Queens of the Sea,” held at a different location each summer.

But Onco Reto Ferre-Mar is the only one this year that has had to be rescheduled due to weather conditions. BCS has been inundated with rain over the past few months as a Super El Niño-charged hurricane season has sent one tropical storm after another hurtling towards the region. Most have been narrow misses that did little damage outside of flooding from the prodigious rainfall, but the latest, Tropical Storm Vance, also seems to have knocked Onco Reto Ferre-Mar from its scheduled calendar slot — although organizers mentioned only the El Niño phenomenon generally in their official statement.

Originally slated to take place on Oct. 31 and Nov. 1, the tournament has been pushed back a month and is now confirmed for early December.

Dates: Dec. 5-6

Location: Muelle Fiscal, La Paz

Cost: Entry is 7,000 pesos per team

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Pest outbreak forces destruction of 52 tonnes of avocados across 4 states
World.content:
