World.title: GYLA challenges conviction of defendant in case over storming of Georgia’s presidential palace
World.content:
According to the Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA), the case against Paata Manjgaladze, one of the leaders of the opposition Strategy Aghmashenebeli party, who was convicted in the so-called “4 October case”, lacks sufficient evidence that he planned, organised or led group violence.

In a detailed assessment, the association says the prosecution has failed to distinguish Manjgaladze’s political activities from any alleged involvement in violent acts.

In particular, it has presented no evidence linking him to the violence outside the presidential palace in Tbilisi.

On 4 October 2025, Georgia held local government elections. Much of the opposition boycotted the vote and staged a large-scale protest in Tbilisi that day. The demonstration ended with an attempt to storm the presidential palace.

GYLA argues that these claims are not substantiated by Manjgaladze’s previous political statements either, as some of them are undated and the circumstances in which they were made remain unclear.

“A political or organisational connection to a protest cannot in itself constitute grounds for liability for organising violence unless the defendant’s specific contribution is established,” GYLA writes.

Paata Manjgaladze

Paata Manjgaladze is the secretary-general of the Strategy Aghmashenebeli party and a former member of the Georgian parliament. On 4 October 2025, he took part in a protest in Tbilisi. Prosecutors accused him of organising group violence and leading it. On 7 May 2026, a court found him guilty and sentenced him to seven years in prison. His case is now before the Tbilisi Court of Appeal.

What Manjgaladze is accused of

Prosecutors charged Paata Manjgaladze on 6 October 2025. According to their account, he and other opposition figures arrested in connection with the case had urged citizens to overthrow the government by force. On 4 October, they then decided to organise group violence.

Opera singer Paata Burchuladze, who organised the rally and was later arrested in the same case, announced the plan at the protest. Murtaz Zodelava, a member of the United National Movement party, then called on the crowd to march towards the presidential palace and seize it.

To support the charges, prosecutors cite witness testimony, media reports, written documents, expert assessments, audio and video recordings from the scene, as well as objects found there and damaged equipment. The investigation also relied on search and seizure records and other materials gathered during the inquiry.

The prosecution maintains that this evidence is sufficient to establish the defendants’ involvement in the crime.

However, it remains unclear which specific pieces of evidence relate directly to Manjgaladze. In GYLA’s assessment, the indictment does not adequately explain what specific actions Manjgaladze himself took or what evidence demonstrates his involvement in the crime.

GYLA argues that political activity, attendance at a protest, a photograph with other organisers or a particular sequence of events cannot, in themselves, justify charging someone with organising group violence. This is especially important when the defendant is a politician. The charges must leave no doubt that the prosecution is not politically motivated.

What GYLA wants the Court of Appeal to do

GYLA is calling on the Court of Appeal to examine what specific actions prosecutors attribute to Manjgaladze, what evidence supports the allegations and how the court assessed the defence’s arguments.

The organisation also notes that Georgia’s Public Defender (ombudsman) has submitted an opinion in the case. The Public Defender likewise found no clear evidence of Manjgaladze’s specific role in organising group violence, arguing that merely describing him as one of the protest organisers is not sufficient grounds for criminal prosecution.

GYLA believes that if the Court of Appeal agrees with its position and that of the Public Defender, and the legal grounds exist, it should acquit Manjgaladze.

Criminal proceedings have been launched against 64 people in connection with the events of 4 October. Prosecutors charged those detained with organising group violence, leading it or taking part in it, attempting to seize a strategic facility, and calling for the violent overthrow of the constitutional order. The case was divided into several separate proceedings.

The first-instance trials have now concluded. Of the 64 defendants:

One person was fined;

was fined; 29 people were sentenced to prison terms, three of them in absentia;

were sentenced to prison terms, three of them in absentia; 12 defendants had their sentences reduced under plea agreements;

had their sentences reduced under plea agreements; 22 people received suspended sentences under plea agreements and avoided prison.

World.title: Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by Italian La Repubblica newspaper on November 4, 2020 (VIDEO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 4. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist", on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline.

The erupted 44-day second Karabakh war ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity.

President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev was interviewed by the Italian La Repubblica newspaper.

-Mr. President, are you already tasting the flavor of the victory?

-Our task was to restore territorial integrity of Azerbaijan, and we are coming closer to this task. We have been waiting for restoration of the territorial integrity for almost 30 years. As you know, during all this time Azerbaijan was strictly committed to negotiation process. But unfortunately, it did not result in any tangible outcome. Plus, Armenian leadership during last couple of years was always provoking us by the statements, and by actions, including military provocations. So the last one took place on the 27th of September. We had to respond and our response was very sensitive to Armenia. So, when we talk about the victory we did not put in front of us such a target. We wanted to resolve it at the negotiation table. But we were always ready to do it on the battlefield what we are doing.

-Putin is not willing to intervene. So, you can act without obstacles.

-Actually, I on many occasions commented the situation that co-chairs of the Minsk Group, 3 countries which are at the same time permanent members of the Security Council of United Nations, adopted resolutions back in 1993 which demanded immediate and complete and unconditional withdrawal of Armenian troops from the Azerbaijani territories. Therefore, these countries themselves created the legal base for the settlement. But Armenia did not implement these resolutions. Another point, which I was referring to is that mediators must be neutral, no matter how they feel about situation. How close their relations are with us, or with Armenia, but if they are not neutral they cannot be mediators. Therefore, the neutrality now which we more or less see on the ground I think is the only way how the things can happen. Therefore, it was not a kind of a green light for us. We responded to Armenian attack on the 27th of September without any 100% understanding who will do what. We just did what we thought was right to defend our country, to defend our people, and to restore justice.

-How useful is the Ankara support to your action?

-It is very useful. This support came from the very beginning, from the early hours of the clashes which started on the 27th of September. President of Turkey made a very clear statement that Turkey stands side by side with Azerbaijan. That was a very important sign of political and moral support, and I many times referred to the fact that this is only political and moral support, but it was sufficient. Because such a strong country as Turkey when openly declares its position on this issue, it also sends the signal to the whole world, that Azerbaijan is doing the right thing. Azerbaijan is restoring it’s territorial integrity, Azerbaijan is fighting on its territory. We are not aggressors, we are not attacking other countries. Therefore, this political support which started in the early hours of the clashes and continues up to now is very important for the conflict resolution.

-What can you say about the jihadists’ presence that president Macron, Russian foreign minister denounced that they are fighting against Armenia with your army. Is it true?

-On many occasions I already during this time, more than one month, referred to this issue and said that this is not true. This is not correct information. I don’t know why this information was circulated, and still is circulated. First, we haven’t been provided with any evidence, any proof about that. All were words, and those words were articulated in the early days of the conflict. And you referred to President Macron’s statement about that. That was only in the first days of the conflict. Since that time, we didn’t hear these kind of statements. So this is first. No proofs no evidence. Second, no need. Many times I said we have an army of a 100 thousand fighters, a regular army. We can mobilize several times more if we announce the total mobilization. We have modern weapons. We have a sophisticated technology. And we have a very high moral spirit. Therefore, there is no need for that. But unfortunately, what happens on the other side is being ignored. We already have enough evidences about foreigners fighting on Armenian side. They say they are native Armenians but first, it does not make any difference, because if foreign citizen is fighting against one country against another, it is a mercenary. Then, we do not have a 100% evidence that all of them are Armenians. We know that there are others. We know that PKK is there, we know that some terrorists from the Middle East joined the so-called "army of Nagorno-Karabakh". Therefore, unfortunately, this issue is absolutely out of picture. So, it creates an impression of a deliberate political attack on Azerbaijan. Plus, why Armenians are also exploiting this false statement, because for them probably it is very painful to admit that we beat them on the battlefield. For 30 years, they have been pretending that they have an unbeatable army. For 30 years they were telling that they on their own occupied our territories. Though, we know that it was wrong. So, we proved them who is who. We proved that their so-called "unbeatable army" is a legend, is a mythology. And for them to admit it is very painful. But they have already admitted their defeat. Prime minister Pashinyan sent a letter to President Putin asking for a military help. This is an admitting of their military defeat and our victory.

-What will be the difficulty for you to manage a possible victory, in the territory which populated by 98% of Armenian people?

-This territory was populated with maybe higher now. It was higher. Because all Azerbaijanis have been expelled. They committed ethnic cleansing against Azerbaijanis. It’s a statistics, soviet statistics, not our statistics. How many people of different nationalities lived in Nagorno-Karabakh autonomous district in the end of 1970s? Almost 25% of the population there were Azerbaijanis. 40 thousand people. Shusha was 98% percent inhabited by Azerbaijanis. Today, there is no one. In Khankandi, there have been many Azerbaijanis. In Hadrut district, in other districts. Khojaly, which they committed a genocide, was 100% Azerbaijanis. So, they have been all ethnically cleansed, killed, tortured and expelled. And unfortunately, no one, no one accused Armenia of that. We did not see any sanctions on Armenia. We did not see any serious information supporting us. So, that was done and they created reality on the ground. This is the first thing. Second thing, 200 years ago, there were no Armenians at all there. Because I many times referred to the treaties which Karabakh khan signed with Russian empire. That Kurakchay treaty of 1805, nothing is said about ethnic Armenians there.

Ethnic Armenians were brought to that region from eastern Anatolia and Persia, by Tsarist Russia in order to change religious and ethnic composition of the region. So, this is historical part. Now coming to your question. I many times said that all those who live in Nagorno-Karabakh will continue to live there in peace and dignity. Armenians are our citizens. There are thousands of Armenians who live in different parts of Azerbaijan, primarily in Baku, and those Armenians who live in Nagorno-Karabakh can be sure that their security will be provided, their financial situation will be much better. And they will live much better life than today under this suppression of the junta regime in Nagorno-Karabakh.

-Three ceasefires as already were broken. The peace talks seem not to get any result. Who is to blame for?

-Armenia. Look at their chronology. First, ceasefire was agreed in Moscow. In less than 24 hours they attacked Ganja with ballistic missiles from the territory of Armenia. It is proven. Russia, France and United States and many other countries can detect the launch of ballistic missiles. So, they know, it was launched from Armenia, and Pashinyan was lying when he said that it was not them. So, that was in less than 24 hours. They attacked at night, in a very mean way. They attacked deliberately the residential settlement. And as a result of two attacks almost 30 people, innocent people, including children were killed. The second ceasefire was violated by them after five minutes of the announcement of that. And the third ceasefire they violated attacking Barda. So, it was not us. What were we supposed to do? Sit and wait when they are killing us? Of course, we respond and will continue to do it. They needed ceasefire in order to continue their aggression, in order to try to regain and occupy again the territories which we have liberated. And also they wanted to create a chaos, panic in Azerbaijan by attacking civilians but they miscalculated the spirit of Azerbaijani people. Yes, we suffer from these mean attacks. We have 91 civilians so far killed, and more than 400 wounded. But this did not break our will, on the contrary, it makes us even stronger.

-What would you answer to premier Pashinyan that I met 3 weeks ago? He said that you’re here for a new genocide in Nagorno-Karabakh.

-Absolutely false. All their history is false. There is no signs of that. You know, as I said, there are thousands of Armenians living in Azerbaijan. There are no Azerbaijanis living in Armenia or in Nagorno-Karabakh. 99% of Armenian population are ethnic Armenians. Can you find any other country in our region where such a full domination of one nationality? It is a mono-ethnic republic. Why? Because either they expel everybody, or other nationalities cannot live there. Azerbaijan is a multi-ethnic, multi-confessional country. Therefore, talking about the so-called genocide is absolutely unacceptable and this is another fake which they want to present as they always do. They always want to present themselves as the people who always suffering, always crying always needing help. And today look, he calls President Putin 5 times a day. He calls President Macron maybe less, but still. He calls everyone. He calls European leaders. He asks for recognition of Nagorno-Karabakh not understanding that there is a unified position of European Union on territorial integrity of Azerbaijan. Therefore, he tries to use every fake method in order to get some support. Therefore, it is absolutely wrong. And as I said, and I am responsible for what I am saying, those Armenians who live in Nagorno-Karabakh can be sure that their security will be provided.

-With Italy you have a special partnership, you are our first provider of oil and gas. Are you afraid that if the war get bloodier and bloodier that partnership could be affected or not?

-I don’t think so. First, I think that the sooner the war stops the better. And we made such a suggestion. And our proposal was very constructive. I said many times during this more than one month, I can repeat once again. We are ready to stop today. If Armenian prime minister makes a committment that they will liberate the remaining part of the territories. He has not made this committment so far. When asked about compromises, he always talks about a self-determination. But self-determination is not the compromise they have to do. Their compromise must be liberation of all occupied territories with respect to the implementation of UN Security Council resolutions, and the basic principles. Because basic principles say that five regions and then two. So, four are already done by us unilaterally. Therefore, he must say that he will pull back the troops from remaining part of Aghdam and Kalbajar and Lachin districts. But he doesn’t make this statement. So it shows that he doesn’t want the war to stop. We are ready. This is first. Second, I don’t think that it will create any complications with respect to our relations with our partners. With Italy we have a special relations. We have signed a document which is called a Strategic Partnership document. And just before the pandemic I paid an official visit to Italy which was very successful and with very big plans I returned back home. I am sure we will implement those plans though pandemic interfered a little bit. But it is mainly non-related to energy sector. On energy track, we did I think all what we planned today. I think Italy for us is a major trading partner, because of oil supplies. And also soon we will celebrate the inauguration of TAP. Thus, Southern Gas Corridor will be completed. Plus, many Italian companies work in Azerbaijan successfully for many years. We are planning to invite more Italian companies as contractors. By the way, they have completed such important projects as petrochemicals here and together with President Mattarella we have been at the opening ceremony. Therefore, I am sure that this conflict will influence our relations neither with Italy nor with any other country. So, I am sure about that.

World.title: 5.2-magnitude earthquake strikes Kyrgyzstan
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 4. A magnitude 5.2 earthquake struck Kyrgyzstan on November 4. Tremors were also felt in several regions of Uzbekistan’s Fergana Valley.

This was reported by the Republican Center for Seismic Forecasting Monitoring of Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Emergency Situations.

According to the report, the earthquake was recorded at 02:34 local time, with its focus located at a depth of 10 kilometers.

In Uzbekistan’s Andijan and Fergana regions, the tremors reached an intensity of 2–3 points. The epicenter was located 134 and 136 kilometers from these regions, respectively.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan plans over 20,000 apartments by end-2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. Kyrgyzstan plans to complete the construction of more than 20,000 apartments under its affordable housing program by the end of 2026, the press service of the President of Kyrgyzstan reported.

Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov said this on Oct. 7 during his working visit to the Naryn region, where he attended the opening of a residential complex built by the State Mortgage Company in the city of Naryn.

New apartments will be built in the cities of Batken, Tokmok, Kara-Balta, Manas, Karakol and Cholpon-Ata, as well as in the Sokuluk, Suzak, Kara-Suu and Uzgen districts, according to the president.

"Across the country, around 150,000–200,000 families need affordable housing. We will continue the activities of the State Mortgage Company in order to justify our people’s trust in the bright future of Kyrgyzstan and the capabilities of the state. To improve living standards, we will fulfill our social commitments to provide housing," he said.

Japarov also said construction of a residential complex had recently begun in the village of Chaek in the Jumgal district. The complex will consist of eight blocks, six floors and 240 apartments.

Trend estimates that Kyrgyzstan could complete around 20,000 affordable housing units a year in 2027–2029 if the State Mortgage Company maintains the construction pace planned for 2026. This would result in around 60,000 additional housing units over the three years.

According to Trend’s calculations, combined with more than 20,000 apartments planned for completion in 2026, such a pace could bring the cumulative number of completed affordable housing units to at least 80,000 by the end of 2029.

That figure would correspond to roughly 40%–53% of the currently estimated need of 150,000–200,000 families, assuming each apartment addresses the housing needs of one family. This is a Trend estimate, not an official forecast.

Two unidentified projectiles strike tanker off coast of Oman
У б
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 4. An incident involving a tanker occurred off the coast of Oman. The vessel was struck by two unidentified projectiles.

This was reported by the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

The incident was recorded 14 nautical miles northeast of the Omani coast, near the town of Lima. Two projectiles struck the tanker's engine room.

According to preliminary information, there were no casualties as a result of the incident, and no reports of environmental damage have been received.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s crude oil exports to Greece rise 7.13% in eight months
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. Kazakhstan exported 2.96 million tonnes of crude oil and crude oil products obtained from bituminous minerals to Greece in January-August 2026, up 7.13% compared with the same period of 2025, when exports totaled 2.76 million tonnes.

This is according to Trend’s calculations based on data from the Bureau of National Statistics of Kazakhstan.

In value terms, exports of this commodity group to Greece increased by 25.06% year-on-year to $1.93 billion from $1.54 billion. Greece accounted for 6.3% of Kazakhstan's total export volume and 6.41% of its total export value during the first eight months of 2026.

In August 2026 alone, Kazakhstan exported 523,394 tonnes of crude oil to Greece, valued at $449.55 million.

Overall, Kazakhstan exported 46.96 million tonnes of crude oil and crude oil products obtained from bituminous minerals in January-August 2026, down 3.65% from 48.74 million tonnes in the same period of 2025. In value terms, exports of this commodity group increased by 16.31% to $30.09 billion from $25.87 billion a year earlier.

During the reporting period, Kazakhstan’s trade turnover with Greece amounted to $1.97 billion, up 22.05% from $1.62 billion in January-August 2025.

Kazakhstan’s exports to Greece totaled $1.93 billion, up 24.67% from $1.55 billion in January-August 2025. Meanwhile, imports from Greece totaled $42.71 million, down 37.36% from $68.18 million in the same period of 2025.

The figures indicate that crude oil and crude oil products obtained from bituminous minerals accounted for nearly all of Kazakhstan’s exports to Greece.

Meanwhile, Kazakhstan’s foreign trade turnover reached $102.96 billion in January-August 2026, up 12.8% in nominal terms compared with the same period of 2025.

Exports totaled $60.39 billion, increasing by 19.5% in nominal terms, while imports reached $42.57 billion, up 4.5%.

Crude oil and crude oil products obtained from bituminous minerals accounted for 49.8% of Kazakhstan’s exports in January-August 2026. Other major export commodities included refined copper and unwrought copper alloys (6.4%), radioactive chemical elements and radioactive isotopes (5.1%), copper ores and concentrates (4.4%), and ferroalloys (2.2%).

Passenger cars and other motor vehicles accounted for the largest share of imports, at 3.3%. Other major imported commodities included telephone equipment (2.7%), pharmaceutical products (2.5%), petroleum gases and other gaseous hydrocarbons (2.4%), and electric generating sets and rotary converters (2.2%).

Italy was Kazakhstan’s largest export destination, accounting for 18% of exports, followed by China (17.6%), Russia (8.5%), Türkiye (7.9%), France (6.1%) and the Netherlands (5.9%).

Russia was Kazakhstan’s largest import partner, accounting for 31% of imports, followed by China (29.8%), Germany (4.6%), the United States (3.9%), South Korea (2.5%) and Türkiye (2.1%).

World.title: Uzbekistan’s microfinance sector capital grows 56.6% to about $366M
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 19. The total capital of Uzbekistan’s microfinance institutions increased by 56.6% year over year to 4.4 trillion soums (about $365.9 million) as of September 1, 2026, while the number of institutions rose to 141.

This was reported by the Central Bank of Uzbekistan.

The sector’s total capital stood at 2.8 trillion soums (around $232.8 million) on September 1, 2025. The increase amounted to approximately 1.6 trillion soums (about $133 million), based on the reported rounded figures.

The expansion was accompanied by an increase in the number of institutions with larger capital bases. The number of microfinance institutions with total capital of at least 10 billion soums (about $831,715) rose from 37 to 48, while the number with capital ranging from 3 billion (around $249,514) to 10 billion soums increased from 39 to 48.

According to Trend’s calculations, the number of institutions with capital of at least 10 billion soums increased by 11, or approximately 29.7%, year over year. The number in the 3 billion–10 billion soum category grew by nine, or 23.1%.

Meanwhile, the number of institutions with total capital below 3 billion soums declined from 49 to 45, a decrease of four institutions, or approximately 8.2%.

Changes were also evident in the distribution of charter capital. The number of institutions with charter capital of 3 billion to 10 billion soums increased from 35 to 45, while the number with charter capital of at least 10 billion soums rose from 25 to 31. These increases amounted to approximately 28.6% and 24%, respectively.

Overall, the number of microfinance institutions increased by 16, from 125 to 141, representing growth of 12.8% over the year.

The share of total sector capital held by institutions with capital of at least 10 billion soums rose from 91.3% to 92.3%, an increase of 1 percentage point.

The figures indicate that Uzbekistan’s microfinance sector is expanding, with a growing number of institutions in the higher capital categories. Institutions with capital of at least 10 billion soums also accounted for a larger share of total sector capital, highlighting the concentration of capital among larger players.

World.title: Iran's Parviz Khan exports goods worth $417M in 7 months
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 29. Exports passing through the Parviz Khan Customs, located in the Kermanshah province in western Iran, amounted to 1.1 million tons, valued at $417 million during the 7 months of the current Iranian year (from March 21 through September 22, 2026).

This was announced by the Islamic Republic of Iran Customs Administration, citing remarks made by Director General of the Parviz Khan Customs Administration Hojjatollah Chavoshi.

Chavoshi noted that during the 7 months, goods exported via the Parviz Khan Customs were primarily destined for Iraq.

The customs representative added that the main items exported through Parviz Khan during this timeframe included steel ingots, fruits and vegetables, rebar, ceramics, construction materials, and dried fruits.

Chavoshi said that, on average, 501 trucks carrying export goods pass through the Parviz Khan Customs daily.

According to him, 24,000 tons of goods, valued at $131 million, were imported through the Parviz Khan Customs during the 7 months.

Chavoshi added that the Parviz Khan Customs is considered one of Iran's significant commercial border crossings, playing a key role in the development of trade turnover between Iran and Iraq.

According to Trend’s calculations based on data from Iran Customs Administration, goods valued at $790 million were exported through the Parviz Khan customs crossing during the past Iranian year. Furthermore, 2.9 million tons of cargo were transited through this customs point. The Parviz Khan customs crossing plays a significant role in Iran's foreign trade.

Iran's Kermanshah Province shares a 371-kilometer-long border with Iraq. There are seven customs points operating within this province. Goods valued at $3 billion are exported annually via Kermanshah Province.

Meanwhile, in Iran, the year is called the "true solar year." The current year in Iran is 1405. The Iranian year begins on March 20 or 21. The first 6 months of the year have 31 days, the next 6 months have 30 days, and the last month has 29 days in 3-year cycles and 30 days in 4-year cycles. Thus, the months of the Iranian year begin on the 21st, 22nd, or 23rd of the Gregorian calendar.

World.title: Staggs says he means no harm with refusal to sing Australian anthem
World.content:
Kotoni Staggs says his decision not to sing the national anthem comes from a place of respect, as he and his Kangaroos teammates find themselves at the centre of a culture war.

Staggs and several fellow Australia team members, who will face Samoa in Sunday's World Cup semifinal at the Sydney Football Stadium, have been criticised throughout the tournament because of their refusal to sing the pre-game anthem.

The Brisbane centre received the backing of Broncos teammate Pat Carrigan for his stance, hoping the decision would open up a wider discussion about Australia's history.

Kangaroos pile on the points in World Cup thrashing of Cook Islands The Kangaroos go undefeated through the group stage of the Rugby League World Cup as they close out the Pool A action with a 66-6 win over Cook Islands in Townsville.

Staggs, who has won nine caps for the Kangaroos since his debut in 2023, said: "I'm a proud Wirajudri boy and I'm proud of who I am and where I come from, and me not singing an anthem doesn't mean that I'm not grateful.

"I still love wearing that jersey. When the anthem is getting played you look around and get emotional.

"But me not singing, it's a whole different meaning to that and that's just me."

Staggs said his position on singing Advance Australia Fair came from wanting to honour his ancestors.

"Obviously in the past and what happened back in the day I've just learned from that," Staggs said.

"You also talk to your elders from back home and grandparents and stuff and [understand] what they had to go through. It's more of a respect for my elders and my family.

Kotoni Staggs says his refusal to sing the national anthem does not take away from his love of representing Australia. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

"I'm a proud Australian as well but at the end of the day it's just something that I've lived by, and I've got no harm in it. It doesn't take anything away from the jersey I wear."

Criticism of Staggs and other Indigenous Kangaroos stars, including Latrell Mitchell, is nothing new.

Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner, a proud Barkindji and Māori woman, has also stressed the importance of walking out alongside the Australian, Indigenous and Torres Strait Island flags during the World Cup.

"All three flags have separate meanings for our country, and it represents that we're a diverse country with many different cultures," she said.

Jillaroos players hold the Torres Strait Island flag over their shoulders during a national anthem at the World Cup. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

"Our team, in particular, this 23, and our staff come from all different walks of life and cultural backgrounds, and we celebrate that diversity. That's a reflection of our country.

"You know, the blue flag is really important to everybody, just as equally as our Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander flag.

"So when you look at the values of that and you educate yourself about those flags, then you can't help but be passionate to be a proud Australian."

Former Australian Test coach Mal Meninga previously defended players for their firm stance on the matter of the anthem.

Carrigan is of the opinion athletes should have the right to stand up for what they believe in.

Pat Carrigan says players should have the freedom to stand up for their beliefs. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

"As sports people there's a focus on us as role models, but it probably points to a greater conversation for us to have as a society outside of football," Carrigan said.

"And about the reason why the boys feel the way about the anthem and perhaps our history as a country too.

"I know that each and every boy here is proud to pull on the green and gold.

"People may say it's represented in singing an anthem. I love Australia and I'm proud to pull on this jersey and I love running out with these guys too.

"I think it's a unique opportunity in sport that we get to be role models and voice opinions on different things, and maybe that's a way for us to look at ourselves as a country and how we can continue to come together."

AAP/ABC

World.title: Former councillor pleads not guilty to stalking senior shire staff
World.content:
A former local government councillor and One Nation candidate in Western Australia is set to fight charges of stalking and ongoing breaches of violence restraining orders.

Gemma Marie Johnston served nearly three years as a Shire of Esperance councillor before resigning in August.

Last year she was a One Nation candidate for the federal seat of O'Connor, winning 11 per cent of the primary vote behind Liberal incumbent Rick Wilson (34 per cent).

The 56-year-old faced the Esperance Magistrate's Court on Tuesday on two charges of pursuing another to intimidate and 41 separate breaches of violence restraining orders.

She entered not guilty pleas to all charges and is set to reappear in court for a trial listing hearing on January 12.

Gemma Johnston (right) with One Nation leader Pauline Hanson on the campaign trail in Kalgoorlie-Boulder during the 2025 federal election. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

The court heard the stalking charges related to two senior shire staff members between February 11, 2025 and May 11 this year, and a separate allegation between August 8 and August 26 this year.

The VRO breaches are alleged to have occurred between May 2025 and May this year, while Ms Johnston was serving as a councillor.

During Tuesday's hearing, Ms Johnston was reprimanded several times by court staff before and during her appearance for the use of her mobile phone in the courtroom, and reminded of court etiquette.

Gemma Johnston was elected in October 2023. (Facebook: Gemma Johnston)

Ms Johnston's lawyer, Nick Terry, requested a copy of his client's phone records, which had been downloaded by police.

The prosecution told the court the volume of data was "extensive" and it would likely take several weeks.

Magistrate William Yoo ordered the records to be delivered by December 18.

Gemma Johnston served as a councillor from October 2023 until her resignation in August this year. (Facebook: Gemma Johnston)

Colourful career as councillor

Between her election in October 2023 and resignation three months ago, Ms Johnston was sanctioned three times by the Local Government Standards Panel for breaches of its code of conduct.

She breached regulations by engaging an external planning consultant to refute the shire's information contained in a council agenda, and was ordered to undergo seven hours of training for elected members.

In August 2025, she was suspended for a month by the State Administrative Tribunal for failing to complete the training.

On another occasion, Ms Johnston was accused of using "inside knowledge" as an elected member to arrange a flash mob outside the shire's administration building to confront then-fisheries minister Don Punch about the proposed South Coast Marine Park.

She was later cleared of that allegation.

Don Punch was met by around 300 protesters outside the Shire of Esperance administration building in April 2024. (ABC Esperance: Emily Smith)

But Ms Johnston was ordered by the panel to publicly apologise to fellow councillor Wes Graham regarding "disparaging" comments she made on social media at the time.

In May this year, the panel ordered Ms Johnston to make another public apology for "improper conduct" after involving herself in an administrative task without authorisation and speaking to a shire contractor in a disparaging manner about a council staff member.

World.title: Lobster fishers rail against salmon industry's antibiotic plans
World.content:
Tensions have escalated between Tasmania's salmon industry and the wild seafood sector over plans to close some fishing areas when antibiotics are used in salmon pens.

Salmon Tasmania has applied for an emergency permit to use florfenicol to treat farmed fish affected by a bacterial disease that caused mass mortalities in 2025.

A separate emergency permit issued late last year had to be revoked in March after traces of florfenicol were detected in wild seafood more than 10 kilometres away.

The new permit application includes a plan to shut wild fisheries for up to six weeks if they are located within the same zone as salmon pens treated with antibiotics.

The closures are designed to avoid trade bans being imposed by countries that have zero tolerance for antibiotics in rock lobster, abalone and other wild seafood.

The Tasmanian Atlantic salmon farming industry has been hard hit by disease. (Tassal)

Under the "Wild Fisheries Market Access Plan", Salmon Tasmania would also provide financial support to affected commercial fishers to ensure they were no worse off.

But lobster fisherman Bryce Way said he and others in his sector were opposed to any reduction in their access to fisheries.

"You've got this introduced species coming around wanting to shut our areas," Mr Way told ABC Mornings.

"And it's just not fair. It just makes no sense to us how they think it is right to do."

Once implemented, Mr Way said he doubted the closures would be limited to six weeks in future years.

"Where's it end?" he said.

"It's only four to six weeks now. What's next year, 12 weeks?"

Loading...

Mr Way said he and others were willing to disrupt the salmon industry through large-scale protests.

" If the salmon industry thinks that five kayaks and one dinghy was disruptive, what do you think is going to happen when you get 150, 200 commercial boats? "

He said no amount of compensation would make up for losing access to fisheries.

"If you're accepting money, you're selling your soul," he said. "That's all you're doing.

" If you care about the industry, you shouldn't be accepting any dollar value to have an area closed. "

Bryce Way says that if the salmon industry was inconvenienced by small protests (above), it should consider what a large-scale action might cause. (Supplied: Bob Brown Foundation)

Tasmanian Rock Lobster Council president Danny Fox said Mr Way's concerns were shared by many across the sector.

"They're not too happy, the fishermen," Mr Fox told the Country Hour.

"The sentiment's pretty poor."

He said there were no plans to "block" the salmon industry, but he would not rule out protests.

" Most fishermen are happy to see the salmon industry there, and it's just got to play by the rules, and they've got to stay in their own lane a little bit more. "

Salmon pens managed by Huon Aquaculture at Surveyors Bay. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

'Very, very small part' of wild fisheries affected

The Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority (APVMA) is expected to make a decision on Salmon Tasmania's emergency use permit later this month.

Salmon Tasmania chief executive John Whittington said, if approved, florfenicol would only be used in the D'Entrecasteaux Channel and Storm Bay when recommended by veterinarians.

"When you look at the areas that would be closed if we were using florfenicol … [it's] a very, very small part of their [wild] fishery," he told ABC Mornings.

John Whittington says the salmon industry is also working on options to minimise the use of antibiotics. (ABC News: Madeleine Rojahn)

Dr Whittington said Salmon Tasmania was in discussions with all trade-exposed fishing sectors about the proposed compensation plan.

These include the lobster, abalone, oyster and periwinkle and urchin sectors.

"What we're looking to do is work with the sectors to develop an industry support program that ensures that if there is any out-of-pocket cost as a result of a closure for florfenicol, those fishers are made good through the process."

The first licence to use florfenicol in Atlantic salmon farms was revoked after traces were found in non-target species kilometres away from where it was deployed. (Abbey Laboratories)

Dr Whittington said the industry was also working on options to minimise the use of antibiotics, including a selective breeding program, vaccinations and improved feeds.

"Ideally, when those vaccines are fully efficacious, when the selective breeding program has really established itself, we will be managing this disease without the need for therapeutants."

A total of 5.4 tonnes of florfenicol was used last summer, during which about 9,000 tonnes of salmon still died.

Tasmania's health department has said there were no reports of adverse human health effects from eating seafood with florfenicol residues.

However, as a precaution, it has said people can avoid seafood caught within 3km of a treated salmon pen.

Pharmaceutical company Abbey Labs has applied to the regulator for a separate "minor use" permit to increase the dose rate and treatment regime of florfenicol.

It also wants to expand the geographical use of florfenicol to salmon pens at Oakhampton Bay, on the state's east coast.

World.title: Five-year-old seriously hurt in e-bike strike outside school
World.content:
A five-year-old boy has been seriously injured after being hit by an e-bike outside a school in the Wollondilly region, south-west of Sydney.

Emergency services were called to Remembrance Driveway in Tahmoor at 3:30pm yesterday after reports of a crash.

NSW Ambulance paramedics arrived to find the young boy had been hit by an e-bike and suffered serious injuries to his head and legs.

He was taken to The Children's Hospital at Westmead in a serious condition.

The popularity of e-bikes has exploded in recent years. (ABC News: Ashlin Blieshke)

The incident happened outside Tahmoor Public School.

A NSW Department of Education spokesperson said in a statement that the school community's thoughts were with the young boy and his family.

"We would also like to acknowledge the staff who supported [the boy] in the immediate aftermath and thank the emergency services who attended," they said.

NSW Police said the 16-year-old boy riding the e-bike was not injured and is assisting officers with their inquiries.

A formal investigation has begun.

Police have appealed for information from the public, asking anyone with dash cam, mobile phone or CCTV footage to contact Narellan Police or Crime Stoppers.

MPs concerned

Independent Wollondilly MP Judy Hannan said she drove past the incident on Tuesday afternoon.

"I'm really hoping that the child who was injured gets better really quickly," she said.

"I feel for him, the school and his parents. I hope they're all looked after."

Judy Hannan says the crossbench will propose new rules to improve e-bike safety. (ABC Illawarra: Brooke Chandler)

Ms Hannan said the crossbench would push for new rules and regulations to better address the risks associated with e-bikes in parliament in the coming weeks.

"It's something we need to address, and we know there will be further accidents unless the government takes a stance," she said.

The NSW government has introduced new standards for e-bikes this year and is undertaking compliance blitzes through NSW Police and Transport for NSW.

Ryan Park says his thoughts are with the family of the child. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

NSW Health Minister Ryan Park said he was concerned to hear of the accident.

"My heart and thoughts are with that family. It must be a very, very frightening time for them," he said.

"We need to make sure people are using these devices safely and effectively.

"We don't want to see young children hurt, or other people impacted by these bikes."

Several children have been injured in e-bike strikes in recent months. Another five-year-old boy was hit in Engadine in September, and a 16-year-old girl was hit at Barrack Heights in Shellharbour in October.

In the year to September 29, the Sydney Children's Hospital Network recorded 183 children presenting with injuries associated with e-bikes and e-scooters, four times the number of presentations in 2023.

But the number of children under the age of eight injured was much lower than older age groups, with only 21 injuries recorded in this year's reporting period, up from eight in 2023.

World.title: Collins Dictionary names 'mogging' its word of the year
World.content:
The UK Collins Dictionary has declared "mogging", which means to upstage someone, its word of the year.

The dictionary is one of many that names a word of the year, with US-based dictionary.com selecting "maxxing" for 2026.

Both words became popular globally thanks to their prolific use on social media.

What is 'mogging'?

"Mogging" means outperforming or upstaging something or someone.

Think, for example, of a steer being much, much bigger than a bunch of other steers and then going viral for its size.

The word comes from the verb "mog", which is thought to have come from the acronym AMOG, which stands for "alpha male of the group".

"It started life around 2016 as a noun in bodybuilding culture, referring to the most physically dominant man in the gym, before morphing into a verb and doing the rounds in the manosphere," Rachel Quin explained in a blog post for Collins Dictionary.

There have been many concerns raised about the impact conversations about mogging has on young people, particularly young men.

Simon Copland, a sociology researcher at the Australian National University, said some influencers used "dodgy science" to give a formula for mogging someone's looks.

"They try to measure these in a quantitative way, and then that defines whether you're good-looking enough, or good-looking at all," Dr Copland said.

"So, naturally, when you use such quantitative measures, it becomes a hierarchy thing."

Loading...

However, Ms Quin said the word has transcended those online spaces into wider use and now was "everywhere".

"Teenagers mog elite athletes, a new video game mogs an old favourite, and your friend's sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving," she said.

"Basically, if someone or something has made you look a bit rubbish by comparison, you've been mogged."

An example of the use of "mog" on social media. (X: @a24victoire)

But there are a few other definitions for the word mog.

Collins Dictionary includes mog as a variation of moggy, which is another word for cat.

Mog can also mean to depart or walk with slow steps.

Another example of how you might use the word mog. (X:@uncledoomer)

What does 'word of the year' mean?

It's something some companies that produce major dictionaries do to reflect the vocabulary trends of the past 12 months (and also drum up publicity for their brand).

While it's not clear exactly how Collins Dictionary decided on mogging as its word of the year, the company did say use of the word had increased by 210 per cent in the past 12 months.

The company said its experts monitored a database of about 27 billion words, which draws from sources including social media, to create its annual list of words that reflect the evolution of the English language.

Other words experts shortlisted this year include:

Bixie: A hairstyle shorter than a bob but longer than a pixie cut.

A hairstyle shorter than a bob but longer than a pixie cut. Carspreading: The tendency of manufacturers to build cars longer, wider and heavier.

The tendency of manufacturers to build cars longer, wider and heavier. Firewave: A series of urban wildfires in a short space of time.

A series of urban wildfires in a short space of time. Fricy: A food that is both fruity and spicy.

A food that is both fruity and spicy. Friendslop: A type of low-budget, independently produced video game, played among friends.

A type of low-budget, independently produced video game, played among friends. Ghost job: A job that is advertised without any intention to appoint anyone.

A job that is advertised without any intention to appoint anyone. Hydration break: A pause in a sporting contest to allow the contestants to drink fluids.

A pause in a sporting contest to allow the contestants to drink fluids. Manchesterism: A political philosophy involving devolution of power to regions and emphasising economic and social progress.

A political philosophy involving devolution of power to regions and emphasising economic and social progress. P(doom): An estimation of the probability that AI will bring about the collapse of human civilisation.

Dictionary.com has already announced "maxxing" as its pick for 2026.

"'Maxxing' is a word that refers to the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimising a certain aspect of your life," the company said.

"It can be used on its own, as in 'everyone is maxxing something … what's yours?'

"But it's especially common when it combines with other words to make new creations like looksmaxxing (optimising one's physical appearance)."

Loading...

Australia's Macquarie Dictionary generally tends to name its word of the year closer to the end of November.

Last year the Australian publication picked "AI slop", while its 2024 word of the year was "enshittification".

World.title: Melbourne Salvos cafe closes as demand exceeds capacity
World.content:
A social service cafe in Melbourne's inner west has closed its doors five months after it opened, as its operator scrambles to find a new location.

The Salvation Army's Lighthouse Cafe opened in May to provide vulnerable Footscray community members with free meals and connection to homelessness, mental health, and drug and alcohol support.

The Salvation Army said the service was relocating due to high demand, which rendered the current space unsuitable.

"We've been overwhelmed by the need," The Salvation Army Melbourne Commanding Officer Major Brendan Nottle told 774 ABC Melbourne Breakfast.

"We're seeing 170 people on average a day come through that cafe, and initially we were expecting 50 to 60.

"Even in the first couple of weeks we were thinking, 'We've got a problem here', because it's one single room and it wasn't big enough to accommodate the number of people coming through."

The Salvation Army says the venue could only cater for less than half of the 170 people attending each day. (ABC News: Tim Callanan)

A man who used the service, who wanted to be known as PJ, said he and others were "pissed off and angry" the doors had shut.

"It's just wrong, man," he said.

"Everyone here is malnourished."

He said everyone loved the cafe.

" The meals were beautiful, the staff were beautiful. "

He said he was upset by the lack of follow-through for the service.

"We were promised a long-term cafe," he said.

"They don't follow-through … they just disappear."

Search for new home for Lighthouse in Footscray

The project had so far received $350,000 from the state government, with another $576,000 earmarked.

Major Nottle said while a new location had not been found, The Salvation Army was committed to keeping the service in Footscray, where the organisation has had a presence since 1887.

"We're relocating to another site that will be more suitable to the work we want to do, not just in terms of being able to accommodate more people in the cafe, but also having additional spaces where we can co-locate with other services," Major Nottle said.

Major Brendan Nottle with local MP Katie Hall at Lighthouse Cafe earlier this year. (Supplied: Project 614)

He acknowledged there had been concerns from surrounding businesses around safety.

"Have there been a couple of complaints from neighbours? Yes, there have," he said.

" But for every complaint there's been three or four really positive comments from people who are overwhelmed emotionally because of the support they were receiving. "

The temporary closure comes as The Salvation Army works to wind down Foley House, a long-term residential facility that has provided beds for homeless men since 2013.

The Salvation Army has said the accommodation would close once the final resident "has been matched with safe, suitable and affordable accommodation".

"Foley House has, due to the complexity of the residents, become a disability-like accommodation without access to any form of accommodation funding other than The Salvation Army itself," the organisation said at the time.

Footscray Community Response's Shifrah Blustein said the closure of the cafe would make people's lives harder.

A Footscray resident says he is angry that the cafe has closed. (ABC News: Tim Callanan)

"Having somewhere you can go for a meal, to not be cold or feel the heat from outside is something, but, at the end of the day, these people need to be supported into housing.

"Providing a few outreach workers or a cafe, it isn't a replacement for housing.

"The community just wants some very, very basic services to be delivered to people doing it so tough on the streets who are being blamed and dehumanised for every social problem under the sun in Footscray.

"This was one tiny measure to address that, in a very sort of superficial way, I guess, to have a place where people could be off the street, be fed, and they can't even sustain that."

The Salvation Army said an interim "mobile and on foot" service would start later this month to provide food relief and connection with support services.

World.title: Jailed former MP pleads guilty to misusing parliamentary allowance
World.content:
Former South Australian MP Troy Bell, who was previously jailed for serious fraud and theft offences, has now also admitted to pocketing more than $20,000 by misusing a parliamentary travel allowance.

Bell today appeared in the Adelaide Magistrates Court, via video link from custody, and pleaded guilty to 15 charges of deception.

He was previously charged with a further 37 counts of deception, but those charges were dropped by the prosecution.

Court documents viewed by the ABC state that Bell pocketed $21,177 by misusing the Country Members Accommodation Allowance between January 2015 and September 2019.

Bell had previously strongly denied misusing the allowance.

Troy Bell will return to the Adelaide Magistrates Court for a pre-sentence hearing next month. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

Last year, the 53-year-old was jailed for at least two-and-a-half years after a District Court jury found him guilty of stealing more than $430,000 in public money while he was employed at the Department for Education between 2009 and 2013.

The money was meant for not-for-profit educational organisations.

The former Liberal-turned-independent member of Mount Gambier stepped down from parliament in August last year after losing an appeal over the jury’s guilty verdict.

He was sentenced two months later to five years in prison, with a non-parole period of two-and-a-half years.

Bell returns to court for a pre-sentence hearing next month.

World.title: Indonesia detains police generals suspected of wire-tapping president's phones
World.content:
Indonesian police say they have detained three senior police generals, including the former chief of police, as they investigate the alleged illegal wire-tapping of President Prabowo Subianto and dozens of other prominent figures.

In a brief press conference on Tuesday night, police outlined allegations that the senior police generals wire-tapped Mr Prabowo's phone number, entering it and others into an interception system without following proper procedures.

Asep Safrudin, head of the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency, said the suspects were being investigated for illegally intercepting communications, accessing electronic systems without authorisation and deleting electronic data.

"The suspects are alleged to have carried out non-procedural or illegal tapping against the telephone numbers of the president of the Republic of Indonesia, state officials, political figures, media figures, community leaders, NGO activists and businesspeople," Asep Safrudin said.

Police identified the suspects as presidential chief of staff General Listyo Sigit Prabowo, National Police legal division head Inspector General Ahrie Sonta Nasution and Inspector General Eko Hadi Santoso, a senior instructor at the National Police Education and Training Institute.

All three were detained at the National Police headquarters detention centre, Asep Safrudin said.

The allegations will send shock waves through the Indonesian political establishment, as police investigate the alleged wire-tapping.

Police have not revealed if there was a recipient of the allegedly wire-tapped conversations and have not disclosed the motive, telling reporters their inquiries remained ongoing.

Yusril Ihza Mahendra says the alleged wire-tapping is a serious concern for the country. (Reuters)

Mr Prabowo and the three suspects have not responded publicly to the allegations.

A spokesperson for the presidential chief of staff's office could not be reached for comment.

Mr Safrudin said police had questioned 10 witnesses and three expert witnesses, and investigators had seized 11 mobile phones, an iPad and four flash drives as evidence in the case.

Police alleged the unauthorised wire-tapping took place between 2025 and 2026, with the suspects ordering wire taps without following procedures established under a 2010 National Police regulation.

Several telephone numbers were entered into the Lawful Interception Management System, or LIMS, without verification, Mr Safrudin said.

He said the suspects also recently ordered the deletion of files containing intercepted communications from the LIMS computer system, allegedly to conceal evidence and erase traces of the wire-tapping operation.

No indication of treason

Coordinating Minister for Law, Human Rights, Immigration and Corrections Yusril Ihza Mahendra said investigators had found no indication of treason in the case involving three active high-ranking police officers.

Listyo Sigit Prabowo served as chief of Indonesia's police from 2021 to October this year, when he was made chief of presidential staff.

He previously served as the police chief in the Indonesian city of Surakarta, where former president Joko Widodo worked as mayor.

Listyo Sigit Prabowo was appointed as chief of police by Joko Widodo.

Prabowo Subianto has not yet responded to the allegations. (Sputnik: Alexander Kazakov via Reuters)

Mr Mahendra said the suspects would be charged under Article 258 of Indonesia's new criminal code, which prohibits the unlawful interception, recording, diversion, alteration, obstruction or monitoring of non public electronic communications.

The charge carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years.

They also face charges under Article 332 of the criminal code, which carries a maximum penalty of six years in prison, as well as Article 32 of Indonesia's Electronic Information and Transactions Law, which criminalises the unauthorised alteration, destruction, deletion, transfer or concealment of electronic information and carries a sentence of up to eight years in prison.

Several civil society organisations said they condemned the alleged illegal wire-tapping, with concerns over the use of surveillance technology by state authorities.

"If proven, the use of wire-tapping equipment without a lawful basis or legitimate purpose would constitute a human rights violation and an abuse of authority, warranting both criminal and institutional accountability," the Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation said.

In 2009, Australian intelligence tried to listen in to the mobile phone of then-Indonesian president Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, according to documents leaked by National Security Agency whistleblower Edward Snowden.

The incident was made public in 2013 and sparked a diplomatic uproar.

Indonesia's former vice-president, Jusuf Kalla, who was also allegedly targeted by Australian surveillance, demanded an apology from former Australian prime minister Tony Abbott.

World.title: Old faces, new ideas: Cheika’s plan to revive the Waratahs
World.content:
SportRugby UnionWaratahs Old faces, new ideas: Cheika’s plan to revive the Waratahs Jonathan Drennan November 4, 2026 — 2:11pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Incoming Waratahs coach Michael Cheika is promising a bold new approach in his second stint in charge of NSW, adamant he will not be using the platform to audition for another crack at the Wallabies job. Flanked by assistant coaches Wycliff Palu and Stephen Hoiles at Allianz Stadium on Wednesday, Cheika also revealed a direct pitch from Rugby Australia boss Phil Waugh convinced him to take on the job he walked away from in 2015. Michael Cheika is back with the NSW Waratahs as head coach. James Brickwood Cheika – who guided NSW to the Super Rugby title in 2014 – joins the Waratahs on a one-year deal, fresh from winning the NRL premiership as an assistant coach with the Sydney Roosters. He also oversaw Lebanon’s Rugby League World Cup campaign which ended with a dramatic win over France on Sunday. “It’s more than 10 years later [since the Waratahs’ Super Rugby title] ... so I want to show them something new, right? I want to show them another way to do things that I think – I’m not guessing, I suppose, but I’m imagining that they haven’t experienced before,” Cheika said.



“There’ll be some things I’m going to do this year that I haven’t even done before. “So, yeah, I want to do things differently because I want to get a different outcome. So I think that this is a very new adventure. I’m not going back to the 2014 or 2015 playbook and trying to reinvent that at all ... as far as footy’s concerned, I want to create a new picture, a completely new picture.” Michael Cheika, with Michael Hooper, after the Waratahs won the 2014 Super Rugby Grand Final. Getty Images Since leaving the Waratahs job in 2015, Cheika coached the Wallabies and had stints in Argentina, Japan and English rugby. He is adamant he has no designs on using his time at NSW to get back into coaching Australia.



“There are no springboards [to a Wallabies coaching job], I’m coming here to get this team to try and win the comp. Isn’t that what we want to do at the end of the day? That’s it,” Cheika said. “I’ve always been like this, it’s what you do now and where you are now, how you perform, even when I was a player overseas, I’d have a one-year contract. If I play good, well, then I’m in charge. If I play rubbish, you can get rid of me. That’s fair. Michael Cheika’s 2016 Wallabies side was the last to emerge from a European tour with more wins than losses. Getty “And I’ve got to be judging my own performance here now, not on what’s happened in the past, not on what could happen in the future ... I just think I really want it to be clear that this is where I am, where my feet are, and that’s it.” Before deciding to return to the Waratahs, Cheika was not short of admirers in both rugby codes. The former Randwick player had taken Argentina to the semi-finals of the last World Cup and then steered a struggling Leicester team to a premiership final in his one season there.



Cheika revealed Waugh’s pitch on the Waratahs ultimately proved successful and said he was eager to steer them back to the finals for the first time since 2023. “I had to decide in my own head that I could do what was necessary to make the team go well. It’s not about me, it’s about the team,” Cheika said. Michael Cheika faces the media for the first time as Waratahs coach. James Brickwood. “So teams need a certain type of coach at a certain time, and that fluctuates. You may not be the right guy for that team at that time, and I had to feel like I would be the right guy for this team at this time. “And then I answered in my own head, ‘OK, this is what I think would need to get done. Can I do that? Can I, in the timeframes that I’ve got and all of that type of thing?’ And I answered to myself, ‘yes,’ obviously ...



“So I didn’t really need to be persuaded. I had to answer my own questions about, can I get the team to where we want it to be?” Another familiar face for Cheika from the Roosters is NRL star Angus Crichton, who is recovering from a foot injury and has been travelling in Europe. It is expected that Crichton will primarily play for the Waratahs at inside centre, allowing Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to gain more experience as a winger. Angus Crichton is expected to slot into inside centre afte recovering from a foot injury. Sitthixay Ditthavong Cheika has enjoyed success with former NRL players including Israel Folau and is confident Crichton can make an impact with the Waratahs, but is putting no pressure on him. “I’m not a real big expectations man, you know, I think that because they usually only lead to regrets,” Cheika said.



Related Article Australian rugby ‘I just kept believing’: Why Kurtley Beale never gave up on a return to the Wallabies “For Angus, he’ll have his own personal ideas and goals of what he wants to achieve, and then he’ll be part of the team’s goals as well. I didn’t talk to him at all about it while we were at Roosters together ... “Angus has been playing league for a long time now, but he played rugby for a while, and I’ve got no doubts in what he’ll bring and how he’ll fit into the team, and what he’ll bring to the team off the field as well.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Friday.

World.title: It took 166 years for a trainer to nail the Cup trifecta. And Ciaron Maher’s not stopping there
World.content:
SportRacingMelbourne Cup It took 166 years for a trainer to nail the Cup trifecta. And Ciaron Maher’s not stopping there Peter Ryan November 4, 2026 — 2:06pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Ciaron Maher is daring to dream with Point Of Law, saying the Melbourne Cup winner could represent his stable overseas against the world’s best once he matures after his stunning victory on Tuesday. After a night of celebrations, Maher was not ruling anything in or out for the northern hemisphere three-year-old who exploded at the end of the two miles with a sensational turn of foot to run the quickest final 200 metres of Tuesday’s meeting. Melbourne Cup winning trainer Ciaron Maher poses with Point of Law at Werribee the morning after their win. The Age Maher, who became the first trainer to prepare a Melbourne Cup trifecta when Zahraan and Juja Kibo filled the placings, said the horse’s connections would map out a sensible plan for Point Of Law but, right now, anything was on the cards. “I always thought, if I had horse good enough, the Gold Cup [Britain’s premier staying race, run at Royal Ascot in June} would be a nice race to have a horse run in. But whether he’s up for that this year or next year or whether at all, he certainly has a few of the necessary ingredients,” Maher said.



Point of Law pokes at the Melbourne Cup which is valued at $1million. The Age He raised the prospect of Point Of Law backing up for next year’s Melbourne Cup, racing in a big Japanese race – given his bloodlines include legendary Japanese stayer Deep Impact – or taking him to Dubai as options connections would discuss over drinks when the time was right. “But we are mindful that he is still raw and has a bit of furnishing left,” Maher said. Despite having achieved almost everything there is to achieve in Australian racing, including winning the 2022 Melbourne Cup with Gold Trip, Maher shows about as much signs of slowing down as any of his stayers. He said his passion remained alive because he loved the sport and the animals.



“I love it. I am a very competitive person naturally, and I love the passion and the culture of the team, and building a team of horses. Getting them to compete on a day like that is a very rewarding feeling,” Maher said. “And [I love] that euphoria of winning.” His stable, which had a record seven runners in the Cup, along with Sydney’s Chris Waller, has led the way with their investment in sport science, horse welfare and data-driven decision-making. Loading Maher said his horses were strategically prepared and placed, taking into account all the information available. “That is the way of any business in this day and age. Everyone uses data and systems [to find] better efficiencies,” Maher said.



“I always look at the way humans are trained, like footy players, compared to the way they are trained 10 years ago. The change is huge compared to the way they used to train, and I think horse racing is no different. The only difference is obviously [a horse] can’t talk. “I am always interested in the why and the how and the science of it all both in the business and also in the horse whether it is nutrition, aerobic or anaerobic.” Point Of Law feasts from the Melbourne Cup the day after delivering the trophy for trainer Ciaron Maher. Eddie Jim That work continues for the remaining two days of the carnival, with Maher teaming up with Ethan Brown in the VRC Oaks on the tough stayer Ice Lady and then running The Everest winner Tempted up the straight in the VRC Champions Sprint. He’ll also saddle up Another Wil in the mile and front-running Cox Plate starters Land Legend and Light Infantry Man in the Champion Stakes. Maher said Ice Lady was “a super chance” in the Oaks after a less-than-ideal run in the Wakeful Stakes when she finished third.



“We went a bit solid so backing up when you go a strong tempo is not ideal, but the horse has had a great prep and I think she’ll run the trip,” Maher said. Related Article Melbourne Cup He used to ride bulls. Now he takes calls from the King and has seven Cup runners He described Tempted as exceptional, now that she has matured into a fully furnished mare. But Wednesday was about Point Of Law as he picked at grass loaded into th Melbourne Cup for the cameras. “He seems pretty good. He knows he has had a run,” Maher said.

World.title: Orbit caps off NSW polymetallic drilling with thick sulphide hit
World.content:
Sponsored BusinessCompaniesBulls N' Bears Orbit caps off NSW polymetallic drilling with thick sulphide hit Brought to you by BULLS N’ BEARS Andrew Todd November 4, 2026 — 2:03pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Orbit Resources has capped off the latest drilling campaign at its Lewis Ponds gold-silver-zinc project in New South Wales with a bang, intersecting a thick 28.1-metre zone of visual sulphide mineralisation in the program’s final hole. The company says the hole drilled into its Spicer’s Lode hit the zone from 199.5m downhole, with sections containing visual estimates of up to 34 per cent semi-massive sulphides. An old shaft entrance at Orbit Resources’ Lewis Ponds precious and base metals project, in the prolific Lachlan Fold Belt of New South Wales. The intersection marks the successful completion of a four-hole resource development program, with assays for all holes, including a 3.55-metre hit at a whopping 50 per cent estimated massive sulphides, due shortly. Those sulphide minerals can host substantial concentrations of zinc, lead and copper - with some carrying up to 86 per cent of their respective base metal by weight - alongside the potential for valuable gold and silver credits.



‘Assays are needed to confirm grades and widths, but the program has delivered what it was designed to do.’ Orbit Resources managing director Jeneta Owens The drilling program was designed to lift confidence in Lewis Ponds’ existing mineral resource by upgrading sections to the higher indicated category, while also supplying fresh core for metallurgical testwork. That resource already hosts a formidable polymetallic base, sitting at 17.52 million tonnes grading 1.12 grams per tonne (g/t) gold, 53.34g/t silver, 2.06 per cent zinc and 1.1 per cent lead with copper credits. In contained terms, that works out at roughly 630,000 ounces of gold and 30.1 million ounces of silver. The company says its visual logging of the final hole identified a polymetallic sulphide assemblage of pyrite, sphalerite, galena, chalcopyrite and pyrrhotite, noting that three of the four holes drilled at its Tom’s and Spicer’s Lodes intersected visual sulphides. Orbit Resources managing director Jeneta Owens said: “Assays are needed to confirm grades and widths, but the program has delivered what it was designed to do, which was to test the continuity of the lodes within the existing resource and provide fresh core for our next round of metallurgical testwork.”



While drilling is aimed at growing the resource, a scoping study released in February has already put some impressive numbers around Lewis Ponds, outlining a base-case pre-tax net present value of $481 million and an internal rate of return of 24 per cent. However, an upside case using spot commodity prices at the time sent the potential project economics into the stratosphere, delivering a pre-tax net present value of a whopping $1.088 billion and an internal rate of return of 40 per cent. Although Lewis Ponds remains the main game, Orbit’s Narraburra ionic-clay project offers another potentially valuable card up its sleeve, despite currently being on the backburner. The renewed scramble for secure rare earth supply chains and the sharp repricing of Chinese-controlled elements have given the project’s yttrium-rich endowment a serious lift, putting its proven metallurgy back in the spotlight. With low-cost, hybrid ionic-clay characteristics and a much larger prospective footprint beyond the current resource, Narraburra has plenty of room to grow. Management believes further drilling could quickly build on the existing resource, paving the way for a scoping study to test the project’s development potential and put some hard numbers around an increasingly attractive rare earths proposition.



Stage two drilling is now complete at Lewis Ponds, leaving Orbit awaiting a fresh batch of assays before turning its attention back to the project’s latest exploration eye-catcher, the Cousin Jack base metals discovery, 350 metres southeast of the existing mineral resource. Discovery drilling in June delivered some encouraging hits, including 15m at 2.8 per cent zinc equivalent from 314m and 11m at 4.4 per cent from 584m, with a high-grade slice of 1.7m at 13.1 per cent zinc equivalent from 585.3m. The company says the pending results will feed into an updated geological model and help guide the next steps at Cousin Jack to the south, a find that could prove a company maker for Lewis Ponds. On paper at least, Lewis Ponds already has the makings of a feasible Lachlan Fold operation and with a potential billion-dollar price tag in its sights, the wait to get the rods spinning again will feel like a long one. World.title: On knife’s edge: David Jones could appoint administrators by Thursday
World.content:
BusinessCompaniesRetail On knife’s edge: David Jones could appoint administrators by Thursday Jessica Yun and Colin Kruger Updated November 4, 2026 — 1:27pm ,first published 12:23pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
